A budget per file for every file (only what every session reads is paid every time; a skill's body or a record is read when needed).
why: The author, 2026-11-17, asked for it, built on what exists: the canon's cold read, the playbook's findability test, idealkb's kb-navigation-measured and its summary layer, the backlog item session-start-size. Measured on linux-phone-oco (research housekeeping-the-start): 35-46 KB before acting, half of it the practices' reasons.

brief: lab-agent retires by parts (token, timers, jobs, board/notify, inbox, root-exec, daemon); oco-agent is not its successor; notify and root-exec become shell
decision:
lab-agent retires part by part, in this order, and oco-agent does not become its successor. Every part has an owner today that is not lab-agent, except two things nothing else gives: a phone push from an unattended unit (notify) and passwordless root for devlab (root-exec); those two move to a few lines of shell each, not to a program.
1 token: the token file moves to a neutral path (~/.config/ideal-agent/token, mode 600), the old path a symlink until land, agent-env, tad/idealkb-update-pins and oco-agent read the new one; cost ~1 h, lost nothing.
2 timers: oco-ask-to-observe (about 44 GitHub requests per 15 min), oco-say-what-is-new, oco-agent-shadow stop with ocoeco's legacy; cost minutes; lost: ocoeco's lenses of the lab (declared dead).
3 jobs: a long build that must outlive a session is `systemd-run --user --unit=NAME COMMAND` (journal is its log, a unit name is claimed once, `systemctl --user status/stop` is standing/stop); walleye-builder's six jobs today are the only use; lab-agent run, oco-agent run and the lab-agent-jobs polling every 5 s retire after one walleye build is proven this way; cost ~2 h; lost: submission from a sandbox that cannot reach the lab (no such driver since 2026-11-15), the replay measure of the 2026-11-11 stall (kept as a concept), and the two inhibit-idle units (the lab sleeps unless a session asks for keep-awake - the author decides).
4 board and notify: devlab watch pushes its alert with `curl` to the ntfy topic from a mode-600 file (notify, 3 lines) and files the standing alert as a backlog row; the board's 40 stale items go to their projects' backlogs or are closed; cost ~3 h; lost: the 5-minute board push on the phone.
5 inbox/guide: the plugin's session start stops running `lab-agent inbox`; practice 04 names the app's session messages; guide is `scripts/ideal-agent practices`. Needs the author's word first: does he still write to the lab from the ntfy app (older traffic NOT KNOWN; empty over the last 12 h)? cost ~1 h.
6 root-exec: devlab and the setup scripts call a root-owned wrapper in lab-machine (`lab-root`, exec argv) granted by one sudoers line - the same power as today, renamed - or, as the author may prefer, a narrower grant per command (fastboot, ufw, nix, pacman) which ends ad hoc root for sessions; the grant is the author's and root's to write, never mine; cost ~3 h plus the author's sudo.
7 self-update, then the daemon and its units, the sudoers line and the package go; cost minutes once 1-6 are done.
Check: `scripts/lab-agent-free` (shows 34 live uses now, must reach 0).
Resolving 2026-11-12-oco-agent ("oco-agent replaces lab-agent, tied to ocoeco by design"): it was decided when ocoeco was the system; 2026-11-17-nothing-of-ocoeco and the author's direction of the same day remove its premise, so it is superseded, not reinterpreted: oco-agent's ideas (the journal as the only truth, a job claimed once, leases, replay as a measure) stay as concepts in its own repository; its program is not extended, and its half-built switch steps 2, 3 and 5 are dropped. A row in that repository's own decisions says so when its owner lands part 3.
rejected: Keep lab-agent as is (a polling daemon, two inhibit units and 44 requests per 15 min for no job); finish oco-agent as the successor (its own premise, ocoeco, is retired; a second runner beside systemd); one big removal now (root-exec and the token are live: devlab flash and every land would break); rewrite lab-agent smaller in Rust (a new program for what systemd-run, curl and a sudoers line do); a Python or Claude-scheduled-task runner (no new Python; sessions end).
why: Measured 2026-11-17: no job through lab-agent since 2026-11-12 (1165 ever, 2 probes since); oco-agent's traffic was ocoeco speaking and walleye-builder's six builds today; live uses left are the token file, root-exec, board/notify for devlab watch, and the inbox call in the plugin's session start. Sessions on the lab, the plugin, ikb and land already do the rest. The author, 2026-11-17: tools of oco became too bloated, make better autonomous independent tools.

brief: Practice 22 is extended, not doubled: a proposal, the author's too, is met by a small look around, kept as a research row with dated material.
decision: Practice 22 is extended, not doubled: a proposal - the author's too - is met by looking at where things stand and how others do it and reconsidering it before acting; the finding is a research row with its sources and its material in a dated folder, and a subject's summary is renewed when due. The how is a skill, look-around-first: where things stand by the base's queries, how others do it (the researcher agent may take it), reconsider, keep the finding as a row plus a dated folder, renew the summary. ask-a-knowledge-base and record-the-work say the summary and the material. ideal-agent's pin moves to idealkb 0.3.0, so its own know-how follows the same layers.
rejected: A new practice beside 22: one nature under two names. A hook forcing a look before every edit: most edits need none, and a hook cannot tell a proposal from a typo. Folding the method into research-a-feature: that is a session's whole method for a hard feature; this is minutes before any change.
why: The author, 2026-11-17: before acting on a proposal, his own included, look around, research a little, reconsider, and record the condensed finding with its research kept out of the way. Proposal processes elsewhere build the look in (research look-around-habit-world); idealkb 0.2.0 gave the place (its decisions 2026-11-17-summary-layer and 2026-11-17-research-aside).

brief: ideal-agent depends on and teaches nothing of ocoeco; landit checks tad places with tad; what remains is passive or the author's words.
decision: ideal-agent depends on nothing of ocoeco and teaches nothing of it: its skills and its researcher look and record through the project's tad knowledge base and idealkb's queries and records only (about, next, find, row, recent, the named records); a place still kept with ocoeco is mentioned in one line as another project's legacy. landit checks a tad place with tad check and make verify, never ocoeco check, and makes no glimpse there (lab-agent #219). What remains is passive: the mark (oco.toml) and gather.yml, by which the author's observatory reads these tables; OCOECO_BY, the name oco-work signs commits with; and the practices' own text, in which 10 of 44 practices name ocoeco (14 counting its lenses and glimpses: 03, 05, 20, 22, 26, 29, 30, 31, 33, 37, 39, 40, 41, 42) - the author's words, reported to him, not rewritten here.
rejected: Rewriting the practices that name ocoeco here, on the agent's own reading (they are the author's practices: what replaces each is his to say). Removing gather.yml and the mark (the author's observatory reads them; his to remove). Reverting ocoeco #458 (harmless to ocoeco, and nothing here needs it any more).
why: The author, 2026-11-17, sharply: our systems must not depend on ocoeco. Measured on main: orchestrate-agents and lab-session-start taught ocoeco focus, record-the-work taught ocoeco note, the researcher ocoeco focus; landit ran ocoeco check in every place, so ocoeco's reasoning lens decided what ideal-agent's about may name (ocoeco #458 was landed only to pass it).

brief: ideal-agent's records live in its own tad database; the commit is the record of the work, no glimpses.
decision: ideal-agent keeps its records in its own tad database: data through tad (tad r NAME), landing through land; the commit and its pull request are the record of the work, signed by the name the session works under. No glimpses and no oco/ tables: the mark exports data/ directly.
rejected: ocoeco's oco/ tables beside a tad database (two tools writing rows in one place); glimpses (a second record of what the commit already says).
why: The author asked for its own tad database. linux-phone-oco found the same way simpler on 2026-11-17 (its docs decision 2026-11-17-one-database): one tool writes the rows, git records the work.

brief: grenudi/ideal-agent is the one home of general agent know-how, a tad database and one Claude Code plugin; each project keeps its domain.
decision: grenudi/ideal-agent is the one home of general agent know-how in the open commons: the practices (moved from the observatory), the shared skills (from creation-guidelines/lab-agent oco-agent/skills), the general hooks (from linux-phone-oco/lab-tools' devlab guard), the general role methods (from linux-phone-oco/docs prompts/) and the research and decisions on how agents are organised. It keeps them in its own tad database and ships them as one Claude Code plugin and marketplace, so one install gives any machine, project or cloud session the same agent. Each old place is retired with a pointer here once the new one behaves the same; what is one project's domain (a device's tool, a project's records, its how-it-stands rows) stays in that project's own data, so both improve in their own place.
rejected: A fifth place beside the four (one nature under five names: each would drift from the others - the move is done only when every old place points here). Keeping it under creation-guidelines (the author chose his own account, grenudi: the know-how is his way of working with agents, not one guideline among others). Skills and hooks kept only on the lab (symlinks into ~/.claude/skills and hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json reach no other machine, project or cloud session, and are versioned nowhere). Domain knowledge moved here too (it would rot away from the data it is about: linux-phone's records stay in its docs database).
why: The author, 2026-11-17: general agent know-how was scattered over four places - live practices in the observatory, skills symlinked from lab-agent only on the lab, general hook rules inside devlab's guard, role briefs written for linux-phone - and he asked for one repository under his own account, with its own tad database and the oco mark. Research (expert-agents-written-not-standing) found expertise is best written down and read by fresh sessions; Claude Code plugins are the standard way to package skills, hooks and agents for every machine.

brief: A resource only one may change has one keeper: a lasting role with disposable sessions, serving a queue others prepare; its tool holds the lock.
decision: The general pattern of a keeper of a shared resource is ideal-agent's: practice 44-one-keeper-per-shared-resource and the role skill keep-a-shared-resource. One owner per resource; a lasting role whose sessions are disposable (hand-over into the resource's how-it-stands record, then end); others prepare and queue items with their proofs, the keeper executes by the weakest link; the queue is a named query over the project's backlog, shown on its face; a scheduled run or the patrol starts the next keeper session when the queue has work and no keeper is live, and a lease keeps two keepers from running; the resource's own tool still holds the lock. A project keeps only its specifics - the resource, its tool, its queue's query, its lease, its schedule (linux-phone-oco: surya's phone keeper, in docs' ideal-agent-linux-phone-oco/, extending this).
rejected: A standing keeper session kept alive (its context rots and is re-read at full price; the knowledge vanishes at compaction - decision 2026-11-17-experts-written-not-standing). Every session changing the resource when it needs to, guarded only by the tool's lock (safe but not flowing: changes race for the device and nobody chooses by the weakest link). A queue kept as its own list or tracker (a second record beside the backlog; a named query reads it off the backlog). The keeper as the lock (the tool already holds it; a keeper that crashes must not strand the resource).
why: The author, 2026-11-17: the general part goes upstream to ideal-agent, the linux-phone part to its orchestration session, which references it. Precedents: LAVA, CI-tron (postmarketOS's hardware CI), Gas Town's Refinery, the actor model (research keeper-of-a-shared-resource).

brief: The practices are a table of ideal-agent's database; guide and the session start read them here; the observatory's copy is retired.
decision: The practices are a table of this database (data/practices.json), entered with tad r practice and exported in the mark, so the observatory gathers and shows them as ideal-agent's rows. lab-agent guide and ideal-agent start read them live from this repository's main; the observatory no longer keeps its own copy (its design/data/practices.json is retired with a pointer here).
rejected: Leaving them in the observatory and pointing to them (the one home would not hold the one thing every session reads). Copying them (two lists drift - the copy was taken from the observatory's main on the day of the move, and the observatory's file is retired, not kept).
why: The practices are the first thing an agent reads; kept in the observatory's design data they sat beside the observatory's own design, read by a URL hard-coded in lab-agent. In the one home of agent know-how they are kept, checked and rendered like every other row, and still seen in the observatory - which shows what places hold rather than holding it.

brief: The practices keep OCO's ideas in tad and ikb terms; those that existed only for ocoeco's tools retire, their reasons kept in the row
decision: Sixteen practices are reworded without ocoeco's tools, their idea and reason kept: 02 (the owning project's backlog), 03 (the role's practices and how-it-stands at the start), 04 (lab-agent inbox and session messages), 05 (the board read off tad q next and about), 06 (work on the lab, in a session there or a lab job - not only through oco-agent), 16, 20 (the weakest link read from the data; hand-work counted on the backlog), 26 (refining recorded in the owning data), 29 (a named query, not a lens), 30 (--about names where work was made), 31 (look the id up with tad q), 33 (a query is seen, not tested), 34 (the author's turns in the place that keeps his words), 37 (ikb practice-shown-in), 38 (ideal-agent's start and skills are the shared words), 39 (what followed read off tad q recent and the landed pull requests). 40 (the window) and 41 (a lens changed in place) retire: a new field retired keeps when and why in the row, the start and the practices query skip it. The role cards take up 03, 05, 29, 31, 34, 37, 38 and 39 where they fit.
rejected: Deleting 40 and 41 (their reasons - why the inside was wanted - would be lost: Chesterton's fence); rewriting the why of each (the why is what happened; a note that it was reworded is added instead); retiring 05, 29, 30, 31, 39 with their tools (their ideas - read off, not typed; never an id from memory - hold in tad); retiring 06 (the lab as the one place where state lives still holds; only oco-agent as the sole way goes); renumbering (a practice is called by its number everywhere).
why: The author, 2026-11-17 (relayed by the coordinator): everything related to oco tools (not oco as a concept) became too bloated and here we are developing ways to detach from that and make better autonomous, independent tools. Keep the OCO concept - an open commons, knowledge kept as data, everything recorded, looked at before acting; retire what exists only for ocoeco's lenses, window, glimpses, focus, fits, fulldome and oco-agent jobs.

brief: A session reads at its start only the practices' first sentences, its role's purpose and its task's summary; everything else only when a step needs it.
decision: lab-session-start says what to read at the start - the practices' first sentences, the first paragraph of the role's brief, the task's subject in summary (tad q about, or the queue's top) - and then 'read only when' for everything else: a record whole when its brief is not enough, another subject when the task reaches it, a skill's body when its step comes, a tool's help only when no command is named, the board and recent only when choosing. research-a-feature, bring-up-a-part and keep-a-shared-resource begin from the summary. keep-the-start-light measures what a started session read from its transcript (scripts/read-weight), not only the front files. Proposed to the author, not done: start roles that need no mail, web search or documents without those connectors.
rejected: Cutting the briefs further first (they are 1-2k tokens of an 80k start). Turning the connectors off from here (a user setting that also becomes the default for new sessions: the author's). Measuring only the front files (the help and whole records a session reads for want of a named command are the part that grows).
why: The author, 2026-11-17, after the first surya keeper: an agent reads only summaries and goes into detail only when its current task needs it. Measured (what-a-started-agent-reads): 73-81k tokens before anything is read, nearly all harness and connectors' tools; the keepers' own reading before acting was 10-12k tokens, the largest part tool help and a subject read whole.

brief: The author's bounds name acting on the world in his name, not reading it: a checked official download is the lane's; a mirror, a host binary, terms or money are not
decision: keep-a-shared-resource's bounds now say 'acting on the world in his name' - sending a message or mail, posting, publishing, a call, a pull request or patch to someone else's project, an account, terms accepted, anything bought or paid - instead of 'anything outward'; and a fourth point says what is the lane's asking no one: everything technical not on that list. A public file from a project's own release site, its checksum or signature checked against what the site publishes, kept in the work's own folder with its source and checksum recorded, used without being run on the lab host (a device may boot it from memory), needs no one's word. A file without a published checksum or signature, from a mirror, or a program to run on the host is the lane coordinator's decision, research first if needed. The coordinator card says the same.
rejected: A list of allowed sites (it ages, and a project's own release site is already the test); every download through the lane coordinator (a checked official file needs no judgment); dropping the checksum check (a file from a hijacked link would be booted); counting licence acceptance as technical (it binds the author: his).
why: The author, 2026-11-17: no need to ask his permission for downloads; roles should prevent this for the future; work should depend on him in such decisions as little as possible - it is a technical question, and roles' expertise handles it. Measured: two download asks in two minutes, from 'anything outward' in decision 2026-11-17-decisions-go-to-the-lane. Others gate the use of bytes, not reading them (auto mode, Copilot firewall, SLSA).

brief: Coordinators research on their own when a method is missing, bounded; what is general goes to ideal-agent as an upstream item its owner decides; every card carries practice 22
decision: look-around-first gains 'When a method is missing': a coordinator (top, lane, orchestration) starts research itself on a sign - work no record or skill covers, a question asked twice, a struggle cluster - bounded: the commons first, then one researcher-subagent round, a research-lead launcher only for a long question; one research per sign, recorded, two lines up. A finding about how agents work or how any device is brought up flows back to its owner: an upstream item naming grenudi/ideal-agent in the domain's base and a message to ideal-agent's owner, who looks around, decides, lands and reads back; no domain changes a general practice, skill or card. Every card carries practice 22; the coordinator, lane-coordinator and orchestrator cards point to the section; lab-session-start says the brief and the author's words are a starting point. The linux-phone briefs and ideal-agent as docs' upstream go through orchestration.
rejected: Research only on a keeper's ask (the missing method was nobody's question); a domain session editing ideal-agent directly (two writers collided on 2026-11-17; the owner keeps one home and one judgment); unbounded initiative (a research per thought; one per sign, the commons first); a new role for it (the coordinators see the signs; a role adds a card to every listing).
why: The author, 2026-11-17: a coordinator should decide to start research on its own and adjust ideal-agent from the results - not take his word for it, but research, look around and decide. The walleye lane lacked the general bring-up method nobody had asked for. Others: the lead decides on more research (Anthropic); findings become owned items in the owner's system (SRE postmortems); the rules themselves are revised (double loop).

brief: One shape, no new role: role health - at start (given, not used) and at work (struggled with) - is read-weight per role, run by the patrol, sent to the top coordinator as a short list
decision: agents-healthkeeper and role-work-simplification are one method - reading a role's transcripts - and become one duty of the patrol, not one or two roles. read-weight prints both sections; the patrol runs it on each role's sessions since its last round and, where a cluster needs reading, gives those transcripts to a read-only researcher subagent; it sends the top coordinator a short list, each item with its evidence, its owner and a proposed fix; the author and the owners decide. What ideal-agent owns from today's list is fixed now: the guard names jq, awk, sed or tad for what Python was reached for; change-a-device says how to wait without sleep; the lane-coordinator card starts sessions on its own turn.
rejected: Two roles, healthkeeper and work-simplification (one method under two names, two cards in every listing); one standing role-health session (holds ~80k tokens to run a script; no analogue keeps one); /insights per role (per user and machine, no split by role); PostToolUseFailure hooks as the measure (they miss schema and permission failures, which the transcript holds); the patrol fixing what it finds (fixes are the owners').
why: The author, 2026-11-17: a role that finds where agents waste time and tokens, weighed with agents-healthkeeper, one shape if they share a method. Measured: 301 of 5,375 calls failed and 56 writes by hand went past named records on one day; ikb-cli's one-off reading of 31 transcripts led to ikb. Others: detection is a script, clustering recurs now and then, owners fix (Anthropic, Microsoft, Langfuse, SRE, paper cuts); no source keeps a standing role.

brief: A role is a card in ideal-agent's agents/; a brief names it (Role: NAME); the first prompt brings the card and only its practices
decision: Seven generic roles - coordinator, lane-coordinator, orchestrator, keeper, research-lead, builder, patrol - each a Claude Code agent card in ideal-agent's agents/: frontmatter model, effort, skills; a body of purpose, owns, never, loads, hands over, reports to; a Practices line. A project's brief names its role under its title (Role: keeper (ideal-agent), Also practices: 42 for a domain's own) and keeps only the domain; the prompt that starts a session begins with that line. A UserPromptSubmit hook (ideal-agent role) gives the card and only those practices at the first prompt, every practice when none is named, and remembers it for a resume or compaction; the SessionStart no longer prints the practices. claude --agent ideal-agent:ROLE starts a session as the role too. What replaces what: the card replaces a brief's generic part and the whole practice list; the role skills stay the methods the cards load; briefs stay the domain.
rejected: A role table in tad with ideal-agent start --role (a parallel layer beside the agent cards Claude Code already loads, and the start cannot see the prompt); role-filtered practices by their for field (it says agents or people, not roles); new role skills such as coordinate-a-lane (would add to the skill descriptions every session reads, and repeat keep-a-shared-resource); agent teams (experimental, skills not applied, the lead not handed over); generated .claude/agents per project for connectors and hooks (a second copy to keep in sync; connectors stay off by default already); renaming the researcher subagent (in use; the session role is research-lead, Anthropic's word for the one holding a research).
why: The author's task of 2026-11-17: a session gets a role and loads only what it needs. Claude Code's native card is the shape others already read (Gas Town primes a role at start; RACI and Team Topologies give owns and reports to); start_session cannot pass --agent, so the role is read from the prompt. Measured: start-weight on docs' main falls 1.4-3.6 KB per role with the Role line alone; the session start from 8.6 KB to 0.5 KB plus a 3.5-5.7 KB role.

brief: The shared procedures and the methods of the roles are skills in the plugin; a project's brief keeps only its domain and names the skill.
decision: The procedures every agent follows are kept once, as Claude Code skills in this plugin (skills/): lab-session-start, land-a-change, record-the-work, change-a-device - and the general methods of the roles that were briefs for one project: orchestrate-agents, research-a-feature, bring-up-a-part. A project's brief (linux-phone-oco/docs prompts/) keeps only its domain part - what it owns, its device's tool, its places - and names the skill for the method. The skills replace creation-guidelines/lab-agent's oco-agent/skills, which were linked into the lab's ~/.claude/skills; that folder now points here. (lab-agent's decision 2026-11-17-skills-shared-by-every-agent, carried here: procedures shared as agent skills, discoverable rather than remembered.)
rejected: Each brief repeating the procedures (copies drift, and a brief is read once at the start). Symlinks from a clone on the lab (one machine only). Role methods as subagents in agents/ (a role is a session of its own that lives for hours and owns places; a subagent works inside one session and returns - kept for the read-only researcher). Role briefs as template files to copy (a copy drifts; a skill is read where it is kept).
why: Read in ArtCraft's organisation (craft-skills, landscape photocraft-fleet). On 2026-11-17 four sessions worked on the lab at once and the same traps cost time more than once (a clone reset by fresh took unlanded files; rendered pages lagged a row entered after rendering; land merged a release PR from a shell without oco-work). Linked into one machine's ~/.claude/skills they reached no other machine and no cloud session; a plugin installs the same set anywhere, versioned with the know-how it carries.

brief: No agents-healthkeeper role: read-weight measures what each role was given and never used, the patrol runs it per role, each owner trims - cards, briefs, the author's settings
decision: Start health folds into housekeeping. read-weight prints 'given, not used' (skills, agents, deferred tools and connectors listed and never used; the first prompt's role and practices). The patrol runs start-weight and read-weight on each role's latest session and files, naming the role, what is over budget or never used. Trimming stays with the owner: ideal-agent's owner for the role cards and what the plugin lists (its 11 skill descriptions cut from 4,080 to 2,287 B now); a project's owner for its briefs; the author for his settings (the skills and connectors every session lists - proposed, not changed). keep-the-start-light and the patrol card say so by reference.
rejected: A standing agents-healthkeeper role (it would add a card to every session's listing and a start of its own to do what a script and the patrol already do; it would trim what others own); a subagent the patrol spawns (the same read-weight run, with a start of ~80k tokens); per-role skill hiding through the role card (Claude Code has none for app-started sessions; the skills field only preloads); changing the author's skill settings here (his, like connectors: proposed); moving the role cards out of agents/ to save their 1.1 KB listing (kept for claude --agent until a measure shows no use).
why: The author, 2026-11-17: an agents-healthkeeper that looks at each role's bring-up and perfects the cards; research first, design only if research says so. Measured: ~18 KB of skills listed and unused by every role. Others: no analogue keeps a standing role - Gas Town's patrols watch liveness, SRE measures by rule and owners fix, friction logs are the newcomer's. Context engineering: smallest high-signal set.

brief: The guard refuses tad sql that writes and names ikb set and ikb remove; record-the-work says so; a one-time migration says TAD_SQL_WRITE_OK=1
decision: ideal-agent's PreToolUse guard refuses a Bash command whose tad sql holds an INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, ALTER, DROP, CREATE, REPLACE or TRUNCATE statement, wherever it runs (sh -c included), and answers with ikb set and ikb remove (ikb 0.5.1, ideal-knowledge-base decision 2026-11-17-ikb-set-and-remove); reads pass; TAD_SQL_WRITE_OK=1 in the command lets a one-time migration through, recorded with it. record-the-work names ikb set and ikb remove for a row no record covers.
rejected: A skill line alone (the writes happened with record-the-work already saying named records); refusing every tad sql (reads are how agents look); no override (a schema change needs a one-time fill, as docs #260 did).
why: 56 tad sql writes by hand in 13 sessions on 2026-11-17 (research work-struggles), past the named records; ikb now covers them with a checked set and remove; the ikb session proposed the guard (its backlog tad-sql-guard).

brief: The session start prints each practice's first sentence, numbered by its id; the whole is one command away.
decision: The session start prints each practice's first sentence alone, numbered by its id and in the order of the ids; each practice whole, with why it holds and for whom, is one command away (lab-agent guide, scripts/ideal-agent practices). Practice 45's opening was split so that its first sentence says the practice.
rejected: The author shortening each long practice by hand (his choice was the first sentence; the whole stays as he wrote it). A summary line written for each practice (a second text of each practice to keep in step with the first).
why: The author chose it on 2026-11-17 (backlog practices-short-at-the-start, proposed by housekeeping): the practices' own words were 13.7 KB of the 14.4 KB session start; their first sentences are 7.9 KB. Numbering by position had shown practice 22, written last into the file, as the 44th.

decision: Every base keeps its work ahead as a backlog table (open, in-progress, done), beside its content and rendered like it.
rejected: A separate issue tracker, or a free-form Markdown TODO file: either splits the record across tools, so it cannot be asked or diffed with the rest.
why: Carried on 2026-11-17 from text-as-data-template's session_log (backlog-as-a-table), before it retired: everything queryable, versioned and diffable in one place. It grew into the standing tables - backlog, session_log, decisions, research, sources.

brief: At a task's start an agent asks only about the task's subject and acts; deeper reading only when a step needs it.
decision: AGENTS.md's generic part says: at a task's start ask only about its subject (about --subject S, or next --about S) and act; a record whole, a file past its first paragraph, another subject or the list of statements only when a step needs more.
rejected: A list of what not to read (an agent reads what it is pointed at; the entry points at the one question to ask first).
why: The author, 2026-11-17: an agent reads only summaries and goes into detail only when its current task needs it. Measured on surya's second keeper (ideal-agent research what-a-started-agent-reads): of 33.5 KB read before its first act, 12.1 KB was tad's help and 9.4 KB one subject whole.

brief: A wait on an item of the same base is named in blocked_by and clears itself when that item is done; waits stays free text for outside things.
decision: A wait on another item of the same base is named, not described: backlog gets `blocked_by` (ids of this base's items, comma-separated, pattern-checked; the records refuse an id that is no item) beside `waits`, which stays free text for what is outside the base (the author, a SIM card, hardware) and may no longer be empty (pattern). An item is clear when `waits` is empty and every item in `blocked_by` is done: phone-next and phone-queue read that off the data (the queue shows `blocked_on`, the items still open), so nothing is typed again when the blocking item is done. Records: backlog (--blocked-by) and backlog-blocked (set or take away). Landed 2026-11-17 in device-template and in surya-lab and google-walleye-lab, with the waits that were plainly item ids migrated (3 and 8 rows); the other waits stay as written. docs' own lane-next, phone-next and phone-queue and idealkb's generic backlog are not changed yet (their tables are the bases' own).
rejected: Reading ids out of the free text of waits: brittle (prose mentions ids without waiting on them). One field that holds either an item id or text, told apart by whether an item of that id exists: an item later created with that id changes what an old row means. A referenced field per wait (tad's references rule): a wait can name several items and the rule checks a single value; the record checks the list instead. A mutually exclusive pair enforced in the declaration: tad has no such rule; the queries read both. Changing the generic backlog of idealkb now: docs and the device bases own their tables, so the generic next query would fail where the column is missing; it follows once every base carries it.
why: Three times today a phone lane stalled on a stale wait - an empty string read as waiting, and twice an item still waiting on one already done - and each time a coordinator re-entered the row by hand. Practice 28: what an item waits on is read off the data, not typed as a state to keep true. The waits already in the two device bases named items in 3 and 8 rows (exactly an id, or a comma list of ids), so the shape was already in use; prose that merely mentions an id (for example 'walleye-ufs-readonly (not required) / walleye-first-fastboot-boot; a person witnesses...') stays free text because a query cannot read intent from prose.

brief: Every record has a one-line brief and every answer gives briefs; the whole is read only when the task needs it.
decision: Decisions and research gain brief, the record in one line of at most 200 characters, required by their named records (a longer one is refused); work, the log and sources have their title as brief. about, find and recent answer with briefs - where an older record has none, the first sentence of what it says - and about --whole true, row --id give the whole. A file opens with its brief, its first paragraph. AGENTS.md's generic part says to read briefs first and deeper only when the task needs it. A follower takes it with the pin; a base that names about.sql its own (linux-phone-oco/docs) carries the change to its own copy.
rejected: A brief only per subject (the summary layer condenses a subject, but each record still came whole in every answer). Cutting answers at a fixed width, as find and recent did with 100 characters (a cut is not a brief: it ends mid-word and says less than a sentence). A brief field on every table (work, the log and sources already open with a title that is their brief: a second one would say the same). Briefs filled by a program from the text (the first sentence stands in only for records written before; a brief is written by whoever records, who knows what matters).
why: The author, 2026-11-17, through ideal-agent: records - tables and files - should all have a brief summary to begin with, read by default; more detail only when the task needs it. Measured here: one subject's about answer 1,965 bytes whole, 273 by briefs.

brief: One pin-and-follow mechanism for the whole chain; improvements go back as PRs recorded as upstream items; rhizoid gets a slice mode.
decision: One mechanism, the one idealkb already has, for the whole chain: a source repository names what it gives (`generic`), releases by tag, and each follower pins a release and takes the slice with bin/follow.sh, weekly through update-pins and its own CI, ending 3 when a follower changed a generic file. idealkb is the source for every base (device bases are consumers of idealkb directly, like docs); device-template becomes a second source for the device layer (the parts contract, devices, phone queries, test-run) with its own `generic` list and releases, taken by device bases through the same script; follow.sh and update-pins.sh learn to take the source from the pin file (backlog). Pushing back: a general improvement made in a base or the template is a pull request to the source repository from the base's branch, recorded in the base as an upstream item (ikb upstream-item, form patch, --file auto for the patch or message, state draft, ready on the person's word, sent with the PR address as forwarded, landed when released). First-class upstreams: every device base ships two upstreams rows - idealkb (kind kb-instance) and device-template (kb-instance) - seeded in the template's data/upstreams.json, so the links are visible and queryable (tad q upstreams); docs records idealkb the same way. rhizoid stays the tool for forking whole repositories to patch them (linux-phone-oco/linux of sm7150-mainline/linux, tad-engine, argenv); what it lacks for this chain - a consumption mode for slices - goes on git-rhizoid's own backlog (slice-consumption), with follow.sh as its prototype, rather than worked around.
rejected: Every device base as a rhizcut (a fork) of idealkb or the template: drags the source's crate, data, research and release files into each base, and a base cannot follow two forks. git subtree or submodule: the generic files must sit at the base's root where tad reads them. Copier or cruft: Python, which the practices refuse for new tools, and an answers file beside idealkb.toml. Renovate as the updater: it can bump the version line but the files have to be laid by follow.sh anyway, which update-pins already does with its own CI. A new `ikb follow` that fetches its own standing parts at run time: attractive later (no clone with tags needed) but the weekly job works; kept as backlog. Waiting for rhizoid to be implemented: its consumption side is undesigned and the CLI stubbed; the chain is needed now.
why: The mechanism exists, is in use for two bases, has a drift verdict (exit 3), a gate on release and a weekly job, and is source-agnostic in follow.sh. What flows is a slice laid into a repository with its own data, which none of rhizoid (whole forks; consumption side undesigned; CLI stubbed), subtree (needs a prefix), Copier/cruft (Python, a second state file) or Renovate (bumps numbers) does. Making the links visible as upstreams rows costs two rows and uses what was built today.

brief: A commons base plus one open base per unit (device); the commons pulls and derives progress, never copies or types it.
decision: A commons base and one open base per unit (here: per device). 1. A device base (a repository made from device-template: surya-lab, google-walleye-lab, a third device) holds everything about that device: its queue (backlog with needs and waits), its log of tries, measurements (test_runs, test_results), decisions and research about that device, the sources it used, and its parts: one row per part of the device with a status, the evidence for it (a run id or link) and the date. It follows idealkb (pinned) and runs ikb like any base; its next item is its own `tad q next` (and `phone-queue` for its keeper). 2. docs holds only what helps every device: concepts, the components/features catalogue, the landscape, general decisions and research (dt-any-phone, how knowledge bases work), shared sources, the tests catalogue, the lab tooling (lab-tools), and a registry of devices (id, name, SoC, the address of its base, the template version). Support status and progress for a device are derived, never typed in docs: a feed record pulls each registered base's `parts` table over HTTPS in CI (feeds.yml), validates it against the contract the template declares, and fills support_status and feature_support with the device's own claim, its evidence link and its date; a device that has not declared a part, or whose base is unreachable or stale, shows "not known yet". docs never copies a device's queue, tries or measurements. 3. A third device is made from device-template (the template carries tables.toml, the idealkb pin, ikb, device.toml and tests); adding it to docs is one `ikb device` record with the base's address. 4. Moving today's mixed records: by the `device` field on backlog (docs 260) and by the project of the row - the rows of surya-lab and google-walleye-lab, docs' own device-named backlog/research/decisions/log, test_runs and test_results move to the device base, replayed record by record with their ids; general rows stay. A cross-reference from a device row to a docs concept is written `docs:ID` in text, since the references rule works within one base. 5. Lanes and launchers: a launcher for a device works in that device's repository and asks its base (`tad q next`, `lane-next` there); docs' lane-next stays only for the general queue; the observatory already reads each repository's oco.toml exports for the cross-device picture. 6. This supersedes decision 2026-11-17-one-database for devices only: docs and its lab tools stay one database; devices get theirs.
rejected: Keeping one database with a device field and lane-next: tells lanes apart, leaves the weight, the keeper's conflicts and one commons holding every device's work - the author's clutter. Per-device status typed in docs and in the device (two copies): drifts. Embedding device repositories in docs as git submodules or subtrees: copies the work, history and drift in. A GitHub template repository with no link back: no way to bring later template changes (the idealkb pin carries the generic part; the rest is a backlog item). Deriving status from CI results only (option C): a phone cannot run in CI, most parts would stay unknown. A push from each device into docs: needs a credential in every device base and a writer in docs' data; pull needs none. Superseding one-database wholesale: its reasons (two tools writing one database, glimpse conflicts) still hold for docs and its tools, which stay one database.
why: What is true of every large open project read: the commons holds schema, rules and process, each unit its own files and its own claim, and the commons derives by pulling - a status typed in both places drifts. Measured here: 40 of docs' own 81 backlog items, 34 of 49 research rows and 14 of 28 decisions name a device; test_results is 1.3 MB of docs' 2.0 MB; the keeper's landings every few minutes conflict whole-file in docs' data; a device is opened by other people as data (surya, walleye are forks of the template), and the author wants docs to hold only general knowledge useful to all devices. The `device` field and lane-next (docs 260) separate the lanes at no cost and stay until the move, but do not lighten docs or its conflicts.

decision: The knowledge-base layer is extracted from a base that already works - linux-phone-oco/docs, one tad database holding every linux-phone record, with the about link and the about query landed and measured - not designed first in the abstract. docs is its first follower.
rejected: Designing the layer first and fitting docs to it afterwards: it would encode assumptions that had not met real content.
why: text-as-data-template was extracted the same way from the software-engineering canon (its session_log, extract-template-from-working-repo, 2026-09-21; tad's 2026-09-21-extracted-from-a-working-repo): an abstraction is only right once it has met a real case.

decision: A base follows a release named in its idealkb.toml (version, and own: the generic files it keeps as its own). The generic files are listed in generic: the named statements whole, and AGENTS.md's and tables.toml's part between the lines idealkb:begin and idealkb:end - the rest of those two files is the base's. bin/follow.sh BASE VERSION lays a release; it ends 3 where the base had changed a generic file. bin/update-pins.sh now, run weekly by the lab machine for every base in consumers, moves the pin, runs the five generic queries against the base's data, and lands through the base's CI - or, where the base had its own change, pushes the branch and opens a pull request that is not landed: its diff is the signal to send the change upstream or to name the file own.
rejected: A declaration tad includes from another file (a change to tad for one layer, and a base that extends a standing table - docs' backlog has project, needs and proof - could not); vendoring as a git subrepo (the template's way: copies drifted); a GitHub workflow in each base (its pull requests start no CI); overwriting a base's change and landing it when CI passes (the change would be lost, not sent upstream); a Rust tool for the sync now (it copies files and compares them - shell orchestration; a tool when it grows logic); a pin moved with no argument (a script that changes state needs its intent said - practice 8: update-pins.sh now).
why: tad's pins are moved the same way (tad's 2026-11-11-pins-moved-by-the-lab): a pull request opened by GitHub's own token starts no CI, and the lab already lands through checks. Marked parts let a base keep its own lines in the same file (the entry's two lines about itself, its own tables) while the generic part stays current. A base's change shown and not landed loses nothing.

brief: A release is tagged only once every follower answers the five queries with main's generic files laid over it
decision: The release workflow runs bin/followers-answer.sh now before release-please, on every push to main: each base in consumers is cloned from its main, main's generic files are laid over it by follow.sh with its own files kept, and the five generic queries are asked of its data. While one does not answer, release-please does not run, so no tag is made; a merged release pull request waits, untagged, until the first push after which every follower answers. workflow_dispatch asks it any time.
rejected: A check on release-please's pull request (it never runs, for that reason); checking after the release, in the weekly pin (the break is found once followers are already asked to take it); a check on every pull request (a change waiting on a follower would block unrelated work); generic queries that test whether a column exists (SQL that guesses at a base's shape hides what a follower lacks).
why: Found 2026-11-17: v0.4.0's find and recent read decisions.brief, and linux-phone-oco/docs, which keeps tables.toml as its own, has no brief, so its weekly pin could only fail after the release was out. Proposed by the ideal-agent session, which made 0.4.0. Tried: ideal-agent answers all five; docs does not, for brief. First built as a check on release-please's pull request, it never ran there: a pull request opened with GitHub's own token starts no workflow, and land merged it with no checks.

decision: How to organise a knowledge base is written once, here, as a layer on tad: tad stays the database (tad init starts a bare one); ideal-knowledge-base pins tad's release and adds the rule of file and table, the about link, the generic named queries (about, next, find, row, recent) and records with --about, the standing tables, and one entry under 3 KB. A base follows it by a pinned release. text-as-data-template is split between the two and retired with a pointer. How an agent finds its way in a base is a skill of grenudi/ideal-agent; ideal-project-playbook keeps the process and points here for its standing records.
rejected: Renaming text-as-data-template into the knowledge base (folds a database's scaffold into it); putting the layer into tad (tad's concern is the data alone); folding it into ideal-project-playbook (a base is not a software project) or ideal-agent (a base is read by people and the face too); a copied template (copies drift); a spec alone (nothing checks a base follows it); a plugin skill as the vehicle (only Claude agents get it); llms.txt as the entry (it serves outside readers of a site); embeddings (a few thousand rows are answered exactly by a checked link and named queries); a table of questions naming their queries (a second index to keep true); folders per Diataxis kind or PARA bucket (the tables already sort by kind).
why: The author, 2026-11-17: one general place for how to organise a knowledge base, used by every base, so that agents find what they need instead of reading everything; corrected by him the same day - tad stays a database, the knowledge base is a layer on top - and accepted. The full record, with what was weighed: linux-phone-oco/docs decision 2026-11-17-ideal-knowledge-base.

brief: An agent starts with ikb --help and ikb help RECORD; IKB.md is for people; completions ask ikb as you type.
decision: An agent starts with `ikb --help` (every record of the base, one line each) and reads `ikb help RECORD` for the record it needs (about 0.8 KB); IKB.md stays as the page for people to browse. `ikb completions bash|zsh|fish|nushell` prints a small glue script; at completion time the shell asks `ikb complete --cur=WORD WORDS...`, which answers from the base's own records (record names, each record's options not yet given, `auto` after --material/--file, shell names) - so the completions are never out of date and never written by hand. The help, the man page, IKB.md and the completions all come from the same records (the argenv contract of the fixed commands plus the run-time records); only the four glue scripts are text. bin/install-ikb.sh writes the completions for the shells it finds.
rejected: argenv's own completions generator for the whole script: it writes the record names into the script at generation time, so a script made in one base is wrong in another and stale after a new record (tad avoids this only for positional words through `asked`; ikb's records are subcommands, not positionals). Writing completion words by hand per base. A fifth, base-specific completion file in each base.
why: Measured by the second before/after: agents read what the skill sends them to; sending them to the 10-13 KB IKB.md (every record concatenated) made their start as heavy as reading tad statements, whereas `ikb --help` plus one `ikb help RECORD` is about 2-3 KB. The author's intent: ikb explains itself through generated help, a man page and completions.

brief: ikb: one pinned binary builds each base's record commands and man page from its records/*.sql at run time; no fork.
decision: ikb is one released Rust binary (crate ikb/ in idealkb, command line declared with argenv, tad's statements library pinned) that is run in a base and reads that base's own records/*.sql at run time: every record becomes a subcommand with its header's typed options, and the contract and man page are built from those headers. What it adds over tad r: per-record help and one man page written to IKB.md; long text from a file or stdin (--NAME-file, - for stdin) so no shell quoting; id made from the brief when none is given; `about`, project and brief length checked before the run, with the accepted values named; research --material creates and names research/SUBJECT/YYYY-MM-DD/; canon and render run after every record and say one line; --by from OCOECO_BY. It does not parse SQL itself, hold any table, or re-implement tad: it calls tad. A base extends ikb by adding records/*.sql, never by forking code. Per-record --help and completion of enumerated values belong in tad (backlog on tad); ikb help NAME covers it until then.
rejected: Rhizoid/rhizcut fork of the ikb crate into each base: a fork is for patching code, and bases differ only in records, which are data - a fork would carry a Rust workspace into every knowledge base and make every pull a merge; rhizoid stays the way for a base that really must patch ikb's source. A library plus a thin per-base binary: still a build per base. Plugins: a loading mechanism for what a SQL file already declares. Static subcommands generated at build time: a new record would need a release. An MCP server over the CLI: adds schema and context cost; the man page is the interface, MCP can wrap ikb later. Sequential ids (adr-tools): collide across branches; ids are slugs of the brief. $EDITOR flows: not for agents.
why: Measured 17% of tad r calls failed, 14 of 41 failures only asked --help, 100 of 240 calls carried long text through shell quoting, and canon/render printed 74 KB. docs already overrides five generic records (--project), so a fixed generic CLI would be wrong for it; reading records/*.sql at run time makes each base's difference automatic and keeps pulls trivial because nothing is copied.

brief: ikb set and ikb remove change or take away one existing row of any declared table, checked; no tad sql by hand.
decision: ikb gets two fixed commands: `ikb set TABLE --key K [--key K2] --field NAME=VALUE ...` changes fields of one existing row of any declared table, and `ikb remove TABLE --key K` takes one row away. Both read the base's own tables.toml: a missing or wrong table lists the tables with their keys, a wrong field lists the fields with their allowed values, a key of several fields says how many --key values and in what order, a row that does not exist is refused (adding is its record's job), an enum value outside its list says the list. tad checks every rule before a change is kept (tad::set puts the file back; a removal runs through tad sql, which does the same); canon and render run after. A named record is kept for what is said in several fields at once (backlog-status, backlog-needs, part). The roles session's idea of a hook that refuses `tad sql` writes belongs in ideal-agent's guard, with this as its message.
rejected: One named record per table and field (backlog-waits, source-remove, decision-about ...): dozens of statements, base-specific, most never used. A generic SQL record taking table, id, field and value: a table or a column cannot be a parameter of a named statement, and the values would not be checked against the declaration. Adding a generic backlog-status to idealkb: docs and the device template already keep their own (with project or without), so it would only create drift in their own lists; ikb set covers its waits. Leaving tad sql allowed with a warning: the agents' route of least resistance stays. Putting the command in tad: tad is released separately; ikb already reads the declaration, and tad::set is what it calls.
why: Measured by the roles session (ideal-agent research work-struggles, 41 transcripts of 2026-11-17): 56 hand-written tad sql writes past the named records in 13 sessions - backlog status/waits/note 22, decisions 8, sources deleting and updating 9, practices 5, test_results inserts 4, research deletes 2, subjects inserts 2. About 41 of them are one field of one row or one removal in idealkb's standing tables; a record per field and table would be dozens of statements, most unused; one generic checked command is one thing to learn and its errors teach the tables. tad already has the checked set (tad set TABLE --key K --set F=V) but with no help for tables, fields or values and no refusal of an absent row - agents reached for sql instead.

brief: IKB.md is not kept anywhere; ikb page only prints; help, man page and completions are generated on demand.
decision: IKB.md is not kept in any base. `ikb page` only prints the one page (for people: `ikb page > page.md`); the `--write` option is gone, docs' verify no longer refreshes it, AGENTS.md points at `ikb --help` and `ikb help RECORD`. The man page, the help, the page and the completions are all generated on demand from the records, never stored.
rejected: Keep IKB.md as a committed page for people, refreshed by verify: a drifting duplicate of the SQL headers, and only honest when ikb runs in CI. Generate it at publish time into the Pages site: no one asked for it there; ikb page can feed it if someone does. Keep `ikb page --write`: a writer of a file nobody reads. Hand-writing any of it: the man page, help, page and completions come from the records.
why: Nothing read it that the help does not serve: agents go to ikb help RECORD, people can open the record headers in records/*.sql on GitHub or run ikb page, CI checks nothing about it. A committed copy of every record header drifts with each record and each wording change (five regenerations in a day), adds a 9-13 KB file to the read path wherever a skill points at it, and needs ikb in CI to be kept honest, which the orchestration rightly refuses. The author doubted the file needs to exist; the measurement agrees.

decision: A research row is the summary of a research: question, finding condensed, sources, date, about - as it was. It gains material, the dated folder holding its own notes, excerpts and measurements (research/SUBJECT/YYYY-MM-DD/, checked by pattern), and supersedes, the research it is a later version of (checked to exist). Research redone is a new row that supersedes the old: the old stays, reachable by find and row, and leaves about's answer; superseded-by is read off, never typed. The folder is the base's own, never a generic file; nothing loads it but a reader who follows the row.
rejected: A new table of research summaries beside research: one nature under two names (practice 32). Typing both ends of a supersession, as adr-tools and PEPs do: one end is read off. A folder named by the research id rather than its subject: the subject is what a reader comes from, and the date tells versions apart. Material inside the row: the row is read with every answer about its subject. Scratch kept out of git (ArtCraft's plan/): fine for scratch, but research must keep its sources.
why: The author, 2026-11-17: research must be kept with its sources and links, yet not load every future agent's start. Others keep detail one link away and supersede rather than delete (research research-aside-world). The research table already is the short summary row the author proposed; what it lacked was the link to its material and supersession.

decision: A subject's answer leads with its summary: a standing table summaries (about, date, says up to 1500 characters, condenses), one row per subject renewed in place, written by tad r summary, which fills condenses from the records about the subject as they stand. tad q about --subject S returns the summary first, then what was recorded since, the open work and the sources of the research shown, and the condensed records by id on one line (--whole gives them in full; row --id one). tad q about without a subject says, per subject, its records, what they weigh, its summary's date, and summary due - when they weigh over 8 KB with no summary, or over 4 KB were recorded since it. The session that records into a subject renews its summary when due, in the same change; a keeper does it at hand-over.
rejected: Rewriting a how-it-stands row as the only copy: it erodes (ACE's context collapse) - the records stay and the summary only condenses. Each summary version kept as a row with supersedes: git keeps the versions, and the records are the history; rows would weigh on find and recent for nothing. A count threshold, as the author offered: what grows without bound is weight, not number - the count is shown beside it. A typed status line each cycle (Cochrane's What's New): what was recorded since is read off the data, never typed (practice 28). A background model on a schedule (Beads): nobody knows a subject better than the session that just recorded into it; it can come later for subjects nobody tends. Condensed records one line each: still about 130 bytes a record, unbounded again; ids alone are a twentieth of it. The author's word how it stands for the table: summary is the plain word with one meaning, and how-it-stands already names docs' itemised hand-over rows, which are records a summary condenses.
why: The author, 2026-11-17: when one subject gathers many records its answer must not grow without bound; a short how-it-stands sits on top, dated, citing the records it condenses, renewed when they move on. Measured: docs' microphone answer grew from 9.4 KB to 15.9 KB as its records went from 18 to 26. Everyone who keeps living knowledge does this (research summary-layer-world); size is the trigger because a bounded answer is the aim, and 8 KB is roughly two thousand tokens - the answer a fresh session still reads whole.

decision: The generic queries are named for the question they answer, in the words an agent already uses: about (everything known of a subject), next (the work ahead), find (where something is said), row (one record whole) and recent (what was recorded lately). find and recent give ids and first words only; row gives the whole as JSON.
rejected: search (find is the word of grep and of every shell), get or show (they say nothing of what comes back), todo (next says it is ordered), latest or log (recent covers every record table, not the log alone), a single ask command taking a question (a second language beside SQL).
why: Measured in docs: the answers are small (2 open items under 0.2 KB, a subject's 18 rows 9.4 KB) when asked by subject; what costs is reading whole rows to find which one. Ids first, then one row whole, keeps every step small.

brief: Upstream work is two tables, upstreams and upstream_items, one shape for any upstream and any form; ikb adds them.
decision: idealkb gains `upstreams` (where knowledge can flow: kind code-project|list|tracker|wiki|standard|person-team|kb-instance|distro, address, how contributions are made, contacts) and `upstream_items` (each thing headed somewhere: form patch|information|correction|question|finding; state draft, ready, sent, under-review, changes-requested, accepted, landed, held, rejected, superseded, not-needed, withdrawn; from_work linking back to a backlog item, decision or research, checked by the record; domain, tags, about, local_ref, file, sent_on, forwarded, bug, version, supersedes, applied_upstream, waits). Records upstream, upstream-item (--file auto makes upstream/UPSTREAM/ID/ for a patch or a long message) and upstream-state; queries `tad q upstream` (what waits, longest first) and `tad q upstreams`; ikb generates the commands. Another idealkb instance is an upstream of kind kb-instance: a general improvement made in a domain base goes upstream to idealkb the same way.
rejected: A second tracker next to the backlog (the queue repo grown into one): two sources of truth drift. Only an upstream column on backlog items: a patch sent in several versions has nowhere to go and no state beyond open/done. Item files with front matter indexed into a table (DEP-3 style): an indexer and two truths; the row stays the truth and the file holds what prose cannot. One kind per upstream (git, wiki, standard): the differences are the form and the how-text, not the shape. Mirroring the remote tracker's status or review threads: link the archive instead. A separate state machine for following an upstream (Renovate): another direction, another table when needed.
why: One shape serves a project, a list, a wiki, a standard, a person and another knowledge base; the item's form says what it is. The state only moves forward and the person's word that a draft may go is the state ready, so an agent never sets a consent flag. A row holds what is queried; the patch or message stays a file beside it. Measured need: docs' six upstream-* items know only open/in-progress/done, and destinations, contacts and send commands live in a README outside git.

decision: A release tag is moved only after the change has landed - by land --tag, which confirms the merge first.
rejected: Tagging by hand in the same breath as landing.
why: A job moved v1.0.1 after its change had been refused, so the tag claimed a fix it did not hold; a rule kept in mind failed, so land enforces it.

decision: Projects call the conveyor's reusable workflows, pinned to a version; nothing is copied into them.
rejected: A template repository; copy-paste with care; composite actions alone (they cannot hold whole jobs).
why: snapall and lab-agent carry about 500 lines of nearly identical workflow each; copies drift and fixes do not travel.

decision: The extraction is proven by moving snapall and lab-agent onto the conveyor with byte-for-byte the same published repositories - same URLs, same keys.
rejected: Proving it on a new project first.
why: An extraction that changes what users receive cannot be told from a regression.

decision: 'Nothing changed for users' means the same addresses and key, every signature verifying, and the README's install line installing the new release - not byte-identical packages.
rejected: Byte-for-byte identical repositories (the earlier wording of this decision).
why: Arch packages built twice differ in their timestamps; the byte promise could not be kept and would test nothing a user meets.

decision: Each project keeps its own signing key for now; one key for the whole commons is considered later.
rejected: One organisation key from the start.
why: A single key would change the trust of every existing installation at once.

decision: The conveyor's direction is to build in the project's own Nix environment (the shell.nix the lab machine uses), from Nix's binary cache; the patient retry stays as a fallback meanwhile.
rejected: Only retrying; switching to another single distribution's mirrors.
why: The author asked whether we must rely on Ubuntu's archive; Nix gives one pinned toolchain for the lab and CI, from a more robust source.

decision: A project describes its delivery in one small declaration file; the workflow inputs stay few.
rejected: Workflow inputs only.
why: Inputs grow without limit and are scattered across callers; a file is read, reviewed and checked like data.

decision: The conveyor's scripts live inside its workflows, not as files it fetches.
rejected: A scripts folder checked out at run time.
why: A called workflow does not know which version of itself was called, so fetched files could drift from the workflow; inline, they move together with the tag.

decision: Arch (pacman) and Alpine (apk, for postmarketOS) first, each with a signed repository.
rejected: Debian and RPM repositories first - installation on them stays verified, as today.
why: These are what the lab, the desktops and the phone actually run.

decision: The declaration is read by a typed Rust reader that refuses unknown fields, not by Python inside the workflows.
rejected: Python's tomllib inline (the first version); a shell TOML parser.
why: Shipped code that other projects call: with Python a misspelled field is silently replaced by a default - a bug Rust's types rule out by design. Asked by the author: no Python for new things.

decision: Cutting versions stays with each language's own tool (release-plz for Rust); the conveyor starts from a release tag.
rejected: The conveyor owning versions.
why: Versioning is part of a project's own decisions and tooling.

decision: A release is said once it can be taken. Each program's releaser makes it a draft, with its tag - release-please with draft and force-tag-creation, release-plz with git_release_draft - and the conveyor, having attached every file, says it: one step, once, at the end of the conveyor every program already calls. A release already said stays as it was.
rejected: Each who takes a release taking the newest one with its files (every reader carries the gap); the conveyor making the release itself from the tag (versions and notes stay with each program's own releaser); a release made public, then taken back to a draft by the conveyor until its files are there (said, then unsaid: the gap only shortened); a draft without its tag (release-please would not find the release before it, and the PKGBUILD's source is the tag's).
why: A release was made and its files were built after it: for minutes the newest release of a program had nothing to take, and each who takes one had to know of it - the author's observatory took the newest that had its files.

decision: An Alpine repository is built in one container and signed in another: the project code (its APKBUILD build) runs where no key is; abuild rootpkg and index, which sign, run in a fresh container that alone receives APK_SIGNING_KEY. The key is the project own (an RSA key made like abuild-keygen), its public half committed beside the APKBUILD.
rejected: Building and signing in one step (the project code beside the key); signing in a later job by splitting and re-signing each .apk (re-packing the format by hand, fragile); GitHub JavaScript actions inside an Alpine container (they do not run on arm64 Alpine); one key for the whole commons (decided per project for now: 2026-11-11-keys-per-project).
why: As with the pacman path, the code being packaged never shares a process space with the key; a fresh container leaves nothing running from the build. abuild signs each package at packaging time, so signing cannot wait for a later job without re-packing the files.

decision: A device lab made from this template holds data only - the manifest, the phone's own checks, its reports, its records; every tool is devlab's and reads the manifest.
rejected: Copying surya-lab and renaming (the scripts would drift per phone); a template carrying its own scripts beside devlab (two routes to the same work).
why: The design asked for 2026-11-10 (linux-phone-oco/docs backlog device-template): the next phone must not inherit a copy of surya's scripts to edit; surya-lab already shows where copies drift (its shell tools and devlab doing the same work twice).

decision: The phone docs begin their own history: their first release is 0.1.0, and versions stay below 1.0 while the docs are still forming. The changelog and manifest inherited from the template they were made from are cleared, with a note saying whose history that was. Release-please reads its config and manifest.
rejected: Releasing 1.0.0 as proposed (promises what is not there); tagging 1.2.0 (it is the template's version, not the docs'); keeping the inherited changelog (it tells another repository's story as this one's).
why: The docs were made from text-as-data-template on 2026-11-04 and carried its history (1.0.0 to 1.2.0) as if their own; never released, release-please found no tag and proposed 1.0.0 - a claim of stability for docs days old and changing hourly. Found after landing: with no release at all, release-please treats the next as the first and gives it its own default, 1.0.0, whatever the manifest says; the config's initial-version (0.1.0) is what decides a first release.

brief: A backlog item names the device it is for; phone-next and phone-queue require --device, and lane-next gives a lane's next item of a kind (phone, research, build)
decision: backlog gains device (a devices id) and needs takes phone, research or build. The records that set needs refuse a phone, research or build item without a device (tad has no conditional rule). phone-next and phone-queue require --device; lane-next --device D --needs N gives the lane's next item, for its keeper and launchers. Filled once: open phone items in docs, surya-lab, lab-tools (about deep-sleep) and sxmo-deviceprofiles (about sx-surya) are xiaomi-surya; google-walleye-lab's and lab-tools' about google-walleye are google-walleye. The briefs, AGENTS.md and the README name the device.
rejected: An optional --device (a walleye keeper would still take surya's items); the lane read off the project (surya's phone items live in docs, about components); a device on components (components are shared across devices); a needs value per device (needs says what kind, device says whose); a table rule (tad has none conditional yet - the records enforce it).
why: Per-lane launchers (ideal-agent decision 2026-11-17-a-lane-starts-its-own) need a lane's next item; needs said only phone, and phone-next could hand surya's items to walleye's keeper. Orchestration (owner of docs), 2026-11-17: the device is a fact of the item, devices.id the reference; required, not optional; list what cannot be placed.

brief: Each phone has a lane coordinator that starts and renews its keepers; a scheduled task only nudges it
decision: A lane coordinator per phone (surya-coordinator) is a visible session in the sidebar: it starts the phone keepers itself, continues or replaces each when it reports, archives finished ones, and routes what needs the author's hands to the top coordinator. The scheduled task linux-phone-keeper-waker only sends it 'continue' when the queue has work and no keeper is live.
rejected: A hidden scheduled waker that does the keeper's work itself (invisible, no parent to receive reports); the top coordinator starting keepers itself (one session for every lane, its context swamped).
why: The author wants every running piece visible in the sidebar, and a keeper's parent receives its reports automatically; the top coordinator then coordinates coordinators.

decision: linux-phone's agents are sessions with a name, a brief kept in docs' prompts/ (bring-up, orchestration, feature-research) and places they own; their shared state is the data they already keep - backlog, decisions, research, session logs, the phone's results - read through ocoeco and drawn on the face, not a tracker of their own. An orchestration session tends the conveyor and the agents: it checks the ways by measuring hand-work, turns every rule it can into a mechanism (devlab's hold, Claude Code command hooks, CI), keeps the face fluent, and starts a research session per hard feature. Research parallelises; changes to the one phone are queued through bring-up.
rejected: A new agents-orchestration repository now (the agents' runner and its redesign live in creation-guidelines/lab-agent as oco-agent, and how-we-work under creation-guidelines; a third place would be one nature under three names - what is linux-phone's stays in docs, what every project shares goes to oco-agent when it is general); a tracker beside ocoeco such as Beads (two records of one work); an always-on watching agent (tokens without end - patrols on a schedule and hooks do it cheaper); one agent per feature implementing in parallel (one phone: changes race).
why: The author, 2026-11-17, asked for an orchestrating agent, per-feature agents, perhaps an agents-orchestration repository, and the most efficient organisation found by research. Read: the Craft apps' fleet (ownership by subsystem, rules kept once, an oracle gating progress), Gas Town (work state in git, agents as identities), Anthropic (few well-bounded workers, parallel only when independent, ~15x tokens), Claude Code (hooks enforce, sessions and schedules run). Our ecosystem already holds most of it; what was missing was roles, briefs and enforcement.

decision: The briefs in prompts/ keep only what is linux-phone's - what a role owns, its places, devlab and the phone, recording in docs - and name the skill for the method from the ideal-agent plugin: orchestrate-agents, research-a-feature, bring-up-a-part, with lab-session-start, land-a-change, record-the-work and change-a-device. The general research and decisions on how agents are organised (landscape photocraft-fleet, gas-town, anthropic-multi-agent, claude-code-agents; decisions 2026-11-17-agents-organised-by-the-data and -experts-written-not-standing) are carried into ideal-agent as its own; the rows here stay as linux-phone's.
rejected: Keeping the whole method in each brief (copies drift between projects); deleting the linux-phone rows that were carried over (they are linux-phone's history and decisions, cited by its own records).
why: The author, 2026-11-17: one home for general agent know-how (grenudi/ideal-agent), each project's docs keeping the domain-specific knowledge, so both improve in their own place.

decision: Calls on surya are made to work as pulpoff/linux-surya carries them - q6voice from sdm845-mainline with SM7150's CVD 2.3 set-up and a hostless VoiceMMode1 link in our kernel, then UCM Voice Call with TX topology 0x10F70 and a 1-channel uplink capture on TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3 - and proven by the phone itself calling blueSIP's public echo line (+49 89 721010 99701): three tones played on the loudspeaker are heard by the bottom mic going up and again, a round trip later, coming back on the earpiece, found by Goertzel envelopes in a Rust subcommand of devlab-health. Its tone line (99702) proves the downlink alone; the SIM's own mailbox is the fallback. At most one call of 25 s a day; skipped as unknown without a SIM, a registration or the call path. Mobile data is checked every boot over the bearer's own interface (registration, DNS, pings, 100 kB), with a weekly 5 MB throughput run, under 0.3 GB a month. The first step is the kernel: q6voice and the VoiceMMode1 link, settled by the check call-audio-path, which fails today.
rejected: Digital loop through in-call record/playback ports (unknown whether sdm845-mainline's q6voice has them; kept for later if it does). A second phone on a stand that answers (hardware and a second SIM; the echo line does the same for nothing). A programmable number (Twilio and the like: an account, money, a public endpoint). sipgate's echo 10005 (SIP-internal, not dialable from a mobile, private customers dropped 2025). Old or foreign echo lines (portunity 0211, sip2sip +31, C*NET: unconfirmed, international rates). Calling the author's other phone as the automatic test (reaches a person; stays the half-manual mode of 2026-11-11-telephony-checks). Downstream's 0x10F71 topology (silence without Xiaomi's calibration). A call on every boot (45 a day in bring-up).
why: An independent mainline tree on this very phone already carries calls with sound both ways, so the biggest unknown is porting, not discovery; the check call-audio-path settles it without a SIM or a call. The echo line is the only public German echo attested across years and sources, and costs a landline-rate call; its tone line splits a failure into downlink and uplink. The acoustic loop proves exactly what a person uses - loudspeaker, mic, uplink, network, downlink, earpiece - and needs no driver feature beyond what calls need anyway (the uplink capture is written to a file instead of discarded). Daily and short keeps the cost to cents and the people reached to none.

brief: docs keeps general knowledge for all devices; each device has its own open base; docs pulls and derives progress. one-database stays for docs and its tools.
decision: Decision 2026-11-17-one-database is superseded for devices only.
