why: Health measured only from the lab is health only while the lab is connected and remembers to ask; a phone that checks itself after every boot leaves a record for every change. Shipped code is Rust (2026-11-11-rust-for-what-ships): strings and structure - JSON escaping, the report - are where shell is fragile. The probes themselves only read sysfs and the system's own tools, which is what postmarketOS's tests and bootrr do in shell, so they can be contributed there.

decision: The health suite reaches phones as an Alpine package (devlab-health: the runner, the checks, the unit and the timer) published through the package conveyor once it publishes Alpine repositories (cv-apk); until then devlab puts the same files on the phone itself, as the development path.
rejected: devlab copying files onto the phone for good (a second delivery route beside the conveyor; nothing updates it); building the package in lab-tools' own CI (copying what the conveyor exists to do once).
why: The commons has one packaging conveyor that every project calls (linux-package-distribution-oco/conveyor) and it already builds aarch64-musl binaries; a package is how postmarketOS installs and updates anything, and it gives the phone updates the way the lab machine already gets them.

brief: The lpoco family has one version: release-plz version_group lpoco, tags stay per package (lpoco-vX, lpoco-health-vX)
decision: lpoco and lpoco-health (and every later lpoco-*) share one version through release-plz's version_group, starting at 0.1.7 (lpoco-health's). The dispatcher refuses a program whose --version differs, so every lpoco-* program must answer --version with 'NAME X.Y.Z' (lpoco-health now does). Tags stay one per package: lpoco-v{version} for the dispatcher (lab-side only, no phone package) and lpoco-health-v{version} for the conveyor's phone package.
rejected: One shared git tag for the whole family: the conveyor reads lpoco-health-v* for the phone package, a shared tag would break it. Independent versions per program: the dispatcher could not tell a compatible program from a stale one.
why: Decision 2026-11-17-bringup-in-lab-tools asks for one version pin for the family and one release; version_group gives it without moving the conveyor's tag prefix. Proof: lpoco-refuses-mixed-versions.

brief: One health suite, lpoco-health, on the phone: upstreamable shell tests in pmOS's shape, our runner; conditions detected at run time; switches with reasons; docs keep only facts and results
decision: linux-phone-oco has one health suite, lpoco-health (devlab-health renamed; same checks, same test_results shape, same report on the phone). It keeps the shape decision 2026-11-17-health-on-the-phone chose: small shell checks printing 'pass|fail|skip TEST COMPONENT detail' (postmarketOS's test shape, so a check can later become a postmarketos-test-* subpackage by a merge request), gathered by our static Rust runner. New: (1) detected conditions - conditions/*.sh work out no-sim, no-modem, no-network at every run; checks say skip_on NAME and report 'skip: no SIM card'; nothing is written down. (2) chosen switches - lpoco-health off TEST --reason WORDS [--by], on TEST, list, kept in /etc/lpoco-health/switches (test, reason, who, when), reported as 'skip: switched off: reason (by who, when)'; never without a reason; from the lab devlab suite off|on|list and the MCP tools health_switch_off/on, health_switches. (3) the command line is declared with argenv (health/src/cli.rs). (4) docs hold only facts about the hardware and the results; the phone's state (SIM in or out) is never recorded there; backlog sim-removed-skips closed as superseded, its log entry stays. (5) provisioning: the Alpine package lpoco-health (published by the conveyor since 0.1.6) is what devlab suite put now takes; --runner builds the runner on the lab for what is unreleased; put migrates the old devlab-health reports, month data ledger and once-a-day marks with nothing lost, and the package keeps devlab-health and /usr/lib/devlab/health as other names until the phone's own checks call the new ones. (6) upstream: we do not fork postmarketOS' test pieces now; we write our checks so they could be sent upstream, and revisit when their system-level tests or farm admission exist.
rejected: A. Building fully on postmarketOS upstream (fork their test pieces into a rhizcut-synced subfolder, send improvements back as merge requests): the right long-term friend - open GitLab, clear review rules, Python only host-side so it does not weigh against it - but today it gives us only the initramfs hook, which halts the boot and covers kernel tests, not the after-boot system tests we run; their farm has one OnePlus 6T and registration is token-gated; whether rhizcuts handle a GitLab upstream and a subfolder is not known; licence/CLA and fork-sync cost not known. Revisit when upstream gets system tests or admits other phones. C. A different shape of our own: nothing to gain over B. rust-script tests with a bundle crate (the author's lean, weighed fairly): the dependency direction is right (bundle depends on tests, not the reverse) and nextest shows it works, but rust-script needs rust+cargo on the phone (Alpine aarch64 72 MiB download, 206 MiB installed plus gcc, musl-dev, llvm-libs, network for crates), a registry (inventory/linkme) is unproven on aarch64 musl and links everything into one binary; kept instead: the same direction by discovery - the runner finds tests in directories, tests depend on nothing of it - and Rust for logic (runner, ledger, tone) built on the lab as a static binary; revisit as prebuilt per-test binaries when a check needs more than shell. Building each test on the lab as its own binary now: cross-build work for 13 small shell checks that need none. A settings store in docs or in devlab's lab-side files: wrong place for the phone's state, goes stale. Keeping the name devlab-health: the suite is linux-phone-oco's, not devlab's; the old name stays only as an alias. Lab-built runner by default: the package is published, so the package is the default.
why: The SIM removal showed that a state of the phone cannot live in docs: it is true for minutes and the phone knows it better. Every mature phone CI (bootrr, LAVA, postmarketOS's test package, CI-tron) keeps tests as small executables with one result line each and a thin runner, device facts as data and an explicit skip; nobody compiles on the device. Upstream postmarketOS (checked 2026-11-17) runs on-device tests only from the initramfs, halting the boot; boot and system tests - the modem, audio, sensors, sleep and budgets we need - are not built, and their farm is one phone behind a token gate. Our checks and runner already have the shape, so it is kept and extended, not replaced (decision 2026-11-17-health-on-the-phone weighed first).

brief: lpoco mcp is lpoco-lab's MCP server with every program's tools under its name: lab_*, health_*, bringup_*; the bare names stay
decision: lpoco mcp runs lpoco-lab mcp. One server lists lab_run/put/get/kernel_*/reboot (the bare names run, put, ... answer the same function), health_* and bringup_image_info/check (which run lpoco-bringup beside it). A new program joins by adding its prefixed tools to that router.
rejected: A proxy that starts each lpoco-NAME mcp and merges their tools: a child process per program and an MCP client for no gain while only the lab holds a phone. A separate lpoco-mcp crate: a second copy of the door and its device loading. Renaming the tools with no aliases: breaks every agent's saved config (lpoco-names-sweep keeps aliases until it ends).
why: Agents look in one place; the rmcp router already held the lab tools, and prefixes by program name need no second protocol layer. Proof lpoco-mcp-lists-every-family-tool lists them over real stdio.

decision: Every test sound is quiet unless the phone's manifest says otherwise: [hear] level_dbfs (default -40 dBFS) and volume (default 25%), capped at full scale and 100%, used by devlab hear and given to every check through the phone's health.env (TEST_TONE_DBFS, TEST_VOLUME).
rejected: Lowering the hard-coded numbers (no setting, and other checks would choose their own); a level per check (a phone in a home has one acceptable loudness).
why: The author, 2026-11-17, urgently: a full-scale test sine played at night; test sounds must be quiet, with a setting for it in the suite. devlab hear had -12 dBFS at 60% volume hard-coded.

brief: devlab no longer says a RAM boot leaves the slots as they were: it reads the bootloader's A/B flags before and after and says what changed; switching the active slot is a gated word of its own.
decision: fastboot boot now and set-active read current-slot and the slot-unbootable/successful/retry-count flags of both slots before and after, and say the difference; the verdict of a boot is where the phone went, not fastboot's exit. set-active (metadata) is refused unless the manifest says [fastboot] slot_switch = true, separate from writes.
rejected: keeping 'nothing written, slots as they were' (true of devlab, false of the phone); folding the switch into writes = true (a flag change is not a partition write, and walleye may need one without the other); restoring slot a by devlab on its own after a try (a write that needs the author's word).
why: walleye's try b: devlab wrote nothing, yet the bootloader's A/B logic ended on slot b with slot a unbootable, and devlab, reading fastboot's failing exit, called the try refused.

decision: devlab holds the phone for every change it makes - flash, provision, reboot, root commands, put, kernel install, try and remove, suite put - by an exclusive lock on STATE/phone.lock, from the command line and the MCP door alike; a second change waits for the first and says so. Reading needs no hold.
rejected: flock around devlab by convention (forgotten once is enough; and wrapped around a devlab that also locks, it would wait on itself); a lock only in the MCP door.
why: Two sessions now work with one phone (the bring-up session beside the conveyor's): a reboot under a kernel try would strand a test or misreport it. A lock each session must remember to take is a rule kept by care; devlab taking it itself is kept by the tool.

decision: devlab offers its structured door over MCP (devlab mcp, stdio, with rmcp): run, put and get a file, the health report, kernel install, try and status, reboot and wait - each the same function the command line calls.
rejected: A separate MCP server project beside devlab (two doors to keep in step); MCP through a generic shell tool (every call a quoting puzzle).
why: Agent access plans every tool's structured door over MCP in Rust with rmcp, devlab among the first (aa-two-doors); an agent then works with the phone without a person and without a shell's quoting layer.

decision: The ways an agent must keep on the lab (land, not a push to main; no Python; the phone only through devlab) are held by Claude Code command hooks that call devlab guard, a subcommand of devlab in Rust, with its cases tested.
rejected: Hook scripts in shell with jq (logic in shell, untested; the guide says Rust for logic); a separate guard tool beside devlab (a second place that must learn the phones addresses); permission deny rules in settings (match command prefixes only: miss sudo, env, sh -c and $(...), and cannot tell a branch push from a push to main).
why: A way that must be remembered is forgotten; the hook refuses when it is tried and says why, to the agent that tried. devlab already knows the phones (their manifests and learned addresses), so the guard knows what reaching the phone means.

brief: Test kernels are booted from their EFI image (vmlinuz.efi), and the conveyor refuses anything else.
decision: Test kernels are booted from their EFI image (vmlinuz.efi), and the conveyor refuses anything else.
rejected: Sort keys, a stored default entry, a second boot partition - each checked and ruled out.
why: A gzip kernel was chosen by the bootloader, counted down, and could not start - silently, before any log.

brief: The audio pin driver's function slots for the SoundWire pins follow the phone's own Android kernel (gpio19 swr_tx_data in slot 3, gpio23 swr_rx_data in slot 2).
decision: The audio pin driver's function slots for the SoundWire pins follow the phone's own Android kernel (gpio19 swr_tx_data in slot 3, gpio23 swr_rx_data in slot 2).
rejected: Treating the clocks switching off as the cause; changing the macros' autosuspend.
why: A bus clash on the TX bus came right before the codec's timeout; the driver's table disagreed with the vendor's pin description on exactly these pins; corrected, the codec came up on the first boot.

brief: Boots that come up without the sound card are measured over a run of reboots before anything is changed.
decision: Boots that come up without the sound card are measured over a run of reboots before anything is changed.
rejected: Unmasking the helper service masked for the suspend crash, on a hunch.
why: It happened once in several boots; the audio processor's service channel never appeared. A guess at a cause would be untestable without a rate.

brief: With the SIM in, the modem is examined read-only first; switching the radio on is the only change made, and nothing that calls, messages or uses data happens without the author's word.
decision: With the SIM in, the modem is examined read-only first; switching the radio on is the only change made, and nothing that calls, messages or uses data happens without the author's word.
rejected: Trying a call or a data connection straight away.
why: A SIM card costs money and reaches people; the phone's state stays known.

brief: The capture failure is not chased in runtime power management.
decision: The capture failure is not chased in runtime power management.
rejected: Changing the macros' autosuspend or the controller's clock-stop handling.
why: With the bus controllers, macros, codec and SoundWire devices all forced awake, the read failure came at the same moment, the same way.

brief: The right channel is the bottom speaker.
decision: The right channel is the bottom speaker.
rejected: An earlier 2 dB lean, taken while the microphone was not yet placed.
why: With the microphone at the bottom speaker the right channel read 7 dB louder (-20.4 against -27.6 dBFS; room -85.7).

brief: Where the community's report and our measurement disagree, both are shown side by side; where we know nothing, the report is shown outlined, dated, as reported.
decision: Where the community's report and our measurement disagree, both are shown side by side; where we know nothing, the report is shown outlined, dated, as reported.
rejected: Hiding a report behind our measurement; filling unknowns as if measured.
why: A disagreement is the most telling part of the comparison - the sensors one may be of our own making.

brief: Telephony is checked in three modes: automatic now (registration; a small download over mobile data), half-manual (the phone calls the author's other phone, the author confirms through the inbox), ...
decision: Telephony is checked in three modes: automatic now (registration; a small download over mobile data), half-manual (the phone calls the author's other phone, the author confirms through the inbox), and fully automatic later (a two-phone stand, or a number that answers with a tone). The number to call lives in a private file on the lab machine, never in a repository.
rejected: Calls by hand without a check; keeping the number in the device manifest.
why: The author allowed data and calls to his other phone, and asked that the checks become part of the test suite so a stand can run them unattended.

brief: sleep-adsp-awake is not the blocker of CX/AOSS/DDR sleep: the weakest link moves to the Apps side (sleep-cluster-params first)
decision: No more LPASS or DSP-vote code for deep sleep now. The audio DSP's own qcom_stats counter stays a separate, smaller question (not known yet whether its firmware counts). The next try is the prepared cluster-parameters dtb (sleep-cluster-params) judged on a cycle, now possible because the wake is solved; after that the sleep set / the UARTs' CX votes.
rejected: Stopping the remoteproc for good (sound and calls need it); more macro-clock work (no effect measured twice); treating adsp count 0 as the cause (the counter may simply not be filled by this firmware: not known yet); a third DSP try (the logs show the DSP is not the cause).
why: A cycle with the audio DSP stopped, and one with adsp, cdsp and modem all stopped, still counted cxsd 0, aosd 0, ddr 0; the PSCI cluster state S2 was entered in the cycle.

brief: surya's cluster sleep parameters are not what blocks CX/AOSS/DDR sleep: the cluster enters 0x4100c244 and cxsd/aosd/ddr still read 0; the cause is unknown
decision: sleep-cluster-params waits on a deeper decision; no more cycles on this dtb until a candidate (SH0 owner, qcom_aoss knobs, XO/VRM, USB, display RSC) is chosen
rejected: More cycles on the same dtb: they repeat the same zeros
why: 8 cycles with ftrace: cluster S2 used, CX/MX 0, sleep set clean except SH0 x=1 y=3, counters 0

brief: Deep sleep on surya is made on mainline s2idle and taken to the SoC's floor step by step, each step measured by the SoC's own sleep counters (qcom_stats: CX collapse, AOSS sleep) across a real susp...
decision: Deep sleep on surya is made on mainline s2idle and taken to the SoC's floor step by step, each step measured by the SoC's own sleep counters (qcom_stats: CX collapse, AOSS sleep) across a real suspend: first a measured sleep on today's kernel, then the cluster sleep parameters from surya's own firmware tables, then whatever holds the audio DSP awake, then the FastRPC helpers stopped across suspend so the sensors come back; waking for calls and messages follows on that floor, by the modem's IPCRTR wakeup with ModemManager's quick suspend/resume, as postmarketOS does on the OnePlus 6. The check soc-sleeps says it after every boot: unknown until the phone has slept, broken if it slept and the SoC stayed up, works once the SoC reached its floor.
rejected: Waking for calls first on today's kernel (postmarketOS's OnePlus 6 recipe as it is): no SIM card in the lab to prove it, it says nothing of whether the SoC sleeps - a phone that rings but drains in a day is not deep sleep - and it is still reported broken on OnePlus 6/6T and Pixel 3a; it is the last step here, not the first. Android's kernel through Halium (Ubuntu Touch runs on surya): deep sleep works there, but on the vendor's 4.14 kernel and Android's blobs, with nothing upstream and the mainline conveyor abandoned; kept only as observed behaviour - its standby current is the number to match. Runtime idle without suspend (the screen off, userspace running, the SoC left to reach CX collapse in idle): nobody has reached the floor that way on Qualcomm mainline, userspace timers keep waking the CPUs, and it needs every vote released that s2idle needs; the counters measure runtime idle too, so nothing of it is lost. A power manager of our own, as Crust on the PinePhone: Qualcomm's always-on subsystem runs signed firmware and the modem is inside the SoC with no ring line, so it cannot be done. Guessing at the cluster parameters or the audio DSP without a measured sleep first: a change could not be told to help without the counters across a suspend.
why: Every step is small, falls back by itself (one sleep woken by the clock; a test kernel tried once) and is settled by a number the SoC counts itself, so progress is certain rather than claimed - nobody has published a measured floor for SM7150 on mainline, and the postmarketOS page that calls suspend working has no measurement behind it. The first step settles the biggest unknown: whether this SoC reaches its floor at all on mainline, before effort goes into waking it. Two causes are already in sight and both are cheap to try: the device tree asks the firmware for SC7180's cluster parameters (0x41001244, 0x4100b244) where surya's own tables have 0x41002244 and 0x4100c244, and the deepest was never entered once; and the audio DSP has never slept this boot. What it changes - a device tree fix, a vote released, a hook - goes upstream to the SM7150 series, pmaports and ModemManager, for every SM7150 phone. Reckoned: the measured sleep 2-3 agent-hours with its devlab verb; the cluster parameters 2; the audio DSP 4-8; the helpers 2-4; waking for calls 6 and a SIM card.

brief: A suspend try's way back is the SoC watchdog kept armed through sleep (patched qcom_wdt), the RTC set first, and ramoops read back after; proven by a dry run that suspends nothing
decision: Before any further suspend: (1) set the RTC (hwclock -w -u); (2) load a qcom_wdt built from the kernel's own source with one change, keep_armed_in_suspend=1, so an armed watchdog is NOT stopped in late suspend; (3) arm it with a timeout longer than the sleep (sleep + 30 s at least) by BusyBox watchdog and kill that process hard, so nobody pets it: it bites if the phone does not come back, and a stuck phone resets itself, boots the stock kernel and is reachable again; the script stops it by the magic close the moment rtcwake returns; (4) the log: a marker to /dev/kmsg before the fuse and the ramoops console (read from /sys/fs/pstore by sleep/way-back.sh collect) show what the last seconds were. Done as sleep/way-back.sh (verbs check, rtc, load, fuse, defuse, collect, cycle; no verb prints usage; cycle refuses unless the way back is in place) and sleep/build-wdt.sh. The way back is proven by 'fuse' on the idle phone (nothing suspends) before the one measured cycle; if the phone does not come back from that by itself, no suspend is tried and the author is told.
rejected: Stock watchdog alone: stopped in late suspend, covers only a hang before it. A timed reboot (rtcwake -m off/disk or a systemd timer): needs the RTC alarm or timers to fire out of the very state being tested, and a power-off wake is the bootloader's business on this phone. Keeping USB awake (devlab-usb-awake): it does not return a phone whose CPUs are stuck in s2idle, and the first hang showed no USB at all. Only a log that survives (pstore): it shows what happened but gives no way back, the author would still hold the power key. A rebuilt kernel with the patch built in: a long build and a boot-counted try for what a module loaded at run time does; kept as the upstream form (the parameter is a small patch for mainline) once the cycle is measured. Serial console: no serial pins open on surya.
why: The first timed s2idle hung with no log and no USB return and needed the author's hands. The stock watchdog is stopped by the driver in late suspend, so it could not have rescued that hang (it ends only a hang before the late phase); the patched module is the only way found that needs no kernel rebuild, no reboot to test and no hands, and a reboot or rmmod undoes it. A bite is a hardware reset and does not depend on USB, the RTC alarm or a CPU that is alive.

brief: Floor: read the suspend entry (RSC flush, last-CPU state, interrupt rate) before any more subtraction; SH0 owner-hunt paused
decision: Read the entry before subtracting anything more. Two phone items, both read-only on the kernel (tracefs, procfs, debugfs; one 15 s cycle via way-back.sh cycle 15 bt-on with the watchdog armed): (1) floor-entry-trace: the rpmh sleep-set writes of the last CPU, the last CPU's idle state, per-CPU cpuidle and cluster genpd deltas, the interrupt delta, wakeup_sources, and every qcom_stats node before and after; (2) floor-irq-quiet: if the interrupts are not quiet, name the top sources and silence them one at a time (the pattern that fixed the same symptom on the Odin 2). Counters are treated as valid; SH0 is treated as one unexplained entry, not the blocker, and its owner-hunt (floor-sh0-owner, floor-sh0-qup-tags) pauses until the trace says whether the flush is what the AOP sees. A build item makes the interrupt check a suite test. Standby current stays the arbiter of last resort for counter validity.
rejected: More owner-hunting for SH0 by tag or by unbinding drivers (three tries, no effect, and a BT-blocked cycle resets the phone); the debug late-suspend kernel first (a build, when tracefs gives the same facts without one); calling the counters broken (their names and ddr rows read fine); porting downstream lpm-levels or smp2p sleepstate (already rejected, no new evidence); the rpmh timeout debug series with cmd_db name lookup (unmerged, useful later to name holders once something is held); dwc3 skip-phy-init quirk (host-mode PHY refcount on the Odin 2; surya is a gadget and the UDC-unbound cycle changed nothing).
why: The counter files exist because their names were read from the RAM, ddr_stats passed its key and moves; the awake icc read that pointed at SH0 is not the state at the flush (USB's 240000 is dropped by dwc3_qcom_suspend, the large peaks are tag 3); and every subtraction so far (DSPs, WLAN, USB, uart8) changed nothing while the three facts that decide whether the SoC can sleep at all - flush, last-CPU state, wake rate - were never read. The closest measured sibling (Odin 2) was held by an IRQ storm through a suspend that reported success. Reading is cheaper and safer than another one-shot dtb.

brief: Way to the floor: subtract holders one at a time, DSPs-never-started and a clock/cmdline read first; not more cluster or DSP code, not S2RAM
decision: Chosen vector: measured subtraction on the existing s2idle, ranked by evidence. Order: (1) floor-read-holders (read only: cmdline, clk, regulator, icc, genpd, cpuidle); (2) floor-dsps-never-started (module_blacklist=qcom_q6v5_pas); (3) floor-no-ignore-unused if the cmdline has it; then one subtraction per cycle: WLAN, UDC, the SH0 owner, aoss knobs; a late-suspend dump kernel only if still open. Each is one change judged by way-back.sh cycle 15 bt-on and the soc-sleeps check (the failing test: it fails after a suspend with cxsd and aosd 0, and passes only at the floor). health-soc-sleeps-ddr widens the check to ddr and the rung. The decisions adsp-is-not-the-floor and cluster-params-are-not-the-floor stand for what they measured, but adsp-is-not-the-floor rested on stopped DSPs, not never-started ones; floor-dsps-never-started settles that.
rejected: Another cluster-state value (state taken equals downstream/sm8150; 8 cycles repeat zeros); PSCI SYSTEM_SUSPEND / s2ram (firmware does not offer it, kernel series NACKed); smp2p sleepstate port (not in mainline for this SoC, weakest evidence, large work); more LPASS macro clock work (no effect twice); treating the counters as broken before standby current says so (kept as hypothesis 6 / sleep-standby-current); a downstream-style lpm-levels port (the flush mainline does matches).
why: Others reach the floor on mainline s2idle only by removing holders one by one (X1E, QCS8550) or fail on named clock votes (sm8250); surya's cluster state equals downstream's and apps_rsc equals sc7180's, so no system mode is missing. The counters are valid but name no client on this layout, so subtraction is the only instrument; the biggest unknowns (kernel cmdline, clk holders, latched DSP votes) are read-only or one cmdline away.

brief: surya's microphones are made to work as the analog mics they are: AMIC1 (bottom) and AMIC3 (top) on the WCD9375's ADC1 and ADC2 (ADC2 MUX at INP3), over the TX SoundWire bus (capture on <&swr2 1>, ...
decision: surya's microphones are made to work as the analog mics they are: AMIC1 (bottom) and AMIC3 (top) on the WCD9375's ADC1 and ADC2 (ADC2 MUX at INP3), over the TX SoundWire bus (capture on <&swr2 1>, ADC2 on its own master port 3 by qcom,tx-port-mapping <2 3 4 5>), the TX macro's decimators and the DSP's TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3 - the path pulpoff/linux-surya and sm7150-mainline PR 60 use, and the one bring-up proved on 2026-11-17 (run 20261117-044744: mic-hears-speaker and mic-top-hears-speaker pass on the kept kernel 7.1.0-sm7150-mic+). What is left, in order: capture through the sound server by a UCM profile (mic-ucm-capture, first: the biggest unknown left for anyone using the phone, since every check so far sets the mixer by hand), the microphones held across boots and out of the known gaps (mic-held), the fixes upstream by joining PR 60 (mic-upstream), the DMIC experiment kept out (mic-dmic-dropped), and the call uplink with the calls feature (calls-audio-q6voice).
rejected: DMICs through the TX decimators with the VA block's clocks (the vendor's va-without-decimation model, bring-up's lead until 05:00 on 2026-11-17): surya has no digital mics - the routes are the QRD board's and the pins are unconnected; the model stays recorded (bolero-v1-capture-family) for siblings that have DMICs. The VA macro's own path (VA_CODEC_DMA_TX_0): this ADSP rejects the port (0xb021, error 3), nobody streams it on SM6150/SM7150, and there is nothing for it to record. pulpoff/linux-surya as surya's kernel: it works, but it is 7.2.15 (end of life), squashed into one commit and packaged for Debian, while the conveyor builds tested branches of linux-phone-oco/linux toward sm7150-mainline - we take its findings with credit, not its tree. Driving LPASS codec DMA from Linux without the ADSP (lpass-cpu, as ADSP-less Chromebooks do): unnecessary and a large, risky driver. A surya capture series of our own for upstream: davinci's PR 60 already carries three of the four fixes; a parallel series would split the review.
why: Measured, not inferred: both built-in mics hear a quiet tone 45-67 dB above their noise on this phone. An independent mainline tree on the same phone records both mics and carries calls this way and names the DMIC pins unconnected; the DMIC reading came from Qualcomm's reference board. What is left is configuration and carrying it upstream, each step proven by a check on the phone; no reverse engineering is needed. Research: microphones-are-analog, mic-zeros-meant-no-input, bolero-v1-capture-family (microphones-are-analog and bolero-v1-capture-family stay in linux-phone-oco/docs).

brief: r3: Bluetooth stays on; the loop aborts itself 'aborted, partial' on a Bluetooth failure or 4 non-sleeping cycles; irq 157 quieting queued after
decision: Coordinator's choice (a) taken (supersedes 2026-11-17-r3-waits-on-the-bluetooth-choice). The abort is on 4 zero-sleep cycles in a row, not 2: 24 of r2's 47 cycles slept 0 s with Bluetooth healthy, so 2 would abort on noise. The abort writes STOPPED 'aborted, partial'; samples before it with charger_online 0 still count. No cycle starts after a Bluetooth failure, so the 30 s fuse cannot meet the retry loop; only the first stalled cycle can still reset the phone. (c) is backlog sleep-irq157-quiet, after r3.
rejected: 2 zero-sleep cycles (noise); BT blocked (hung hard).
why: Same evidence as the research; the zero-sleep rate is r2's cycles.log.

brief: r3 runs with Bluetooth on but ends itself, unscored, before any cycle after a Bluetooth failure or 4 non-sleeping cycles
decision: Option (a) of 2026-11-17-r3-waits-on-the-bluetooth-choice, taken on the coordinator's order to make r3 safe: standby-run.sh counts hci hardware error / irq 157 nobody cared / freeze refused in dmesg and, once the count rises, or after 4 cycles in a row that slept 0 s, writes STOPPED and ends without another cycle (no fuse can fire then); a run without DONE and a full measure phase is never scored. r1 marked INVALID, r2 UNSCORED on the phone. The first cycle that stalls can still reset the phone; then the run is unscored and the boot journal says so.
rejected: (b) BT blocked: hung hard before. (c) quieting irq 157 first: a driver/dt change no research decided.
why: Bluetooth blocked hangs the phone hard (research 2026-11-17-surya-s2idle-bt-blocked-hang) and irq 157 quieting is untried; (a) changes only the run and keeps the phone as stock.

brief: r3 does not start until the lane coordinator picks how the run treats Bluetooth; r2's samples are not scored
decision: r2 is closed unscored. r3 (a run that needs the author to unplug again) is not armed yet: the run must survive Bluetooth's failure, and that has three ways, a turning point sent to the surya coordinator: (a) bt-on as now, but the loop stops itself and writes BAD when a cycle sleeps 0 s twice in a row or hci0 reports a hardware error, so it ends with an honest 'not measured' instead of a reset; (b) Bluetooth rfkill-blocked for the run (it hung the phone hard in cycle 15 with BT blocked, research 2026-11-17-surya-s2idle-bt-blocked-hang, so only with the watchdog fuse and the UART wake irq handled); (c) the QCA UART irq 157 quieted first (research 2026-11-17-qca-uart-wake-across-suspend: the serial's power/wakeup switch).
rejected: Re-arm r3 unchanged: the same stall resets it again and costs the author's hands. A longer fuse: the qcom watchdog counts 32 s at most.
why: The cause is in the run's own design, not the phone: a stalled cycle past the 30 s fuse resets it, so any r3 on the same script meets the same end once BT fails, and each try costs the author an unplugging.

brief: The sensors on surya come through the stack postmarketOS already ships - hexagonrpcd's sensors helper, libssc and iio-sensor-proxy - with the firmware's own pre-parsed registry kept current so the ...
decision: The sensors on surya come through the stack postmarketOS already ships - hexagonrpcd's sensors helper, libssc and iio-sensor-proxy - with the firmware's own pre-parsed registry kept current so the audio DSP never needs to write it: the 46 sensor configs given Android's fixed mtime (1230768000) so they match the registry's record, sensorspd alone unmasked (rootpd stays masked). First a bounded probe on the kept kernel; then it made lasting in the device manifest and offered upstream (firmware-xiaomi-surya, pmaports, a word on hexagonrpc #19/#29); then the helper across suspend, tied to deep sleep's sleep-fastrpc-helpers; then proximity blanking the screen in a call. If the probe still sees the DSP write, the fallback is write support in hexagonrpcd (sensors-registry-writes). Proven by the suite: motion-and-light and proximity-reads, with no-processor-crashes and the microphone and call checks unchanged in the same boot.
rejected: Write support in hexagonrpcd first (#27, a -S state dir, the 700-line #29 patch): days, our own build of a daemon upstream has not decided on, and on X1E it stopped the crash yet found no sensors; kept as the fallback, not the first step. Serving the phone's real persist registry (!8203, the 2026-11-09 real trial): without the marker served it changed nothing here, and serving it needs the same hexagonrpcd change; closed upstream. Linux drivers for the chips on the sensor core's buses: the DSP owns those buses and would fight for them (X1E), stk3a5x has no mainline driver, and it costs power. Android's sensor stack through Halium: the vendor's 4.14 kernel, nothing upstream, the mainline work abandoned. Leaving the sensors masked and faking proximity with the touchscreen: no light, no rotation, no real proximity - the author ranked the sensor hub second.
why: The crash is explained by two conditions the trials of 2026-11-09 never met together - every config looks changed to the DSP (real mtimes against the registry's 1230768000) and the version marker is unreachable - and the first of them is settled with no code: a touch of 46 files and one service unmasked, undone by masking it again. The registry already holds the light and proximity sensor, so neither writes nor the panel property are needed if nothing is re-parsed. It disturbs the DSP that carries the microphones and calls only for the length of a probe whose fallback is the mask that holds today, and every step is proven by the same boot's audio checks. What it yields - configs at the vendor mtime - is a packaging fix every SM7150 phone with these firmware packages can take (davinci's loop looks the same), where write support is days of work on a daemon whose maintainers have not settled where writes go. Reckoned: the probe 1-2 agent-hours; lasting 1-2; across suspend 2-4; proximity in calls 3-6; the fallback, if needed, 8-16. Research: sensors-registry-rebuild, sensors-hardware-surya, sensors-family-state, sensors-across-suspend.

brief: Bluetooth stays up through suspend with the serial's power/wakeup off for the cycle; blocking, unbinding and a device-tree change rejected
decision: way-back.sh cycle SLEEP bt-on: unblock Bluetooth, write 'disabled' to /sys/bus/platform/devices/88c000.serial/power/wakeup before suspend, put the old value back after. Bluetooth cannot wake the phone for now (wanted later only for paired devices, with the sleep-wakes-for-calls work).
rejected: rfkill block bluetooth before suspend (the earlier way: the phone hung at suspend entry once, and Bluetooth is wanted up); unbinding hci_uart/btqca before suspend (loses hci0, reloads firmware at every resume, and a failed rebind could leave the UART dead); deleting the second interrupt in the device tree (a dtb rebuild and a reboot for what one sysfs write does, and it removes the paired-device wake for good); persisting the off state in a udev rule now (not until the sleep path is proven)
why: The wake that ended s2idle was the serial's dedicated RX wake irq 158, armed because that device's wakeup is on; the sysfs switch is the mainline way, reversible, needs no module build or reboot, and keeps hci0 and its firmware loaded (resume needs no re-setup). Result: 3 cycles woke by the RTC alarm, Bluetooth up after.

brief: SH0 sleep vote: remove the console UART's (then the QUP) ALWAYS tags in a one-shot dtb; QMP is read-only first and off the path
decision: Chosen vector: subtract the SH0 sleep vote at its source, in the device tree. Step 1 (read only): at late suspend list which interconnect paths through qns_llcc/SH0 carry a SLEEP-bucket vote. Step 2: one-shot dtb with uart8's (debug UART) interconnect tags set ACTIVE_ONLY, console moved or the UART unbound, then cycle 15 bt-on: judged by the sleep-set flush (SH0 gone) and soc-sleeps. Step 3, only if SH0 stays: the other QUP/crypto TAG_ALWAYS nodes one at a time. If SH0 goes to zero and the counters still read 0, SH0 is cleared as a holder and the next suspects are hypotheses 2/3/6 (clocks, UFS/GDSCs, counter validity; sleep-standby-current). QMP no-ack: read-only discriminators, no change to the AOP path.
rejected: Fixing QMP first (the knobs only test hypothesis 5, unlikely; wiring equals sm8150, nothing points at the cause; kept as a read-only item). A late-suspend dump kernel first (a build and install for what one dtb answers; kept waiting). Zeroing SH0 by a driver patch or keepalive=false (it is by-design on all siblings and hides the consumer; the DT tag is the honest change and the one that could go upstream as a correction). Treating SH0 as a firmware latch (the sleep bucket is built only from consumer tags). Reading the Aspire 1 sleep set as proof SH0 is harmless (not measured by anyone).
why: SH0 is the keepalive BCM of LLCC on sdm845, sm8150, sc7180 and sm7150 alike (bcm-voter forces it only in AMC/WAKE), so the sleep-set x=1,y=3 is a consumer's TAG_ALWAYS vote through qns_llcc, visible and removable in the device tree; uart8 (debug UART, avg 1 peak 1 across suspend) is the recorded candidate. It is the only non-zero sleep entry and one dtb away, while the QMP no-ack has no cheap explanation and serves only a low-ranked hypothesis. Whether SH0 blocks aosd is not known yet; the test settles it by the counters.

brief: Standby current in a real s2idle cycle is the arbiter of deep sleep; the counters and the AOP's view are clues, regulators and wakeups are the hunt
decision: The floor is judged by battery-only average current across a suspended cycle (charge_counter delta over the time, screen off, modem on), the line to match being 9 mA until Android on surya is measured. Next phone steps in order, each read-only or one change per cycle: (1) read every power-domain idle_states row and regulator_summary users before and after one cycle; (2) allow USB runtime PM (power/control auto on the PHY and controller) and read again; (3) the standby-current cycle itself. The AOP view is not chased further: the flush is sound and has no Linux-side reader.
rejected: Reading the AOP's log or message RAM beyond the stats (no mainline reader; downstream-only); more tracing of the flush (done: floor-entry-trace); S2RAM (rejected by floor-research-path); measuring Android by flashing surya now (changes the phone, not research's, and the miatoll figure gives a line meanwhile); treating aosd/cxsd counts as the only pass (peers show they can stay 0 while the draw is dominated by rails)
why: The entry is in order (flush, deepest cluster state, quiet IRQs). The closest peer (pmaports#4846) shows counters can read poorly while holders are fixed one by one with no current change, and that regulators and USB, not the AOP, were what moved the draw; a measured 9 mA Droidian figure on the same generation gives a line. Only current is independent of the doubts about the counters.

brief: Standby drain becomes the test standby-current: median of 3 runs of >=60 min, scored from the charge counter, witness unplugs
decision: Entered as a test with a witness step (the author unplugs USB), threshold 15 mA, scored as mean current from the charge_counter delta over the window (current_now only a cross-check), at least 60 min measured after a 10 min settle, Wi-Fi on, Bluetooth on and off as separate runs, screen off, samples every 30-60 s, charging samples discarded, invalid runs kept as invalid. The one-off run now prepared is the first such run (Bluetooth on).
rejected: A single 10 minute measurement (counter too coarse); scoring by battery percentage (least trustworthy); a name 'suitcase test' as a standard (none exists); Android's number as a gate now (not known yet).
why: Made repeatable so every kernel change is scored the same way; the charge counter avoids the wake-sample bias; see research standby-drain-as-a-repeatable-test.

brief: A test kernel that proves a part is built from pushed branches of linux-phone-oco/linux (a test branch merging the fix branches), never from a hand-edited tree. Hand-edited trees stay for one-off e...
decision: A test kernel that proves a part is built from pushed branches of linux-phone-oco/linux (a test branch merging the fix branches), never from a hand-edited tree. Hand-edited trees stay for one-off experiments (switches, traces), their changes kept as patches in surya-audio/patches; a finding becomes a commit before it is called proven.
rejected: Keeping the working tree that proved something as the reference: nothing reads it, it drifts from the branches, and what is sent upstream is not what was tested.
why: On 2026-11-17 the WCD device tree on feat/surya-wcd937x-mic-headphone turned out never to have been the tree proven on the phone - wrong SoundWire controller addresses, a vote the DSP rejects, the reset's polarity - because the proven tree in surya-audio/kernel-rc3/src-wcd was edited by hand and never committed. The branch kernel built from PRs 3-5 then booted healthy with the codec.

brief: surya-lab gives up its own conveyor scripts, devlab now doing their work for any phone: lib/phone.sh (devlab phone: the same script-on-stdin way, the USB address then the learned Wi-Fi one, now fro...
decision: surya-lab gives up its own conveyor scripts, devlab now doing their work for any phone: lib/phone.sh (devlab phone: the same script-on-stdin way, the USB address then the learned Wi-Fi one, now from device.toml, and held for each change), tests/run.sh with tests/automatic/checks.sh (the phone runs its own suite after every boot: lab-tools health/suite and tests/health here), tests/to-docs.sh (devlab gather, through tad - the Python dc.py it called is gone), flash/flash-dtb.sh (pointed at a flash.sh already gone; devlab flash --dtb). ui/switch.sh now reaches the phone through devlab.
rejected: Keeping the scripts as a fallback (a second way nobody runs drifts, as flash-dtb.sh had); moving them into the template (devlab already does each, for any phone).
why: One way to reach and test a phone, held and measured, instead of two that drift (device-template dt-surya-from-template). The reasons each script carried were read first: the full kernel log from the journal and BusyBox-safe awk live on in lab-tools health/suite/lib.sh; the checks not yet carried are on lab-tools backlog health-carry-old-checks.

brief: The macro hw-vote release stays out of the kept kernel: it did not move adsp, so it is a candidate patch, not a fix
decision: Keep the patch as research material only; the kept kernel and the dts stay as they are. Next measure the DSP side (what the ADSP firmware waits for: sensors PD, call audio, a vote from another subsystem) before touching more LPASS code.
rejected: Landing it into the kept kernel as a fix: no measured effect and not yet explained why clk_summary still shows count 3. Switching rx/tx to the full PM clock framework conversion now: bigger change, same unproven effect.
why: Measured on the phone: cycle 15 bt-on on the try kernel gave adsp 0, cxsd 0, aosd 0 as on the kept one; sound checks still pass (35/0).

decision: What has run is observed by this observatory alone: the lab asks it to observe what has run every quarter hour, and its voice says what newly comes into view here - urgently where the lens of signs says so. A part observed writes only its own tables. ocoeco is taken from its release, checked against its sums, in seconds where building it took minutes.
rejected: The lab observing and pushing what it saw here (one more writer of this record); this observatory observing every quarter hour on its own schedule (GitHub's schedule is seldom kept that often); keeping both and quieting one voice by a rule.
why: Sign runs-are-observed-twice (open-commons-observatory/ocoeco): the lab observed what had run on its own every quarter hour, beside this observatory, because this observatory observed only every six hours and on landings - too seldom to hear in time that something broke. Looked at first: the observation that is the place's own is this one - its record keeps what it saw, and its page is made from it; the lab's was there for timing only. Tried before: observing a part rewrote what the whole had found (decision 2026-11-14-a-part-observed-speaks-for-itself in ocoeco).

decision: Every line of what followed leads somewhere: the site lays out a page for each thing the author said that work followed - offered by the conversation's place, and placed here - and a page for each record of work of the last three days and each thing such a record entered or changed, beside the pages for places, signs, angles of the form and decisions a sign came to. A page of a thing says the thing in full, and what is around it.
rejected: A page for every thing in view (ten thousand of them, laid out anew at each observing, to say what nobody steps to); pages only for what the latest turn touched (the turn before it would lead nowhere the moment the author speaks again).
why: Opened on what followed, the front showed lines one could read and not step on: a decision, a reflection, a record of work had no page, and the line about it was only text - a dead surface in small. What a look shows is where one goes on from.

decision: The page this observatory shows first opens on what followed the latest thing the author said - the lens the conversation's place brings, placed before the sheet: his words, and what was done, seen, learned, entered and released since. Then the sheet, the perfect form, and every other lens.
rejected: A page of its own, linked from the front (what he looks for first would be a step away, and the front would open on what he did not ask); placing it after the sheet (the sheet says what waits - mostly on him - and changes little from one thing he says to the next; what followed is new each time).
why: What the author looks for first when he comes back is what came of what he last said - and until now he read it as text the agent wrote in a chat. On his own page it is read off the records of work, each line about a thing one can step to, and it is there whether or not anyone wrote it.

decision: ocoeco is taken from its newest release that has its files. A release is made first and its files are built after it: for those minutes the newest release has nothing to take, and the one before it serves.
rejected: Building ocoeco from its source here (minutes, where taking it is seconds); waiting in this workflow until the files are there (a wait of unknown length, for something the release before already gives); leaving it (a run failing on main is a sign on the sheet, and this one would be about nothing in this place).
why: On 2026-11-15 a run failed on main: asked to observe a minute after ocoeco 0.49.0 was released, it found no files to download. Five releases were made that day, each opening such a gap of a few minutes, and the lab asks this observatory to observe every quarter hour.

decision: The pages are laid out and published where the whole was observed - four times a day, and whenever an observing is asked for. An observing of one part only - what has run, asked for by the lab every quarter hour - keeps what it observed and leaves the pages as they are.
rejected: Fewer pages (that every line leads somewhere is what the pages are for); leaving it (an observing asked for after a change waits behind the quarter hours, and the same pages are laid out ninety-six times a day to say what changed four times).
why: With a page for each thing the author said, each record of work of late and each thing it touched, the site is over a thousand pages and takes six minutes to lay out. Laid out anew at every quarter hour, the observatory was laying out pages most of the time, each observing waiting on the one before: on 2026-11-15 a job that waited for none to be under way waited a quarter of an hour. What the quarter hour is for is that the lab's sheet sees what has run - and that is in what is kept, not on the page.

decision: The lens behind the sheet keeps a line by what it is about, not by its words: it reads the plane, and the shape the language names for what holds work back, and keeps the lines about a thing the author holds back. The sheet may word its lines as it will.
rejected: Asking the sheet to word its lines for this lens (the lens in front would have to know what stands behind it); a second query of what holds work back, written here (the language names that shape once: this reads it).
why: Kept by its words, the lens would go blind the day the sheet said the same thing otherwise. A plane says, for each line, the thing it is about; what that thing waits on is in the graph, and the language already names the shape that reads it. So a lens behind a lens reuses what is there twice over: what the lens in front shows, and what the language knows of it.

decision: The page of the author's observatory reads the language as its place keeps it: ocoeco's place, held with the rest while observing, is where the language is read from when the page is laid out - not only the language the release carries. What was changed in the language from the window is on the page at its next laying out, with no release waited for.
rejected: A release made for each change to the language from the window (minutes of building for a few words); the program built from main for each laying out, as the first observatory does (minutes, where taking the release takes seconds).
why: The page is laid out with the newest released program, and the language came with it: a lens changed from the window lands as words, which make no release, so the page showed the language as it was at the last release of a change to the program.

decision: What waits on the author is read off the sheet by a lens behind it: waiting-on-the-author places still-showing, seen through held-back-by-the-author - a lens that reads a plane and keeps only the lines held back by him. Nothing of the sheet is changed, and nothing is asked of the data twice: the new lens adds only the difference. It is looked through by its name; where it is placed - on the front, or said aloud - is the author's to say.
rejected: A second sheet asking the same of the data (two sayings of one thing, which drift apart); the lines picked out in the sheet's own query (the sheet would have to know who looks at it); placing it on the front page unasked (the front shows the whole sheet already).
why: The author, 2026-11-16: something different from a lens is made by adding a lens that includes it, more lenses on its plane to add, and a lens behind it to leave out what is not wanted - all of it in the new lens, and in the structure. This is the first lens made so, in his own observatory, about what only he can move: what waits on his word.

decision: Every Rust tool in the commons declares its invocation surface - arguments and environment - with argenv, the commons' own crate: ocoeco, tad, the engine, devlab and tone move from clap, one at a time, proven equal (the same commands and environment behaviour).
rejected: Keeping clap (a second way to declare a surface, and environment read by hand).
why: The author asked whether all our tools use argenv; only lab-agent and snapall did. clap was chosen by default without looking inside the commons first; argenv gives one declared, typed, machine-readable contract for argv and env, readable by agents and by ocoeco.

decision: There is not one observatory. OCO is the ecosystem - the agreement (ocoeco) and its tools - that lets anyone have one. A constellation has its own fulldome; an observatory is someone's place where the fulldomes they care about come together, and observatories can be brought together, one gathering others. Observer and observatory named one thing: observatory is kept. The author's observatory - where his own constellations come together - is one of many, to be parted from OCO the ecosystem, with which it is mixed today in one organization. Refined the same day by 2026-11-12-places-lenses-acts: observer is kept after all, as the part of ocoeco that observes - an act, not a place.
rejected: One observatory for everyone (a centre the commons would then depend on); a special home of observers above observatories (an observatory gathering others is enough); two words, observer and observatory, for one thing; parting the author's observatory from the ecosystem at once (a careful move, later).
why: The author, 2026-11-12: the point of OCO is that it is not one observatory; anyone will be able to create theirs, and all or some can be brought together to share their views of the sky; OCO as a project had got mixed with his own projects. An observatory that can gather others needs no special home above it - the same thing, nested, as Ostrom found lasting commons to be.

decision: oco- before a name marks a star of OCO itself (oco-agent). -oco after a name marks a place someone made with OCO - a constellation or an observatory alike (linux-phone-oco, marshall-oco). The name says made with OCO; the mark says what kind of place it is.
rejected: A different ending for constellations and for observatories (the mark already says the kind, and a name that says it twice can say it wrongly).
why: The author, 2026-11-12: OCO's stars are named with oco preceding; the observatories others make with OCO end in -oco; the author's own observatory has its organization, marshall-oco.

decision: OCO is three kinds of things. Places, where data lives (git repositories today): a star produces; a constellation is a family of stars that belong together, gathering their data and keeping what holds between them; an observatory is someone's looking, gathering what they care to see. Ways of seeing: a lens - the data it needs, where it comes from, how it is shown - made once and used by anyone; and the fulldome, the outermost lens, the same for every place over whatever it holds. Acts of ocoeco: record (a star producing its data where things are fresh), observe (the observer: gathering from other places, the same at every scale) and show (running lenses). The observer brings data and the names of lenses; since a lens shows the same data the same way anywhere, taking a ready render is a shortcut, not a principle.
rejected: Star and observatory alone (belonging and looking are different claims: one about the stars, one about the looker); the fulldome as one lens beside the others (it would no longer be the whole); the fulldome as something other than a lens (a second mechanism); observer as a second word for observatory (2026-11-12-many-observatories is refined: it is an act of ocoeco, not a place); a lens that must bring its own instruments (a plugin system); observatories gathering only renders (a view of the whole needs the data).
why: The author, 2026-11-12: star, constellation and observatory come from the need for places; without the constellation the relations between projects have nowhere to live; the fulldome is the board taken to its full potential, realized in ocoeco's structure and lenses; a lens, once done, just works for anyone in ocoeco; the observer finds its place in ocoeco as what allows the gathering of gatherings. Sorting the words by kind shows the same shape at every scale (the-same-at-every-scale).

decision: The whole is called the fulldome, not the room, and it has no walls: a part of it is a lens, and what is connected - a decision, its research, the work it caused, the result - is seen as connected. The fulldome shows the story (why a star exists, what it must reach, how, what is happening), time (the sky on any date: the data's own history) and intent, and it is touched and acted in, not watched. What a lens and a render are is not a protocol beside ocoeco: it is ocoeco - the shared language and the mark grow to say them, and ocoeco's tools read, check and write them, so a star follows the agreement by using ocoeco, not by remembering it.
rejected: Room and wall (2026-11-12-the-room keeps its substance; its words are replaced); a render agreement as a protocol of its own (rules to read and remember: the thing ocoeco exists to make unnecessary); a fulldome one only watches (a planetarium's audience: the open commons' must invite).
why: The author, 2026-11-12: room and wall do not fit the whole; a planetarium's dome shows not only constellations but the story behind them, relations, a history, intent; and ocoeco is the agreement and a convenient way to follow it automatically - not principles on paper, a ritual, or a discipline in someone's head. Fulldome belongs with star, constellation, lens, observer and observatory; a dome is one continuous sky, where walls divide.

decision: A board is the room, not a list: the open commons' obeya, where anyone sees the whole. ocoeco's entities are its walls, and a wall is a lens. OCO is described by four words: a star (one idea or project keeping its own ocoeco data), a constellation (stars seen together), a lens (queries and how they are shown, over the same data), an observer (gathers renders, renders nothing of others again); OCO is the home of observers. The flow of work built as ocoeco board is one lens of the room, not the room. A view across stars is a lens of their constellation, rendered once there from the stars' data, so observers still only gather renders; and a render carries a small agreement - its lens, its format, where it starts - so an observer can place it. Lenses declared as data replace three things planned apart: the renderer leaving tad, presentation as data, and the observatory engine's hand-written views. Its words are replaced the same day by 2026-11-12-the-fulldome: the whole is the fulldome, and a part of it is a lens, not a wall.
rejected: The board as a view over the backlog alone (one wall taken for the room: 2026-11-12-the-board is refined by this); a board entity of its own; observers rendering stars' data themselves (a star owns how it is shown, and no star may need an observer to be seen); a framework's ceremonies and score boards; adding words that name no distinct part of the whole.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: ocoeco is the next step, for open commons, of the room where everyone sees the whole - as a principle, a system and an implementation - learnt by seeing and touching, not by cramming; too much had been centred on the backlog; and words are added only where they reflect the whole and make it simpler. The research (the-room) shows the walls are already here, and that the author's four words and the room are one design.

decision: What argenv declares and what a lens declares are one nature, cut in two: a command line is an entry. Laid side by side from the files: an input's key, type, allowed values and whether it is required are a field's name, type, enum and required; a command with the inputs scoped to it is an entry with what it asks; the environment's door and a default are what the computer supplies; help is what can be entered; and a value known only when the program runs - the word asked, designed the day before - is a relation, of which sixteen are declared, answered by the rows that exist with no word and no function. So the step designed for argenv (asked as a field beside allowed, with a check that the two do not disagree) is not built. What is tried next is small: one act of ocoeco declared the way an entry is, read by argenv's own reader of what is typed - and what the trial shows decides the rest.
rejected: Building asked beside allowed, with its rule (an eighth writing of the one nature); a build step translating lens files into argenv's declarations (two forms of one thing, and a translator to carry); keeping a door open to another project's generators (complying held open, called patience); deciding the whole merge in advance (it is discovered by the trial).
why: The author, 2026-11-13: a rule is something imposed from outside without being derived from inside; what argenv does in nature - transparency, self-speaking, interactability - cannot be done without friction when a program is split into programs and files; its nature can be discovered in what ocoeco already has; the cuts of the whole are artificially imposed and can move. Looked at the same day: the design kept a rule after naming rules as the thing to avoid, and kept it to leave a published field as it was - the friction was in the cut, argenv as a sealed thing obeyed from outside. And the one nature is written in the commons as argenv's declaration, its reader, two generators of completions, a usage typed by hand, ocoeco's own reader of an entry's words (437 lines), its form (141 lines), and commands declared for the older library in five programs.

decision: What is being worked on, and what waits, are read off the work, not typed. A record of work says which item it advances: the items worked on lately, how often and by whom, are a fact. What waits is what something not yet done halts: a relation, which ends when that is done. What is left for a person to say is intent - this is next, this is done, this is set aside. Until the read-off states have earned trust they stand beside the typed ones, and where they disagree that is a sign.
rejected: A state set by remembering to set it (it drifts, as the rung did); removing the typed states at once (half the records of work name no item: the tie must hold first); a form to fill for each move (the work already says it).
why: The author, 2026-11-13. Looked at the same day: of 183 records of work since 11 November, 90 say what they advance; read off them, the items most worked on in two days were typed waiting (safety-first 23 times, lenses-as-data 16, constellations 8), and the one item typed in progress had no work done on it at all - the word recorded an intention. waits_on is a sentence, so waiting cannot end by itself; and one driver is recorded under three names, because who is typed too.

decision: The whole is continuous, and a program that starts, answers and dies is a moment of looking at it. Continuity is the flow's, never a program's: what is true is kept as data that goes on being written whether or not anything looks, and a window follows it - it may close and nothing is lost. A finger put into the flow is an entry. What is tried next is small: the lab's own record of what happens - oco-agent's journal, beats and what was said - becomes a place a lens can read, so that what is being done now is read off it.
rejected: A long-lived program that holds what is true (the incident); a new one written for this (the living part exists); cost as the reason (measured: a fifth of a second a look).
why: The author, 2026-11-13: ocoeco is treated like a command line - it starts, takes something in, gives something out and dies - while what we have built is continuous, and what changes is the interaction with it; running continuously it can treat its surroundings as part of the flow, and in progress becomes a continuous reflection of observed signals. Looked at the same day: the flow exists on the lab and is cut off from the lenses. oco-agent keeps three tables in the language a lens declares tables in; the journal's last row was the job reading it - claimed, not finished: being done now, to the second, typed by nobody. No lens reads it and nothing gathers it; what is being worked on is read off the records of the last three days, and the voice starts from nothing twelve times an hour to ask whether anything changed. One look takes a fifth of a second: the reason is not load, it is that a moment cannot notice. And held from 11 November: one long-lived program held everything, stopped, and all went silent - so the truth stays in the flow.

decision: OCO is a constellation in a place of its own - open-commons-observatory/ecosystem - gathering ocoeco, ocoeco-engine, tad and lab-agent (oco-agent). The author's observatory is in its own organization - marshall-oco/marshall-oco.github.io, published at marshall-oco.github.io - gathering his nine organizations, OCO among them as one constellation. Both were made by ocoeco init --gathers and observe only what they gather. The first observatory, in OCO's organization, is untouched and stays until the author's stands where it does.
rejected: The name open-commons-observatory/oco for OCO's place: it is the old name of the engine's repository and GitHub still redirects it - a new repository there would destroy the redirect, and any clone still pointing at it would talk to another repository unknowingly; that cannot be undone, where renaming ecosystem later keeps a redirect. Moving the first observatory at once (nothing public breaks on the way). The observatory's repository as OCO's place (it holds the first observatory's own records).
why: OCO is the ecosystem, not an observatory (2026-11-12-many-observatories); the author, 2026-11-13: my observatory tracks the OCO constellation itself. Until now the observatory's site, its harvest and its data lived in OCO's organization, so OCO looked like one person's observatory.

decision: What goes wrong is a sign that something does not fit the whole - stale, overlapping, lacking, unclear - not a thing to be countered. A sign says what in the whole it points at, and it ends when the whole is changed so that it cannot arise; what changed the whole is named as a link, not written as a remedy. A guard, a rule or a step added to carry is itself a sign. The lens of problems is to be reshaped to this, and no more is written as a countermeasure.
rejected: Problem and countermeasure as the shape of the record (it names an enemy and a remedy, and the remedy accumulates); a field of prose saying what was done about it (what changed the whole is a row to be pointed at); counting handled problems as a measure of health (it counts counters).
why: The author, 2026-11-13. Looked at the same day: of seventeen records written as problem and countermeasure since 12 November, about five changed the whole so the thing cannot arise (runs observed, never gathered; the pulse is the watcher; a place born able to record), and the rest added something to carry - main read back after landing, a practice to remember, pipefail, a wider search, two patches in turn on one guard. Read as signs they point at few things: that a change on the lab is not one act (three practices and every job's growing preamble); that what is observed is committed where work lands (the harvest's guard); that a word does not say what it is (readiness is a rung); that a link is typed where it should be chosen (the guard on writes). Countering the sign leaves the misfit, and the counter becomes one more part that can misfit.

decision: The way the conversation is read is kept where the conversation is: read-transcripts, in the place's tools. A transcript is read once; a turn is who spoke, when, and the words; a turn by the same speaker at the same moment as one already there is not added - the seam between two transcripts repeats the reply during which it was cut; a turn entered as it was said before its transcript was kept is joined, in order; each turn follows the one before. What it prints is added in the place, where the place's own check says whether anything to be kept out is showing.
rejected: A route said in the language (the transcripts are kept where an agent works, not where a place is held: a route reads where a place is held); reading them by hand each time (it left a repeat at every seam).
why: On 2026-11-15 two more transcripts were read - 68 turns, the author's of the thirteenth evening and the fourteenth as he wrote them. The way of reading them existed only as commands typed in a sandbox that is not kept. Read by hand, a reply was added that was there in two halves, and the reply at the seam twice; two earlier readings had left the same. Each was merged through the language: the turn after followed the first, and the repeat was taken back.

decision: Every change carries a record made by ocoeco (a changes table in the shared language), the commit message is rendered from it, and ocoeco release consumes the records to set the version, write release notes tied to milestones and backlog, and tag - taking over from release-please and release-plz. The guarantee is at the boundaries that cannot be skipped: land refuses a change with no record, and a CI check on every pull request does the same; a local hook only points the way. Local commits stay free; the record is per change. Refined the same day by 2026-11-11-glimpses: the record is the glimpse, made while the work is fresh; a change is the glimpses it carries.
rejected: Records only in commit messages (lost to squash merges, readable only through git); refusing every local commit with hooks (they fight rebase and amend, are bypassed with --no-verify, and the bypass becomes routine); adopting changesets or Knope as they are (a bump and a summary, tied to nothing else); keeping release-please (prose that drives nothing).
why: The author: data about work goes stale because nothing guarantees it is produced; release tooling writes prose nobody consumes, while ocoeco already knows tasks, goals, decisions and effort. 48% of recent landings produced any data.

decision: ocoeco check reads a project's essence as advice and never fails on a gap.
rejected: Failing the check until every step is served.
why: A gap is the truth about a project, not an error in its data.

decision: Code is changed by structure: whole items replaced with ast-grep, matched by their signature; logic kept outside macros where tools and readers see it; new views and tools added as new files; every edit verified before anything lands.
rejected: Text patches with better anchors; Comby (language-agnostic, less exact for Rust); writing our own rewriter.
why: Patching source by matching text was the heaviest manual work (19 times) and the cause of most failed runs, one of which landed a commit that changed nothing.

decision: Hand-work saturation is measured in effort - minutes weighted by load on Borg's CR10 scale - as well as count; there is no deliberate status: looking, listening and deciding are counted and automatable like the rest.
rejected: Count alone; NASA-TLX's six ratings on every bump (too heavy); exempting judgment from automation.
why: The author's 30 kg box: ten seconds, yet draining. And tests must judge sound and pictures themselves, with no person judging mid-run (jidoka).

decision: The record of work is the glimpse, made through ocoeco at any moment while the work is fresh; ocoeco supplies most of it (what ocoeco note wrote since the last glimpse, the backlog items and milestones they serve, the effort), and the person or agent types a line. ocoeco commit renders a commit from the glimpses not yet committed, with a trailer per glimpse; ocoeco release consumes the glimpses of what has landed. Git depends on ocoeco, never the reverse: a glimpse needs no git.
rejected: One record per change, written at commit time (later than the work, and tied to git); records only in commit messages; hooks refusing every local commit.
why: The author: capture data where it is fresh, while the work is remembered, not sorted out afterwards; and git operations depend on ocoeco, not ocoeco on git. This refines 2026-11-11-changes-are-records, whose record was tied to a change.

decision: Hand-work becomes part of ocoeco's language: a handwork table of atomic actions with counts, recorded by ocoeco hand (match, bump, or ask), shown by the observatory as hand-work worth a tool.
rejected: Logging whole tasks (they never repeat); free-text notes in the session log (they cannot be counted); bumping on any resemblance without asking (silent merging of different actions).
why: Proposed by the author. A board task is many steps and never repeats; atomic actions do. The wording is kept from drifting by the tool, as the vocabulary keeps words from drifting.

decision: ocoeco check names every table a repository keeps beside its exported ones but does not export.
rejected: Exporting every file automatically - some are kept for a project's own use.
why: A device lab's whole backlog and a tool's decisions and log went unseen by the observatory for days; ocoeco note found it by refusing.

decision: The shared language is language.toml, a tad declaration; ocoeco note checks each row it writes with tad's check_row; the shapes kept as Rust constants are gone.
rejected: Rewriting every project's tables in tad's canonical form now (churn in 22 projects, no reader gains); keeping the shapes in Rust (a second declaration language).
why: One way to declare and check tables across the commons: tad's, readable by people and by any tool. A test proved the file said exactly what the constants said before they were removed; ocoeco's own tests pass unchanged.

decision: Hand-work is called manual work everywhere - the table manual_work, the command ocoeco manual, land --manual; every record and bump appends a timed event to manual_events.
rejected: hand-work (less plain); ocoeco did (the person does, not the tool); inventing times for the history recorded before.
why: The author: manual work is the plain word, and with the time kept it can be set beside commits and releases. A command named manual could be read as documentation; the vocabulary defines it, and ocoeco has no documentation command to collide with.

decision: Rows are recorded with ocoeco note, not hand-written per job.
rejected: A per-job script; a general JSON editor that knows nothing of the format.
why: Every job wrote its own script to patch JSON: the same handwork again and again, each a chance to break a table. On its first use the tool found that ocoeco itself exported no decisions.

decision: ocoeco manual without an action opens a list in the terminal (ratatui): type to narrow, arrows, Enter, the usual minutes and load offered.
rejected: A web form (not TTY-first); fuzzy matching on typed text alone (it guesses).
why: Asked by the author: typing an action again is a chore and splits the ledger into near-duplicates.

decision: Research joins the language as its own table (question, found, sources, date); decisions cite it and name the steps they are about; the observatory badges each step with its decisions.
rejected: Sources alone (a list of works says nothing of the question asked); a separate research page with no link to steps.
why: Asked by the author: research should back decisions visibly, beside the milestones and progress they concern, and looking around should be a practice for agents and humans alike.

decision: Any row may be researched rather than live: it cites a research entry and is drawn outlined, with its age and a link; research gains versions (topic, date, supersedes), a refresh horizon, and a place in the attention view when it goes stale.
rejected: Copying outside claims in as if measured; overwriting research on refresh; marking live data (live is the default).
why: Asked by the author, to fill the picture honestly with what others achieved.

decision: Vocabulary becomes part of ocoeco's language: a vocabulary table (term, means, not, see), the shared words defined by ocoeco itself, a project's own words beside them, translated like everything else, and shown in views.
rejected: Folding definitions into the concepts table; a glossary written by the observatory about projects.
why: Asked for by the author, so the work can be spoken about clearly; concepts and vocabulary answer different questions.

decision: Where the whole is weakest right now is where attention goes.
rejected: triage (medical jargon); focus; priorities (a ranking someone sets)
why: What should be looked at next, read from every project - not what is loudest.

decision: An idea a project rests on, with why it matters, is a concept.
rejected: principle (a rule to follow, a narrower thing); belief
why: Distinct from idea (why the project exists) and from vocabulary (what a word means).

decision: A shared process that projects call, not copy, is a conveyor.
rejected: pipeline (CI jargon, and one run); template (copied, the opposite)
why: A conveyor carries any load the same way; you put work on it, you do not build your own.

decision: A lens chosen to stand in the observatory's navigation is curated.
rejected: featured, pinned (web jargon); official (claims an authority it does not have)
why: Says chosen with care, and nothing more; any lens is still found without it.

decision: An owned fork pinned upstream and changed only as patches meant to go home is a cutting.
rejected: fork (suggests drifting apart); vendored copy (a frozen copy, nothing goes home)
why: Rhizoid's gardening word: a cutting is a living piece of the parent plant, grown in your soil.

decision: A choice taken, with why and what was rejected, is a decision.
rejected: ADR (an acronym a reader must be taught); choice (says nothing of the alternatives)
why: The plain word; the rejected options are what make it worth keeping.

decision: Minutes weighted by load are effort.
rejected: cost (money); toil score (jargon); workload (NASA-TLX's wider measure)
why: Effort is the plain word for time and strain together - the 30 kg box.

decision: A project's whole chain on one page is its essence.
rejected: overview, summary (say less, not more); dashboard (numbers, no reasons); at a glance
why: Essence is what a thing most truly is; the page shows why, what, how and now at once.

decision: The daily job that writes down what a project's work produced is its gatherer.
rejected: collector (monitoring jargon); logger; recorder (plain, but breaks the metaphor)
why: One metaphor, kept whole: gatherers in each field, the harvest brought in by the observatory.
