rejected: A waits_on field that holds a link (one more place saying what a connection says); the halt removed when it is over (what was is the record); the typed waiting taken away now (it stands beside what is read off until the reading earns trust - the part that shows them apart is how it does).
why: The board's own next step for reading off the act: waiting read off what halts it. Looked at first: of twelve items typed waiting, eleven said what they wait on in a sentence - nine naming a row - and eight halts were drawn, one of them over: argenv's open lists halted ocoeco on argenv, and the trial showed it did not wait after all, with nothing to say so (a halt is a state, and it was typed).

decision: A table a place keeps on another branch of its own repository is kept by it all the same: where the place is held, it is read there with git, and it is as of when that branch last changed - which the beam says. Its rows are things like any other.
rejected: Leaving them to observation (the same place seen two ways would differ in what it has); copying them into the folder (a second copy to keep in step).
why: Looked at on 2026-11-14: 18 places keep their activity, what CI did and their releases on another branch, written nightly; they were read only by observing, and passed over in three places in the program where a place is held. The mark already said the route - a path, and a branch; nothing read it.

decision: The lenses a place keeps as rows are brought from what an observatory observed as from a folder with a mark: by whatever route its rows arrived, a place has the lenses it keeps. So an observatory's sheet is in view on its published page, as it is where the observatory is held.
rejected: Bringing lens files from what was observed (what is observed is rows; a lens kept as rows is what travels).
why: From what was observed the author's sheet was not in view at all: its rows were there, observed, and lenses were brought only from folders with a mark. Tried in a copy observed anew: the sheet from what was observed is the sheet looked at live, line for line.

decision: The parts that took a written link apart to find what it points at read the graph instead: an edge says each of its ends as parts - where it is held, its star, its table, its id, and the connection it came through - and a lens joins on them. Six parts moved: in work, what was done and what nothing advances; in signs, what is showing and what came of it; in purpose, what a milestone rests on, twice. Over every place each of the three lenses shows what it showed before, line for line. What tests tell of a milestone is still counted as it is written: a condition is not yet an edge.
rejected: Moving the parts and judging the difference by eye (each lens compared line for line before and after); keeping both ways side by side (one meaning in two places); making a condition told by tests an edge in the same step (what it points at - a feature at a level - asks its own look).
why: The trial of the graph (2026-11-14-the-graph-under-the-tables) showed the links are all there as edges; what it had not done was let other lenses use them. Of 36 parts, 6 took a link apart with splitting, cutting and matching inside text; the others that rewrite a name only shorten it for showing. Proven by the strongest test there is: what a person sees is unchanged.

decision: An observatory may observe by holding: each place it gathers that carries a mark is brought to hand with git, as it is on GitHub now, and read there as any place held is read - its tables, those it keeps on another branch, and what the routes read. What is observed is then what is held, as of when it was brought: one way of reading, not two. And what a route reads - a commit, a guard, a file of source - is a thing in the graph like any other, named by what it names of itself and not by the line it stands on, and is observed with the rest; the places are read side by side. A record of work was made standing on what is there when it is made.
rejected: Teaching the way that asks GitHub to read each route through its own calls (every route written twice, forever); bringing everything a gathered owner has (the first trial brought a fork of the Linux kernel - 4.2 GB, six minutes; only what carries a mark is a place, and those are 26 MB and a minute and a half); copying what a route reads into the place's own files (a second copy, as of nobody knows when).
why: Sign what-a-route-reads-is-not-a-thing: a route was read only where a place is held, so a published page - built from what was observed by asking GitHub - had no history, no source, no guards; and one could not stand on a guard. Looked at: observing already had two ways of reading, asking GitHub and reading folders under a root, and the second read a table kept on another branch from the wrong place. Tried on the lab: observed from held folders and by asking, 43 of 44 tables were the same byte for byte - the other differing by one run that happened between - and holding gave 1,703 changes, 532 guards and 126 files besides.

decision: A row belongs to the place it is of: the place it names - its project - where that place is in view, else the place that keeps it. The same row reached by more than one route - observed by two observatories; held here and observed - is one row: the one whose own moment is the latest, and where it says none, the one that came first. The ways in say so once, and both a lens's gathering and the graph read rows through them.
rejected: Leaving one observatory's observation out of view by a rule (which is the fresher is said by each row, not by a list); naming such a row by its keeper (it is about the place it names: its keeper only observed it).
why: Sign a-run-in-view-twice: looked at live from the author's observatory there were 98 rows for 49 runs - two observatories each keep what they observed of what has run, and both are in view - and one of the two was a day older: a run as it was on the 13th beside the same run as it is on the 14th, both as if so now. Had the older failed and the newer passed, the lens of signs would have shown a failure that is no more. The author: a place is not its route; and a route must not hide as of when.

decision: A part that puts another lens's plane or shape beside this lens's own says places; through is left to light passing a focus - the beam's rows in, so many through. Side by side and one after another, the two ways lenses go together, each have their own word. Every built-in lens and the rows the author's observatory keeps say it so.
rejected: Reading both words for one field (a name is not the place - but two names in the program for one field is the overlap kept); leaving the beam's word to change instead (through is what light does).
why: Sign through-is-two-things, seen in the review the author asked for: one word for two natures.

decision: A repeat is asked as what it is: not a line but a group. The lens of the graph keeps repeats out of the longest line of one kind, and shows instead what repeats joins - every thing reached through repeats, whichever way, as faces of one nature.
rejected: Leaving repeats in the walk and capping it (a ring counted as a length); keeping a direction on a repeat (the first written is not the first in nature).
why: Sign repeats-walked-as-a-line: walked as a line, repeats came back to where it began - argenv's open lists repeat ocoeco on argenv, which repeat argenv's open lists. A repeat says two things are one need with different faces (2026-11-13-a-need-for-clarity); the author: where two separate things turn out to be of the same nature they merge as one with different faces.

decision: A lens may read a shape another lens names, as it reads a table another lens defines: it takes its light from that lens - its tables, what it reads, and its shapes, made ready before its own, followed as far as shapes lead. One lens names a shape and others read it; a shape named by two lenses, or named like a table, stops the build. The beam says such a shape as light coming in, shaped by the lens that names it. The lens of the graph names what points nowhere, and no longer shows it; the lens of signs asks of it, as a sign read off the graph.
rejected: A shape copied into each lens that needs it (one meaning in two places); a lens reading another lens's projection as laid out (the shape is intelligible before any surface); shapes free of the rules tables keep (two of one name, met in use).
why: The named shape (2026-11-14-a-named-shape) let a projection feed a lens within one lens; the author's picture is light passing from one lens into the next. And what points nowhere was the graph's to know and the lens of signs' to say: both needed it, and only placing could pass between lenses - which lays out, and cannot be asked of.

decision: The work lens shows where the work is happening - the things stood on while records of work were made in the last day, of any kind - and an item stood on while work was recorded is in progress, as one a record says it advances. What a driver does is seen where it is done; nothing is typed to place it.
rejected: Typing what a record advances so the board shows it (the form-filling the act replaces); a board of items only (work happens on a decision, a thought, a sign as well).
why: The first record of work made the truer way said where it was made and nothing of what it advances, and so would not have shown on the board, which read in progress only from what was typed. The author: work is seen when it happens, through ocoeco.

decision: What points nowhere is known in one place, the graph: the check, the guard that refuses a write adding a link to nowhere, and moving rows all read it, as the lens of signs does through the graph's shape. The graph gives the edges of one place, followed into the others; an edge keeps the link as it was written, and for a connection whether its near end holds too. The program's own walk over every relation and row, apart from the graph, is gone. The check says what it said before, word for word.
rejected: The check bringing a lens into focus to learn it (it would ask the engine once for every place, where the graph is read in the program in a moment); a check that says it in new words (the words it said are what people and the jobs read).
why: Sign what-points-nowhere-is-asked-twice: when the graph came it said the same as the check - two places knowing one thing; with shapes across lenses the lens of signs read it from the graph, and the check still knew it on its own. Tried in two copies of OCO's place - one link made to point nowhere, and one connection's near end - before and after: the same words.

decision: The graph is made of the places in view by whatever route what they keep arrived: a folder with a mark, or what an observatory observed of a place, each row naming the place it is of. What is observed carries what a mark says of its place - the other names its tables go by, what kind of place it is, what it gathers - so that what was observed says it as the place itself does.
rejected: A second way of making the graph for what was observed (one graph, made of places however they came); leaving what a mark says out of what is observed (the conditions milestones rest on would point nowhere on the page).
why: The beam, the first time it said by which route its light came: from what the author's observatory observed - as its published page is built - the links were 0 and the shape of what holds things back was empty. The graph was made only of folders with a mark; so everything read off it - what holds things back, what each sign waits on, what lies ahead, where the work is happening - showed nothing on the page. The author: a lens behind does not care where a shape came from; it cares about the shape.

decision: Within one look the graph of the places in view is made once, and given to every lens and every table of it that asks: a lens brought into focus with all it places, its beam, a place checked - each is one look, and a look within another is the same look. Nothing is kept beyond it: what stays open, like the dome in a terminal, sees what has changed.
rejected: A smaller graph (what was added is what one stands on); the graph kept from one run to the next (it would show what was, as if it were so now - the thing answered all week).
why: Measured on 2026-11-14, after the language, what the routes read and the tables kept on other branches had each become things: a look through signs took 1.2 s, the check of one place 4.7 s - and git, asked for a table or a history, a hundredth of a second or less. One graph took under half a second; it was being made again for each table of it a lens asked of, and by the check for every lens in turn. Every job checks all 25 places: jobs outran the wait for them three times that day.

decision: Every link in the commons is read as one relation - this, how, that - and looked at through a lens. Every row of every place in view is a thing, named by where it is held, its table and its id; every link a row holds in a declared relation is an edge named by its field; every connection is an edge named by how it bears, through the connection that says so. Whether an edge holds is said where the place it points into is in view, and left unsaid where it is not. No place keeps these rows: ocoeco makes them from the links, as it makes the language's from the lenses. The lens of the graph asks what rows alone could not: what is pointed at most, what nothing points at, how things point, and how far a line of one kind runs - the walk done by the engine, not by the program.
rejected: Leaving the files behind for a graph store now (decided in a head, before the trial); a graph kept by a place (it would drift from the links it describes); naming a thing by its table and id alone (stars of one name live under several owners - lens is four).
why: The author, 2026-11-13: tables are a particular shape of data, exactly like a lens - why pass everything through a middle man? Researched the same day (research tables-or-a-graph): at rest we already keep things with ids and links between them - nodes and edges, written as text; the tables appear only when a lens asks. Of 36 parts in the lenses, 8 take a name apart to find what it points at, and 280 lines of the program check links, 473 rewrite them, 59 walk a chain. A trial, not a move: it lets the commons see whether the graph is already there.

decision: A table is looked through as itself where no lens has its name: every row passed through, each field as it is - the identity, the passthrough lens over what a place keeps, with no file. And the lens of language shows where a lens's two faces do not meet: an entry that puts into a table none of the lens's own parts asks of - what is put and not then got by the same lens.
rejected: A lens file for each table (the identity declares nothing); the identity listed among lenses in the fulldome (one per table, filling every plane); enforcing the law as a refusal (shown, as a sign is, while it is so).
why: Research the-simplest-lens: the smallest whole set of lenses has the identity, three ways into a shape, two ways together and two directions held to a law - what is put is what is then got. ocoeco had both ways together; it lacked the identity - a table kept as another kind of thing than a lens, though it is the passthrough - and the law between glimpse and focus was nowhere said.

decision: The language is in the graph: every lens in view and what it is made of - its tables and their fields, its entries, its relations, its parts - are things; and how they go together are links - a part is part of its lens, rests on the tables and the shapes it asks of, and places another lens; an entry is for the table it fills; a lens rests on what it reads. One stands on a lens, a part or a table as on anything, and walks from what is laid out back to all it was made of. And standing on a star shows why it exists, in its own words: the rows of its idea.
rejected: A lens of its own for walking the language (the graph is one; the language is in it); a link from every row to its lens (a row is of a table; its table is part of a lens).
why: Signs a-lens-is-not-a-thing and a-star-s-idea-is-not-reached, from looking at the whole on 2026-11-14: one could stand on anything but a lens built into the program, and only the lens of language saw the lenses, as rows of its own; and a star's idea - 95 rows across the stars - was pointed at by nothing, a walk arriving at the one line of its mark. The author: when a projection is not what we want, we navigate everything - how lenses compose, how shapes come together into a shape of shapes - from what we see on a surface back to anything that was before it.

decision: The lenses built into ocoeco are kept in language/: the shared language, built into the program. lenses/ is where any place keeps the lenses it brings. ocoeco's repository is still both the program's source and a place - but its source is no longer read as a place's lenses, so a lens file left there by work in hand is not laid out by the installed program as if the place had brought it.
rejected: A place's lenses read from somewhere a mark names (a setting for what one name can settle); ocoeco's place left unmarked (it is a place: it keeps decisions and work); keeping the folder and skipping ocoeco's own place by its id (a rule for one place).
why: Sign the-program-and-a-place-at-once, met three times: when the lens of signs was landed (the program installed and the place disagreed), and when a lens file left by a failed attempt was laid out by the installed program as ocoeco's place's own. One folder, two natures: the program's language and a place's lenses shared a name. The program itself already called these lenses the shared language.

decision: The lens of the graph shows one line of each kind: the longest, and of those equally long the first by where it begins and ends. Where it begins and where it ends are of the same line.
rejected: Showing every line that is longest (hundreds, among the turns of the conversation); leaving it, as only a comparison had noticed (a lens that answers differently each time cannot be compared with itself).
why: Sign the-longest-line-is-not-settled: where many lines were equally long the lens showed a different one each look. Looked at: it took where the longest began and where it ended each on its own, so that among equals the two could be of different lines - a line shown that does not exist.

decision: A relation says the nature of its pointing, where its field's name is one word among several for it: what a thing rests on (a milestone's criteria; a decision's research and sources; research's sources; a word's decision), what it is for (what an item or a working serves; what a record of work advances), what it follows (what a decision refines; what a reflection answers), what it is about (what a record or a reflection touches; where a record was made or a sign seen; what a decision is about). An edge carries it; a connection's how is its nature already. Standing on a thing shows the natures, as sentences - this rests on that; that is for this - and the graph shows the seventeen words as the few natures they are.
rejected: Renaming the fields to one word each (the language grows and does not rewrite what it said; and each word is right where it stands); directions declared as up and down (what a thing rests on and what it is for say it in plain words); a list of which word is which nature kept in a query (the lens that declares the relation says it).
why: The author, 2026-11-14: look at the whole - how everything relates, what overlaps, what is behind it where there is less friction; and before: navigation between composing and stepping back, without losing relations. Looked at through the graph: seventeen words for how one thing points at another, among them four for what a thing rests on, two for what it is for, two for what it follows and three for what it is about - and nothing saying so. What it rests on and what it is for are the way down and the way up.

decision: Every place is a thing in the graph, saying what it is for; and what a place gathers - a constellation its stars, an observatory what it looks at - is drawn from it, as its mark says. The lens of around shows where a thing is held, and from a place what it holds by kind and the milestones it reaches for. So a walk from one record of work arrives at the whole: the item it advances, the milestone that rests on it, the star that holds it and what that star is for, the constellation and the observatory that gather it.
rejected: An edge from every row to the place that holds it (three thousand edges saying what each thing's name already says); a table of places kept by a place (a mark is where a place says what it is; the graph reads it).
why: Looked at through around, the day it was made: a walk could not reach the top - a star's purpose is said in its mark, not in a row, so nothing arrived at what the whole star is for; and what gathers what was said in marks and drawn nowhere. The author: a whole is as far back as we can go, and navigation back must not lose the relations.

decision: A record of work says it touched the rows remembered since the last record that are there when it is made. A row entered and then put back - a trial thrown away, a change refused - was not touched by this record.
rejected: Clearing what is remembered by hand after a refusal (handwork, and forgotten the next time); forgetting on every refusal (what is remembered and still there was touched).
why: The same day entries began to be remembered as what a record touched, two refused attempts in the canon's place left such memories of rows no longer there; the next record said it had touched them, and the reader refused it for links pointing nowhere - rightly.

decision: What a run's ending means, and that a failing one is urgent, is the lens of signs' to say, in one place: its part failing on main is marked urgent, and what newly comes into view there is said so. The voice carries what a lens says is new - urgently where the lens says so - and decides nothing. Observing only observes: the program's own deciding of what fails, and its saying of what changed, are gone. What is no longer in view is said as the line it was, under its heading.
rejected: Keeping the program's own list of what fails beside the lens (the two disagreed within an hour); urgency decided in the voice's script (a meaning kept outside the lens); a third observer of runs kept quiet by a rule (left as it is: two observations, of the lab and of GitHub, now say the same way).
why: Sign what-fails-is-decided-twice: what a run's ending means was decided by the lens's query and by the program's own code, and within an hour of one being corrected the lab told the author urgently of two failures that were not; a third thing - the voice - said nearly the same. Urgency was the one thing the voice could not know, and it is meaning: so it belongs in the lens.

decision: The lens of language asks what a value is - words, a whole number, a number, yes or no - not what its type is called: a date is words held to a shape, as an id may be held to a pattern, and is not another nature than words.
rejected: Rewriting what the language said to make the kinds match (it grows; what it said stands); leaving the lens to list a date beside a moment kept as a number (one is a shape held, the other a different nature).
why: Sign a-date-held-two-ways: date was declared a date in reflections and words in decisions and research - all three as the language stood on its first day, so none may be rewritten. Looked at: the two are not two natures. A moment kept as a number of seconds beside a moment kept as words is; and the lens asked about the name of a type, where it should ask what a value is.

decision: What an observation could not read is a sign - it does not fit, and the observation is who saw it. It is written among the signs the places keep, said by the observation and of the place it is about; it shows where signs show, and is gone by itself once the thing reads again.
rejected: Another file for what could not be read (a second kind beside the signs, and a second place to look); leaving it to the line the observation prints (gone when the run's log is).
why: Sign what-could-not-be-read-is-overwritten: observing wrote what it could not read to a file of the same name as the table of signs, and the table then overwrote it - the observation said 3 problems and nothing kept what they were. Two things under one name, and they were one nature: something that does not fit, said by whoever sees it.

decision: What each sign showing waits on is read off the halts drawn to it: the shape of what holds things back holds signs as well as items, saying which it holds; the lens of signs asks of it, and says for each sign what holds it back, or that nothing drawn does and it can be taken up now. What nothing has come of is shaped once in the lens of signs, and both its parts ask of it.
rejected: Saying it in a summary (it drifts from the data, and did); a field on a sign for what it waits on (a halt is what says that, from anywhere).
why: The author, 2026-11-14: why keep using prose instead of ocoeco - if something is lacking that you want to reflect, the whole point of the ecosystem is to capture and reflect it with lenses composed for it. What was lacking was what each sign waits on: it was said in words beside a sheet that could not say it, and the words were wrong - one item waits on the token, not two.

decision: What fits for a link reaches every star in view - every place kept beside the one stood in - not only the rows of this place: from a blank it offers this place's rows and the stars to go into; typing a star narrows to its kinds of row, then to its rows, each stroke choosing what fits the next blank.
rejected: Offering every row of every star at once (thousands, and no shape to choose by); a link into another star written by its short name (stars of one name live under several owners).
why: Sign what-fits-knows-only-the-place-stood-in: twice in one hour a link into another star was typed from memory and refused by the guard - a decision in OCO's place written from ocoeco. The author: each stroke choosing what fits the next blank; being on a blank showing what can be entered.

decision: From a blank on a typed line, what may come next is read off the language and the rows that exist - a lens asked the other way: the commands; the entries; an entry's fields not yet given, saying which are needed and which hold one of a set; for a field held to a set, the set; for the id, the rows a change would be made to; for a link, the kinds of row it may point into that hold any, then the rows that exist there, each with a few words of what it is; for free words, nothing. ocoeco fits answers a person, and with --shell answers a shell as it asks (complete -C 'ocoeco fits --shell' ocoeco). Nothing is written apart from the language: it is read.
rejected: Completions written for each shell from a list (the list is the language, and it changes); a word for where values come from, added to argenv's contract (what an entry and a relation already say); offering every row of every kind at once for a link that may point anywhere (the kind first, then the row).
why: Waited on all week: the author's picture of entering - each relation selected, not entered; each stroke choosing what fits the next blank; being on a blank showing what can be entered. And the sign met three times in three days: an id typed from memory and refused. Everything it reads now exists: what each entry asks (entries), the values a field allows, which tables a link may point into (relations), the rows that exist.

decision: Any lens may say what it keeps out of a place - a token, a key, a private channel, an address - told by its shape, and what of that shape is let be. It is kept out as a row is written, in the one function every row is written through: the words around it stay, and what was kept out is named where it stood. The program makes rows of it - where something was kept out, and where one is showing in what a place keeps - and the lens of what is kept out shows them. The check that runs before a change lands says where one is showing.
rejected: A list of what may be read or run (a wall; and a lens only takes a shape from what is); a pattern kept in a script and run by whoever remembers (what was done by hand for the conversation); refusing the whole row (the words around a token are the author's, and stay).
why: The author, 2026-11-14: no need for boundaries when everything is transparent and traversable; it was all one need - for clarity. And of the gap named in answer - that clarity works when someone looks; a secret is a surface too; what stayed out of the conversation was 41 things removed by hand with a pattern, a filter that should itself be a lens and be seen - exactly: you see it. Looked at first: every file every place keeps held no token, key, channel or address of someone, and one address of a machine that no one beyond it can reach.

decision: A lens that says nothing of where one stands is looked through from a place - lens@place - and sees what is in view from there: a star what it holds, a constellation its stars, an observatory all it looks at. So a constellation and an observatory are places a lens is looked through from, and nothing more. And looking through a lens from a thing leaves a step on the driver's trail; a record of work says where it was made - the things stood on since the last one - supplied by the act, never typed.
rejected: A lens for each place (a place is where one looks from, not another lens); holding a table as it stood to gain no field (the language grows: a field after those it had is growth, as a new relation is - what it had stays as it was, and the guard now holds exactly that); recording every look as a row (the trail is the driver's own; what it leaves in a place is where a record of work was made); keeping the typed advances as the measure of work (the act says where it happened).
why: The author, 2026-11-14: are a constellation, its stars and an observatory now presented like everything else, like lenses - names of those lenses? And: the work is not seen by what was planned (dead-weight records) but when it happens, through ocoeco - traversing the relations, looking, supplying glimpses are the concrete moments where it is happening. Looked at: a place was a thing one could stand on, not something a lens was looked through from; and what a record of work advances was typed by the driver in every job, over what the record already derives from what it touched.

decision: A change made through ocoeco is part of the record of work it says the same as: read off what both say, never typed; a saying several records share is the saying of none. Standing on a change shows where it is on GitHub; and on a page, an address of the web is a way out. So one walks from why something was decided, to the work, to what changed, and on to the code itself.
rejected: A field on a record of work for its change (a change cannot name itself before it is made; and it would be typed); a page of the site for every change (some two thousand: the code is on GitHub, and the way there is an address).
why: The author: to navigate anything from the abstract to the concrete and back. Walked on 2026-11-15, from an angle of the form to a decision to the record of the work - and there it ended: a change was in view as a thing and nothing joined it to the record that made it, nor led out to the code. Of 417 records of work, 349 said what a change in their place says; a record of work had nothing pointing at it.

decision: The route through git history says when a change was made in UTC - 2026-11-14T23:08:46Z - as every record of work, run and turn says its moment, whatever clock its maker kept. What git answered before is asked anew.
rejected: Working the moment out in every lens that reads one (the same working-out written again in each, and forgotten in the next); keeping the maker's clock and reading moments as instants in the engine (which clock a maker kept says where a machine stood, not when the change was made - and git keeps it, where it stays).
why: On 2026-11-15 at 19:46 UTC the flow said the latest thing in view was at 20:46. A change made on the lab says its moment in the lab's clock, an hour ahead - 2026-11-15T00:08:46+01:00 - and read as words, as a lens orders and compares moments, it comes after everything said in UTC within that hour; the engine too, asked to read it as a moment, drops the offset and keeps the hour. A lens that takes a change for following a thing said would be an hour off. A moment said in one clock is told apart by what it says alone; one said in the clock of whoever made it has to be worked out each time it is read.

decision: A part laid out once for each of something says, at its heading, the thing it is laid out for, where its value names one: the thing of that name, or the place of that star. While a site is laid out, the heading says that thing's page too, and the page leads there from the heading: a star's card, to the star.
rejected: A line of its own in each card to lead to the star (the card's name is the way, as on the engine's page); a heading that knows stars (it knows a value, and asks the names of things what that value is); a page lens that builds an address from a star's name (the page is the site's to say, by its own lens; the surface only leads where a plane says).
why: The first observatory's whole stands its stars side by side as cards, as the engine's front page does; the engine's cards lead to each star, and the language's led nowhere. A line already says the thing it is about, and a surface leads to its page; a heading said nothing of what its part is for, though the part knows: it is laid out once for each value of a column, and that value is a star.

decision: The shape that tells an address of someone lets through a lens looked through from a place named as GitHub names its pages: around@marshall-oco.github.io is written as an address is, and is no one's.
rejected: Changing the words of the turn (a turn is kept as it was said); letting the turns in past the check (the check is how nothing to be kept out gets in).
why: Reading two more transcripts into the conversation's place on 2026-11-15, the place's own check stopped the turns from being kept: one held an address of someone. It was a lens looked through from the author's observatory. What a place keeps out is clarity and not a wall: a shape that takes what is not an address for one hides what should be seen.

decision: A lens reads a table whichever lens in view declares it - one built into the program or one a place brings - and its shape is checked among the lenses in view from its place, not among the program's own alone. Where a lens reads a name that no lens in view declares as a table or names as a shape, the look says so, in words.
rejected: Making what followed parts of the conversation's own lens (it would then say where one stands, and a lens that does is no longer placed with every other); declaring turns a second time in the lens that reads it (a table has one lens); leaving the engine's own words to say it (they name a table, not what the lens lacks or where to look).
why: On 2026-11-15 a lens was made to say what followed a thing the author said - read off the records of work by their moments, in place of an overview drawn by hand in a chat. It reads turns, which the conversation's own lens declares, and the look stopped with the engine's words: Catalog Error: Table with name turns does not exist. What a lens reads was looked for among the tables of the lenses built into the program only: a table a place adds to the language could be read by the one lens that declares it. One lens defines a piece of data, many read it - that is how the language is meant, and it held for the program's own lenses alone.

decision: A look may be in passing: looked through from a thing without standing there, and no step is left. To stand on a thing is a driver's attention being there; a comparison of how something looks, or the timing of a look, is not.
rejected: Standing there first, so the step is in both looks (it holds for one thing, and a comparison of two moves between them); steps left out of what is compared (they are things like any other, and should compare).
why: Since a step is a thing, a comparison of how standing on a thing looks before and after a change left a step by looking, and saw it the second time: the look moved what it looked at. With two things in one comparison every look would have left another. Seen on 2026-11-15 in the first job that used oco-work.

decision: A name says what it means where one is about to use it: when what fits offers the fields of an entry, each says the first sentence of the word of its name. The words of the shared language go where the program goes - the program carries the words ocoeco's own place keeps, as they were when it was built - and a place's own word for a name is the one said there. The lens of language counts a lens as saying what it is by what it says of itself, and lists what still says nothing.
rejected: A meaning written on each field of each table (one name means one thing wherever it is carried: said once, as a word); meanings only where ocoeco's place is in view (a name should say what it means in any place the program is used); counting a lens as saying nothing where no word bears its name (every lens says what it shows: that is its meaning).
why: The angle with the least work toward it was holding it in one's head. On 2026-11-15, 143 words were entered for the names of fields and tables - 150 of 160 field names and 39 of 42 table names then said what they mean: most of it known nowhere but in the program and in a conversation that ends. A meaning kept in a table and shown nowhere is not felt; and from a place alone the words were out of view.

decision: A thing's whole name is where it is held - owner and place - its table and its id. Its shorter name, without the owner, is its name only where no other thing goes by it: a name of several things is the name of none, and a line about it leads nowhere. A site leads to a page by every name that names its thing alone; and no two of its pages are written in one place.
rejected: The shorter name going to whichever came first (a way that leads to the wrong page is worse than none); whole names everywhere (the shorter one is what is said and read, and is one thing nearly always).
why: Sign a-shorter-name-is-several-things. And the site command had been landed before it was tried - the trial failed for a reason of its own making, and the job went on: tried afterwards, it showed this. The trial is now part of the job, and each part of it a reason to stop.

decision: A part of a lens is known by one name: the id it is kept as. A lens kept as rows names each part by the id its row is kept as, and the graph finds it by that id alone; a lens kept as a file has no ids of its own, and its parts are named by where they stand in the file - which is then the id. Records of work that touched a part since taken back now touch what is still kept: the lens it was part of.
rejected: Renumbering what a place keeps so that its ids follow where its parts stand (an id is what is pointed at: it does not move when another part is added or taken back); a link that says what it pointed at was taken back (the two are what came before taking back was refused when pointed at; a part to carry for two rows); leaving the two records as they were (history, but a link the whole says points nowhere is a sign every look then carries).
why: On 2026-11-15 two looks at one whole gave two answers: through what was observed, two records of work pointed nowhere; over the places held, the same records were said to hold. Read off the source: turning the lenses in view into rows named every part by where it stands - the fifth, the sixth - beside the rows a place keeps under their own ids. So over places held a part had two names, and a link to a part taken back landed on whichever part stood in its place. What was observed names parts only by their ids, and saw it. The two records date from before taking a row back looked at what points at it.

decision: Work done by hand is counted by naming its record: ocoeco manual --id ID counts it as it is, without its words said again; a record that is not kept is not made of nothing. Where neither words nor a record are given and there is no terminal to choose in, that is said in a sentence.
rejected: Asking for the words each time (the record already has them: a thing typed twice drifts); opening the list wherever nothing was said (where there is no terminal that is a panic, and says nothing of why).
why: On 2026-11-15 a job counting the day's handwork named each record by its id, as the command says a record is bumped, and stopped twice with a panic - failed to initialize terminal: without the words of the action the list to choose from was opened, and a job has no window. What it lacked could have been said in a sentence.

decision: What a route reads of a place both held and observed is read once: a row of one place under one id is one row, the first to arrive - looking from a place, that is the place as it stands.
rejected: Passing over everything observed of a place held (what only observing brings - what has run, what was released - is kept by no place, and would go out of view).
why: Since where one stands is read as it stands, a place looking at what it observed is in view twice: held, and observed. Rows a place keeps were already one row by two routes; rows a route reads - a change, a document, a guard - were not, and the lens of results listed each change of the place one stands in twice, on the published pages too. Seen on 2026-11-15 by looking at the whole one step up and then into results: found by looking, the day it came in.

decision: A row is taken back by saying so: ocoeco take-back, the table and the id. It is no longer kept where it was - refused, and put back, where something in that place still points at it. The inverse of entering one, and guarded the same way.
rejected: A mark on the row saying it is no longer so (what is taken back would stay in every look, to be filtered by each lens); renaming a field through it (a field is the shape of a table and is named in what parts ask: that is still made by hand, and is said so).
why: Sign a-row-cannot-be-taken-back: each merge of two things of one nature - the act the whole is refined by - ended in changing a place's files by hand, with a program outside the language. Moving rows between places with every link rewritten was already an act; taking one back was not.

decision: The pages of a site are read from everything its lens brings into focus - also from what a lens placed in it brings. So a place may offer pages of what it holds, as a lens of its own, and an observatory place them among its own. The lens of the site is asked once.
rejected: The observatory's lens reading the conversation's shapes (it cannot be checked from its own place: what a lens reads must be in view where it is kept); telling the author's turns from the agent's by which turns a record of work entered (true today by how turns are entered, and wrong the day an agent's turn is entered the same way).
why: The conversation's place holds the turns and the lens of what followed them: a page for each thing the author said is its to offer. The author's observatory could not ask for them itself - a lens is checked from its own place, where the conversation's tables and shapes are not in view. A lens of lenses says only what to place together: that held for what a page shows, and not yet for which pages there are.

decision: A site is said by a lens: each row of what it brings into focus is a page - where it is written, what it looks through, and the thing it is the page of. ocoeco site lays each out on a surface. While a site is laid out a plane says, for a line about a thing that has a page, where that page is - and the page lens makes that line's words the way there. So a walk on the web is pages that lead to one another: nothing fetched, nothing run, and which pages there are is rows a place may say for itself.
rejected: A script in the page that fetches and draws (a second program, on a surface that cannot be looked through); a loop in the workflow (which pages there are, said where no lens sees it); a page for every thing at once (some nine thousand: a site says which it has, and may say more).
why: The author: what is most important is navigating - and the perfect form does not say on what surface. The published page was one page, and could not be walked. The engine's site is many pages written by a program; looked at on 2026-11-14, what the fulldome lacked of it was a page for each place. With a surface said by a lens and a plane saying what each line is about, which pages there are was the one thing left unsaid. Tried on what the author's observatory last observed: the whole, with the ways to other pages taken out, is the page the program writes, byte for byte.

decision: A step is kept as a row: who stood where, and when. Where ocoeco keeps its trail on a machine is a place that machine holds - it says so itself, once - and steps are a table of it: in view from an observatory standing there, never gathered, never leaving the machine. A step is a move; standing again where one stands is not one; and steps do not pile up without end. A step is about the thing stood on, so standing on a thing shows who stood there and when; and the lens of the flow says where each driver stands now, read off their latest step.
rejected: A new way in for the trail (it is rows in a file, of a place: the way in there already is); every look as a step (looking again where one stands is not moving); steps gathered with everything else (where one looks is one's own, and of that machine).
why: The author: me using the window is itself a flow of data; what I am working on becomes intelligible and exactly derivable from what I do in it. Sign where-the-drivers-stand-says-nothing-of-when. oco-agent already kept its own record as a place of the machine; the trail was beside it and said nothing of being one.

decision: Looking through a lens from a thing, the lens may read that thing in full: in_full, a table the program gives for the thing stood on - a row for each field it carries, as it is kept, by whatever route its rows come. The lens of around says it first: itself, in full, in the order its table declares its fields. A lens that reads it is looked through from a thing, as one that says {here} is.
rejected: Keeping every thing's whole row in the graph (the graph is made of everything in view for every look: the words of three thousand turns would be carried to each); laying a table out as itself from a thing (the passthrough says a row as one line, field after field - a decision's why and what it rejected run together); a lens for each kind of thing (what a thing carries is said by its table: one part says any of them).
why: On 2026-11-15 what followed a thing the author said became a look: each line of it is about a thing, and a step down from a line led to a page that said the thing in seventy characters - the few words the graph keeps of everything - with all that is around it, and nothing more of what it says. The why of a decision, what it rejected, what a reflection learned were read only in the files of the place that keeps them: outside the ecosystem. A thing is what it says before it is what it points at.

decision: A thing says when: by the field its table says dates it, or else its moment, or else its day - where that is shaped like one; a moment kept as seconds is said as a moment, so all of them sort as one. The lens of the flow is everything in view that says when, the latest first, whatever kind it is and wherever it is held. Standing on a thing shows what came just before and after it in its place: a step in time, as the rest are steps along what points at what. And a look may follow: it does not end, is asked again when what is in view has changed, shows the whole anew on a screen and elsewhere only what newly came into view, and waits without load.
rejected: A program that stays running and holds the whole (the next thing, perhaps - and it would have had nothing of time to hold); a table of events kept beside the things (when is already said, by each thing, in the field its table names); the look that does not end as the window's own (it belongs to no surface: any look may follow).
why: The author: it is a process of a whole, with no defined start and no end; idle, it flows without load like an open window; in progress is not a one-time render but a continuous reflection of observed signals. Looked at on 2026-11-15, the angle nothing had touched: nothing in the graph said when - the whole was a still picture, drawn again each time. Sign the-whole-has-no-time-in-it. A process cannot begin with a program that stays running if what it shows has no time in it.

decision: What a place adds to a lens it does not keep - a relation, a part, an entry, a route said for a lens the program brings or another place keeps - is joined to that lens wherever it is in view: the lens looked through is the one it names, and this besides. Only what is added is recorded; the rest is referenced. A table stays defined by one lens: nothing is added to another's. The check says when a place adds to a lens that is not in view from it.
rejected: Copying the lens into the place to change it (the whole recorded for a little added, and two lenses of one name); adding the relation to the lens in the program (right for this one, and it leaves the next adjustment a change to the program again); adding fields to a table another lens defines (one lens defines a piece of data: widening it is another question, not answered here).
why: The author: no concept of a wrong lens - adjusting makes a new lens that changes the composition of the previous one a little, like a new node where only what is added or changed is recorded and the rest referenced. Sign what-is-added-to-a-lens-is-dropped: the first relation the ecosystem tried to add to itself by its own means was dropped without a word. Measured 2026-11-15: with it followed, the 538 guards each point at the file they are in.

decision: In the window an entry is made by saying its name where one stands. Said alone, it is shown what it asks, which of its fields point at things, and where it would be kept. Said with what it asks beneath it - each as FIELD: words - it is made by the entry itself, as it is made anywhere, where the thing stood on is held or in the place given. In a field that points at things, here names where one stands; where no name is given it is named by its first words. One then stands on what was entered.
rejected: A form made in the program and asked field by field (a driver without a terminal answers in one turn; and what an entry asks is the language's to show - a lens of it is what comes next); the link to where one stands supplied without being said (an entry may point at things by several fields, as a connection does by from and by to: which is meant is said, as here).
why: The author, 2026-11-15: one acts from within. The window showed which entries can say something of the thing stood on, and they had still to be made from outside - a command, its flags, the thing's name typed again. Standing on the thing already says what the entry is about. And his word the same hour: the program is what expresses the inside from outside for now, as assembly once did for a language; what it does is to be said from inside as the inside grows able to say it.

decision: An entry said in the window is made standing in the place it is kept in - an entry a place's own lens declares is known there, and nowhere else - and where it is not made, all of why is said. In a field that points at things, a mark names what it marks in what was last shown, as here names where one stands: a thing is pointed at, never named from memory.
rejected: Every entry of every place known from wherever one looks (an entry belongs to the lens of a place, and two places may call different things by one name); the other thing named by its id (remembered from outside, or copied by hand from what was just shown).
why: The first entry said in the window, on 2026-11-15, was the author's own turn - standing on the turn before it - and it was not made: the conversation's entry is declared by the conversation's lens, the window asked for it from the observatory's folder, where it is not known, and of the reason only its last line came back: For more information, try --help. And a connection says how one thing bears on another: standing on the one, the other was still to be named by typing what it is called.

decision: The lens of the graph says what is joined to nothing - it points at nothing and nothing points at it - by kind, beside what nothing points at. An island is a gap in the whole: something taken in and not yet joined to anything. The sheet of the perfect form shows the islands.
rejected: Changing what the older part counts (what nothing points at is true as it is said, and a place may place it); a number alone (which kinds are islands is what shows where the whole has a gap).
why: Looked at one step up on 2026-11-15: half of everything in view - 5094 of 9969 things - was said to have nothing pointing at it, every change and every guard among them. But a change is part of its record of work and a guard is part of a file of source: they point, and are joined. What nothing points at mixes the leaves of the whole with what stands apart from it; and what stands apart - a translation, a release, what was done on GitHub - is what is not yet seen in the whole.

decision: What git answers for a commit is asked once, and kept beside the repository under that commit: a place's history, and a table kept on another branch. It is found again for as long as the name stands at that commit, and asked anew when it has moved - read from what git keeps of where its names stand, without asking git. Where that cannot be read, git is asked each time, as before. And the graph says where its own making went, stretch by stretch, in a lens's beam.
rejected: Keeping answers for a while (it would show what was as if it were so now - what is kept here is kept under the commit, and is exact); asking git side by side (less to wait for, and still asked every look); a program that stays running to remember (the same, held in a program instead of beside what it is of).
why: Sign making-the-graph-takes-time-not-understood. Timed stretch by stretch on 2026-11-15, the graph's 400 ms were not where they were looked for - working out the lenses in view took 7 - but in reading: 137 ms for what the places keep and 90 for what the routes read. 57 tables are kept on another branch and 27 places have a history: some 84 questions to git on every look, two or three thousandths of a second each. A commit does not change, so what was answered for one is exact for as long as the name stands there.

decision: Each time something is done by hand is a row of its own: counted again within the same second, it is named apart - by its moment, its record, and which time of that second it is.
rejected: A moment to the thousandth of a second (two times can still fall on one, and every other moment in the records is said to the second); one row saying how many times (each time has its own minutes and load, and what was done by hand is counted by its rows).
why: On 2026-11-15 a job counted three waits for a run, and later three looks at a page, one after the other: each time was written as a row named by its moment - to the second - and its record, and those of one second were named alike. The first observatory kept 16 times done by hand under 3 names. What is counted by its rows was counted rightly, and none of those rows could be told from its twin, pointed at, or changed.

decision: A lens of lenses that stands on a thing places lenses that look from a thing, from there. Placed by its name, a lens that looks from a thing stands where the placing lens stands; placed as every lens, they are the lenses that look from a thing, each left out where it brings nothing from there. From nowhere every lens is, as before, every lens that looks across - and a lens that looks from a thing places none. The lens of around places them: standing on a turn of the author's, one is shown what followed it.
rejected: A lens declaring which kinds of thing it stands on (it says so already, by bringing something or nothing from there); a page of its own for what followed a turn (a second answer to standing on the same thing, on one surface only).
why: What one sees standing on a thing was said twice for a turn of the author's: a page looked through what-followed, a step in the terminal or in text looked around. A step is one on every surface - around the thing - and what else looks from a thing belongs to what is around it: said by a lens of lenses, not by which surface one happens to be on.

decision: Standing on a thing shows what changed for it: the changes that are part of the work that was about it, each with where it is on GitHub - two steps of the walk, taken as one. And a look cut short by whoever reads it ends there quietly.
rejected: A page for every record of work (four hundred more pages for a step that can be taken at once); leaving the words of a failure (a person looking at the first lines of a look is told something broke).
why: On the site a decision has a page and a record of work has none: from why something was decided the way to what changed was two steps, and the second led off the site. The lens of around can take both at once. And a look piped to something that stops reading ended with words of a failure that was none - seen in a dozen outputs and passed over.

decision: A row is taken back only when nothing in view points at it: from a place, nothing in that place; from an observatory, nothing in any place it has in view. What is said to hold everywhere is asked of the whole - no link in view points nowhere - and not of one place against the others.
rejected: Looking only where one stands (from an observatory the whole is in view: that is what it is for); checking each place in turn after every landing (twenty-seven checks of three seconds: the whole says it in half a second).
why: On 2026-11-15 a part of the author's sheet was taken back from his observatory, where every place is in view, and a record of work in another place was left pointing at nothing. The refusal looked at this place's own links; and the word in oco-work for 'every place holds' ran a check that looks at one place. The graph over the whole saw it, and the voice said so.

decision: A lens looked through from somewhere - from a thing, from a place - has its beam traced as it is looked through from there: the beam of that look.
rejected: Leaving the beam to lenses looked through from nowhere (the walk is looked through from a thing every time).
why: Asked for on 2026-11-15, the beam of standing on a thing said nothing: the beam took the whole of around@thing for a lens's name, and found none. A step of the walk was the look whose cost was least understood, and the one look that could not say where its time went.

decision: The page is drawn by what the plane says, and the plane says two things more. A lens placed as one of every lens in view says so (of_every): the page lays open what a place put first, by name, and folds every other into a card that shows its name, what it says of itself and its figures - an index of the whole. A part laid out once for each of something says what (per): parts of one kind, where each is short, stand side by side as small cards - a star with its idea and how far it has come. Within a part the page draws by what the lines carry: measures as rings, a chain stepped in, short lines in columns, sentences as rows - the first eight of many, the rest folded beneath. What a line is known by is set strong where its words say that name; a thing named whole is the way to its page. The page of a place's whole is headed by what the place is called - the name on its mark - and says under it what the whole says it shows.
rejected: A card for every part, side by side (tried first: 80 of 85 parts are lists of sentences, and a narrow card breaks a sentence into a column of fragments); a field by which a lens says how it wants to look (a lens says what a thing means and a surface how it looks, so one lens looks right on every surface); telling a star's name from the punctuation of a line (the plane says what a line is known by, and nothing is guessed from words); the name The fulldome at the head of every whole (a visitor meets a place, and a place has a name); folding by a number a place sets (the page folds by what is there: what came as one of every other, and what is long).
why: Looked at on 2026-11-15, the page said by a lens was every part as a box the width of the page, one under another: 85 parts of the first observatory's whole in one column, and nothing said which came first. The engine's front page was still the one a visitor meets, because it shows each star as a card with its milestones as rings. Looked at before replacing: those cards are a composition the language already has - a part laid out once for each star, a measure on a line - which the engine draws by knowing what a star is. A surface can draw it by a meaning, knowing nothing of stars. What was lacking was two things the program knew and did not say: whether a lens was placed by name or as one of every other, and that a part is one of several of one kind. Said in the plane, any surface may use them; the page does. Tried four times on the lab without landing, and looked at each time in light, in the dark and at a phone's width before the next.

decision: The page is said by a lens: as-page lays a plane out as a page of the web - each part a section, its heading and its lines as a list, a measure as a meter - with its frame and its style in what the lens says. A plane's rows say where each comes in its part and how many lines the part has, so a surface knows where a part begins and ends from the row itself. A frame may say {scale}, which whoever asks for the page fills with what is looked at and when.
rejected: Changing how the page looks while saying it in the language (it cannot be looked at from here: equal to what was is how it is known to be right); taking the program's page away at once (it is what the lens is held equal to, and one observatory still asks for it); letting go of the commands nothing outside asks for (looked at: the search by topic is the commons' open door, and recording work done by hand is a designed thing with its own reasons).
why: Looked at through the lens of the program on 2026-11-15: of 105 changes to ocoeco in four days, 82 changed only the program - 12,476 lines added, against 1,835 in what lenses say. The program is changed from outside because it keeps being where things are said. The page was 57 lines of it, and how the page looks was a line of program too. Measured: what the author's observatory last observed, laid out by the program and by the lens - the same, byte for byte.

decision: The parts of a lens ask the engine in one go: what the lens gathered is loaded once, and each part's question is answered after it - a part finds its answer by its place among them. Where they cannot all be answered together - one of them fails, or the engine answers some other way - each part asks for itself as before, and says for itself what is wrong.
rejected: Keeping the engine running between looks (a program to hold, where asking once is enough); fewer parts in a lens (a lens says what it shows: how it is asked is the program's).
why: A step of the walk took 1.2 s and the author's sheet 2.6 with the graph made in a third of a second: most of a look was not the graph. Read on 2026-11-15: each part of a lens asked the engine in a run of its own, and every run loaded everything the lens had gathered again before answering - the whole graph, nine times, to stand on one thing. Found after the graph had said where its own time went, and it was not there.

decision: The program no longer has the page or markdown as surfaces of its own: the page is the lens as-page, and its old name, html, asks that lens. The guard that held the lens's page equal to the program's goes with it - there is one page, and nothing to hold it equal to. And gathering each table is timed: a lens's beam says, beside by which route a table came and as of when, how long it took, where that is worth saying.
rejected: Keeping the program's page as a second way (two of one nature, and a guard to carry); taking the text surface out too (a look is asked for many times a minute, and saying text through a lens costs it another question to the engine); guessing where the time goes (twice in these days a guess about cost was off).
why: Sign the-page-was-said-twice. Both observatories ask the lens for their page as of 2026-11-15, and no workflow asked the program for one. Looked at through its own lens, the program had grown by twelve thousand lines in four days; this is the first time it holds less. And a step of the walk had come to take a second and a half, slower than any other ordinary look, with nothing saying why: the author asks that what is not as wanted be seen in its projection, not guessed.

decision: A walk belongs to no surface. A plane says, for each line, the thing it is about - what its answer names as a thing, or its star and id where they are one thing only: never what its words suggest. Where a driver stands is kept beside the trail, and stays when the trail begins again: a lens that says where one stands, asked for from nowhere, is looked through from there - on whatever surface the last step was taken. To stand is one act, the same everywhere. A surface lays out what can be stood on its own way - a completion, a link, a pointer, a line to read - and adds nothing of its own. The terminal window is given the plane's rows like any other, and finds nothing by itself.
rejected: Making the window better at guessing (more of what was in the way); a walk of its own for each surface (the same excuses, once for each); taking the window away (it is one surface among others, and the open one - only not the place where walking lives).
why: The author, 2026-11-15: the perfect form does not say on what surface the interaction is, and the terminal window has a lot of excuses that make friction with it. Looked at: every part of the lens of around already named, as a value, the thing each line is about; looking and entering were already the same two acts everywhere; where one stands was already data. The window had its own copy of each. Sign the-walk-lives-in-a-window.

decision: The way up from a look is a surface said by a lens: as-outline lays a plane out one step up - each lens placed in it by its name and what it says of itself, its figures, and each part by its heading alone; parts laid out once for each of something as one line, how many and which. The whole in view is then some hundred lines, and the way back down is what a line names, looked through by itself. It is the page's folded cards, said for text: one meaning - a part is its heading and how much it holds - on two surfaces.
rejected: A flag that cuts a look to so many lines (a cut by count hides whatever comes after it; an outline hides nothing of the shape); a command of its own for the outline (a surface is a lens: it lays out any plane - the whole, one lens, a sheet - and a place may say its own); cutting short what a lens says of itself (it is the one line that says what the rest is).
why: Asked on 2026-11-15 whether the work still dives up through the ecosystem itself, the driver looked: the whole in text was every line of every lens, thousands of them, so each job cut a look down by hand - its first lines, the lines that begin a part - many times that day. A cut by count hides whatever comes after it, and nobody can say what it hid. The canon already says the form - every layer is the top of the layers beneath it; an outline is generated from the thing itself; a cold read is given the outline alone - and the page had been given it the same day, a lens folded to its name, what it says and its figures. Text had not. Tried first as a lens brought by a throwaway place, with no change to the program: the whole came out as 117 lines, and in them stood what no look of the day had shown - a run failing on main, there for ten minutes between two observings, and a change listed twice.

decision: The whole one looks through is the one the place one looks from says for itself - a lens of its own that places every lens - in the window, as text and as a page alike; where it says none, every lens in view as they come. It is read from that place's own lenses, not found among all in view.
rejected: Finding it among every lens in view by who keeps it (what was observed does not say who keeps a lens; the place itself does); a name for it in a place's mark (a lens that places every lens is already what a whole is).
why: The rule was first written as the whole a place in view says: an observatory that has another in view would then begin on the other's sheet - the first observatory on the author's. And only the window followed it; the whole as text and as a page still came as the program orders it.

decision: The window in the terminal opens on the whole a place in view says for itself - a lens of its own that places every lens, with what comes first - as the page does; where no place says one, on the flow of work, as before.
rejected: A lens named in the program as where one begins (what a place shows first is the place's to say, and it has said it); a new field for it (a lens that places every lens is a whole: that is already what it is).
why: Looked at on 2026-11-15 for the first time, through a recorded terminal replayed into the screen a person sees: the window opened on the lens of work, whose first screen was where a driver had stood, while the author's observatory says what it shows first - its sheet, then the perfect form - and its page honours that. Walking in the window, guarded by tests and never taken, was taken: right began it, down moved, Enter stood on a sign, the line of keys said what they now do, and the step was kept.

decision: Said with no command - nothing at all, or words that name none - ocoeco is the window, where there is no terminal to move in: one is shown where one stands, a mark before every line about a thing, and says a mark to stand on what it marks, a lens by its name to look through it from there, back, or up. What is shown is what lenses bring into focus - around the thing stood on, or what the place shows first - laid out by a surface a lens says, as-window: the lens looked through whole, what it places one step up. What was marked is kept beside the trail, and a plane gives each thing its mark. Standing on a thing, the lens of around also says which entries of the language can say something of it.
rejected: More flags, and what fits as one types (a line to be typed is still remembered from outside); a window made in the program for drivers without a terminal, as the terminal's is (what a window shows and offers is a lens of lenses, said in the language: any surface lays it out); a mark numbered by each surface for itself (the mark one says must name what was shown: the plane gives it, once).
why: The author, 2026-11-15: the interface is to be actually interactive - one stands in it and acts from it, it presents itself from itself, and one navigates from within, not by remembering where something is or which flag a command takes; not even what fits as one types; and it is all just another lens of lenses. A page, he said the same hour, is only one surface a lens of many lenses projects to. The agent had kept walking outside: looking through commands with flags held in its own context, reading the places' files and pages from its workspace, composing each act by hand. The fulldome in the terminal is a window for whoever has a terminal to move in, and it is made in the program, behind its brackets; a driver without a terminal had none.

decision: What a place has is kept by table and id, made once all its rows are read: whether a link holds is found, not looked for through every row of the table each time.
rejected: Keeping the graph from one look to the next (it was not the making that was slow, but one question asked the slow way); a program that stays running to hold it (the same).
why: A step of the walk had come to take a second and a half. The beam, timing what it gathers since 2026-11-15, said the graph took 571 ms of a one-second look; each thing it is made of, looked through as itself, took a few hundredths. Read: for each of some seven thousand links the program went through every row of the table pointed at - and each of 2,900 turns points at the one before it. Found by a look saying where its time goes, after two guesses about cost in these days had been off.

decision: A lens may read what was just given in the window - given: each field named, and its words - and what was marked in what was last shown - marked: each mark, and the thing it marks; and it may say who is looking: {who}, the driver. Going up is kept as a step - who left what, and when - so that where one stands is read off the steps: the thing of one's last step, unless it says one went up from it. Where a lens called entering is in view, an entry said in the window - by its name, or by its mark where it is marked - is said as that lens says it: with nothing given, the lens is looked through from the entry and shows what it asks; with what it asks given, the lens says the row it would keep - each field and value, and the place it is kept in - or what is lacking, and the program enters what the lens says. One does not stand on an entry: here stays where one stands. Where no such lens is in view the program says it itself, as before.
rejected: Where one stands handed to the lens by the program (it is in the steps, once going up is a step too: the lens reads it); an entry stood on like any other thing (here would then name the entry, where one came from would have to be guessed from the steps before it, and every record of work would say it was made standing on an entry); the lens built into the language before it has been tried (a lens that does not come into focus stops the check of every place); the program's own saying taken away at once (until the lens says all of it, the way in must not close).
why: The author, 2026-11-15: the program says the inside from outside only until the inside can say it itself - a hand that draws itself. What an entry asks, how the row it makes is named, which thing a word like here or a mark points at, and where the row is kept were all said in the program. A lens can say them once it is given what it lacks: the words just given, what was marked, and who is looking - where one stands is then read off the steps, which is why going up had to become a step: the trail said one still stood where one had left. The lens is made and tried as a place's own first, and built into the language once it says what the program said.

decision: In the lens of work, what is in progress and what was finished lately come first; where the work is happening - the things a driver stood on - comes after.
rejected: Leaving the order as the parts were written (it was the order they were made in, not an order chosen for a reader).
why: Looked at on 2026-11-15, in the window and as text: the lens of work opened with twenty lines of where a driver had stood, before what is in progress. From a place that says no whole of its own, that is the first screen a person meets. Where one stood is how what is in progress is read off - the ground under it, not the first thing to read.

decision: A lens may say what comes first: a part that places every lens places every other - not one a part before it has placed, and not a lens that looks from a thing, which from nowhere has only how to stand to say. A page is headed by what it is - the title its row gives it - and has a way back to the whole. And an entry may supply the moment, to the second, where a day is not enough.
rejected: An order of lenses fixed in the program (what an observatory shows first is the observatory's to say); holding the page equal to what was (it told that nothing had changed, not that it was good).
why: Looked at on 2026-11-15, as a browser draws it, for the first time since the page was said by a lens: the first thing on the author's published page was the lens of around telling a reader to type a command, then nine turns that said continue; his own sheet was near the bottom of 1,900 lines; every page was headed The fulldome and none led back. The page had been held equal, byte for byte, to what the program wrote - and that was a poor front page. The observatory's practice says to look after a change to how something looks; I had said I could not, with the tool for it on the lab.

decision: What the lens of language shows of the language is answered in the language. A line written twice is said once, as a named shape: how a pointing is said, in the lens of around. A table that leads to no surface is brought to one or let go: each time something was done by hand is brought into focus by the lens of results - what it took, the most first - and each such time repeats the work done by hand it is a time of.
rejected: Letting the table go (it is kept, and it is what the author means by handwork: what would be most worth making through the system itself); leaving the line twice (small - and the lens exists to show it).
why: Looked at on 2026-11-15, the lens that looks at lenses showed three things of the kind the author asks to be looked for: a name holding two kinds, a line written twice, a table nothing brought into focus. The table is the handwork itself, recorded by five places and seen by none - and what the engine's site shows as manual work worth a tool, which the fulldome lacked.

decision: Looking from a place at what was observed, the place one stands in is read as it stands and every other place as it was observed: the place, where it has a mark, is in view beside the folder of what was observed, and what that folder holds of the place's own lenses is passed over. Its lenses are then looked through as they are now - the same lens that names the whole - and a change to them is seen at once, not after the next observing.
rejected: Observing again before every look (minutes, and a trial before landing would have to be published to be seen); reading every place as held when one stands in an observatory (what was observed is the whole as one moment, and what the published pages are made of); passing over what was observed of every place held, rows as well as lenses (a row already is one row by two routes, the freshest, and a guard holds that).
why: On 2026-11-15 the whole was named from the place's own lens and brought into focus through the copy in what was observed: a lens just changed was looked through as it was.
