Twice that day it stood in the way - the first observatory's face, tried before it landed, had its rows copied by hand into what was observed; a check that the author's whole had its new name read the old one and stopped a job whose change was right. Both places held and observed already meet for rows, which are one row, the first or the freshest; for a lens, two of one name stopped the look.

decision: A change to the language is checked where it is read: the language's own place, checked with the places beside it, brings into focus every lens they keep, each over its own place, with the language as it is there. And a lens that looks from a kind of thing comes into focus, in any check, from the last thing of that kind its place keeps - so what it asks is asked with rows passing through.
rejected: Every place checked again after each change to the language (minutes, where the lenses that read the language are a few); a list of the lenses that read each shape, kept to know which to check (kept by hand, where bringing each into focus says it).
why: The shape of the signs nothing has come of was said anew from the window, and the landing was checked in the language's place, where only its own lenses come into focus. The conversation's lens of what followed asks of that shape, and failed in the engine when looked through from a turn; brought into focus from nowhere, nothing passes through it, and nothing would have failed.

decision: A driver's first step keeps the trail as a place of its own, and what is in view is read again after each thing a saying enters: so here and back name what was just made in that same saying, from a driver's first step on.
rejected: A trail kept as a place before anyone steps in it (a place with nothing in it, made on every machine that runs the program).
why: A trial driver with no steps yet said a sign and the connection leading from it at once: the connection's here named nothing, for the trail became a place only with that first step, after what was in view had been read.

decision: A part that places a lens may say the lens it is seen through - through: a lens that reads a plane. What the placed lens brings into focus is then given to that lens as its plane, and what it lays out - or leaves out - is what the part shows: a lens behind a lens, kept in the lens that places them. So a lens that differs from another is made by adding, never by changing: it places the other, adds parts of its own, and sees the other through a lens that leaves out what is not wanted. The part points at both - it places the one, and is seen through the other - so the arrangement is in the graph like everything else, and can be walked.
rejected: The filtering said in the placing part's own query (a part that places asks nothing; the lens behind is a lens, reused wherever it is wanted); the two written into one name, behind@placed (the name would point at no lens, and the graph would not show the second); only widened to leave lines out (only picks one heading of what is placed: leaving out is another lens's saying, not a flag on this one).
why: The author, 2026-11-16: if I want something different from a lens A, I add a lens B that includes A; to add, more lenses on its plane; to filter out something of what A projects, another lens behind it - all of it in B, reflected in the lens structure, nothing hidden. All of that held but the lens behind: a surface could be put behind a lens only at the moment of looking - as-window@lens - and no lens could keep it. Looking through a lens from a lens already worked, lens behind lens, to any depth; what lacked was a part's way of saying it.

decision: A lens that looks from a kind of thing comes into focus, in a check, from the few things of that kind that came last - by when each says it was - and not from the last alone: the last may have nothing passing through it yet. And where the language changes, each lens a place beside it keeps comes into focus with all of those places in view, as it is looked through where the whole is seen.
rejected: Every thing of the kind (hundreds of looks, where a few that came last carry what is asked now); the thing with the most behind it (asked of each lens in its own terms).
why: The check with the places beside the language's place brought the conversation's lens of what followed into focus from its last turn, over the conversation alone - and the shape that had stopped it passed: what followed a turn is done in other places, and no row went through it.

decision: A lens is of its place, as a thing is: two places may each keep a lens of one name. It is called from where one stands - the one kept there answers to the name alone, every other is called in full, place/name; where none is kept there, the name alone is no lens and the words say each in full. What a lens says of another by name means the one its own place keeps. In the graph a lens was always a thing of its place; only looking through it knew it by name alone.
rejected: Every lens always called in full (the language's own lenses and every lens that is one of its name would be said the long way for a meeting that is rare); the first place in view winning the name (whose lens a name means would turn on the order places are listed in); names kept one across the whole, with a prefix by habit (the habit is the sign).
why: Two places keeping a lens called site stopped every look that saw both, and neither saw why: the first observatory's lens of its pages had to be called commons-site because the author's observatory keeps one.

decision: In the graph, what a lens's rows name - the lens a part is of, the lens it places, the one it is seen through - means the lens of that name its own place keeps; else the one lens of that name in view. Where several places keep one and its own keeps none, the name alone is no one lens, and nothing is drawn.
rejected: A relation of the language declared for each field a lens's rows name (the rows of the language are drawn from the lenses as they are, built-in ones too: no place keeps them as a table, so no declared relation reaches them); a part linked to every lens of its lens's name (a part is of one lens).
why: The first observatory's part of its lens site was drawn as part of the author's lens called site: looking through a lens had become of its place, the graph still read a lens's name across the whole. Standing on the part, it pointed at the wrong lens - and, renamed by hand with its lens, it had seemed to be no thing one could stand on.

decision: A lens that looks from a thing may say the kinds of thing it looks from - looks_from: their tables. From a thing of another kind it is not asked: around such a thing it is not placed, and said by its name in the window it is looked through from nowhere, as it is where one stands on nothing. The lens of entering looks from an entry; what followed, from a turn.
rejected: Leaving each lens to bring nothing where it does not fit (it is asked every time, and the window cannot tell nothing to show from not from here); telling the kind from what a lens asks (a lens says what it is; it is not guessed).
why: Every lens that looks from a thing was brought around every thing, to say nothing: a third of a second in each look, for the lens of entering alone. And what followed, said while standing on anything but a turn, showed nothing - where from nowhere it shows what followed the latest thing the author said.

decision: A part of a lens is said to rest on a shape, or to ask of a table, where the name stands in its query as a word outside what is quoted. Within quotes a name is words the part says or compares with, not something it asks of.
rejected: Reading the query as the engine reads it, to learn what it asks of (the graph is drawn where no engine is, and a query that still holds here or today in braces is not yet one); a list of names never to be taken as shapes (it would be kept by hand, and wrong again with the next lens).
why: The link was read off the name wherever it stood as a word, so the part that names a row - which compares what was given with the word here - was drawn as resting on the shape here of another lens. A link the graph draws is followed: one that is not so leads astray, where one that is missing only fails to lead.

decision: A part of a lens goes by the name it was made with - one given to it, or, where none was, the place it was made at - wherever it comes to stand: its place among the others is not its name, as it was not for a part kept as a row. An entry may put a part where it is to stand (part: N); every part whose place then changes is written with the name it went by, and a part put among the others is given a name of its own, for a number names a place. And what is written above a part in its file is what the part says: read with it wherever the language is read, and written by its entry.
rejected: Naming every part anew, by its shape or its heading (what points at a part by its number would point nowhere, and a heading changes); keeping a part's old name beside a new one (one part known by two names at once); a key says written in a part (the files already say it above each part: it would be said two ways in one file); a part taken away (a part that landed is touched by the record of its landing, and what landed cannot be taken back - a sign of its own).
why: In a lens file a part was known by where it stands, so a part put before it would have taken its name, and whatever pointed at it - records of work, steps, connections - would have pointed at another. A part kept as a row already had its name and its place apart: still-showing/2 stands third. And the words above a part, where the files say what each part is for, were read by whoever opened the file, and by no lens, no entry and no window.

decision: A place that keeps no lenses yet is given its first by an entry as a file of its own, in lenses/ - where the lenses of a place are read - as a place that keeps lenses as files is given another.
rejected: The place given rows of lenses to keep in its mark first (a mark said for one lens, where a file is read as it is); the lens kept for it in another place (a place says what its own tables are).
why: The phone's docs keep their test runs, and no lens says what a test run is; the place keeps no lenses, so a lens entered for it from the window had nowhere to be written.

decision: A link may be said of what was: a record of work points at what it touched and where it was made, a step at what was stood on, each as it was when it was written. A thing taken back since is what the record said then: the link does not point nowhere, and it keeps nothing from being taken back. So a row that landed may be taken back where only what was said of the past points at it - and two things found to be of one nature can become one.
rejected: Records of work passed over by name when a row is taken back (a step, a record and whatever else says what was would each be named apart, where they are of one nature); a record rewritten to leave out what was taken back (a record is what was done: what it says is not changed after); a row taken back left behind as a mark that it was (what was taken back would pile up as marks).
why: Every row that landed was touched by the record of its own landing, and a row is taken back only where nothing points at it: nothing that landed could be taken back, and what was found to be of one nature with another stayed beside it. A record of work says what was then; it was read as if it said what is.

decision: A row entered without a name is named by its first words - and by the day before them, where the rows of its kind already kept are named so: read off what is in view, most of them. A table that asks the day of every name still says so itself.
rejected: The table of decisions asking the day of every name (asked of every place that keeps decisions, it would stop the ones that named some otherwise); the day before every name (a sign, a connection, an item are not named so); a list, in the lens, of the kinds named by the day (kept by hand, where what is kept already says it).
why: A decision entered without a name, in a trial, came out named by its first words alone, where every decision and every reflection in view is named by the day, and no sign, connection or item is: the lens looked only for a table that asks it, and none of the language does.

decision: The rows a record of work touched are those remembered since the last record that are there now - and a row of a lens the place keeps as a file is there as the file has it. So what an entry changed in the language is among what its record touched, like any row.
rejected: Reading them off where the record was made (that says where one stood - they were there only because the window steps onto what it makes); not asking whether a remembered row is there (a trial put back would then be said to have been touched).
why: Whether a remembered row is there was asked of the tables a place keeps, and a lens file is not one of them: the rows were remembered, and then let go. What followed a turn is read off what records touched, and the changes to the language - the ones made from within - were the ones missing from it.

decision: A saying in the window that comes to nothing leaves one standing on nothing, and says where one stood. Whatever is said next from where one stands - an act on it, an entry kept where it is held, a lens looking from it - finds nothing to act on and asks, instead of acting on a place one meant to leave. Where several entries are said at once and one is not entered, what came before it stays entered and one stands on nothing.
rejected: An act naming its object in the same saying (it makes one act safe and leaves every other act from where one stands - an entry kept where it is held - as it was, with a name to type for what one already stands on); a rule for whoever drives: read each answer before the next saying (a step to remember - the window would still keep a footing one meant to leave, for whoever forgets); staying where one stood when a saying fails (where one stands is then a place one meant to leave).
why: A part of a lens was named to be stood on and was not found; the act said next, called site/1, fell on the turn stood on before. Where one stands had stayed where the driver meant to leave: the act was right, the footing was not.

decision: A site is laid out once for each language it can be read in: in the one it is written in where it always was, in each other under a folder of its tag, the same paths within - by one asking, the program laying each out afresh. The languages are read off what is in view: each one a translation is in. Each page says its language, and offers the same page in every other by that language's own name - which a place says as a row (languages), like any word.
rejected: Every language under its own folder, the root only redirecting (every address there is would move; the language it is written in stays where it was); a list of languages kept in the program or said to the command (they are read off the translations there are); flags for languages (a flag is a country's); one program run switching languages as it goes (what was read in one would be kept for another).
why: Reading in another language was there, but a visitor could not reach it: the page said it was English whatever it was read in, and nothing led from a page to the same page in Russian.

decision: A star written by its shorter name is the place that goes by it, where one place in view does: a link written so is resolved like one written in full - it holds, or it points nowhere, and it ends at the thing itself. Only a link into a star that is not in view is not told.
rejected: Writing links in full from the window (the shorter name is what is shown, and what a person writes); saying such links hold without looking (a link is told by what is there); every link that is not told stopping a place (a place alone does not have the others in view: what it cannot tell is not wrong).
why: Everything pointed at through the window - by here, by a mark, by a name as it was shown - is written by the star's shorter name, and the graph looked the star up as written: nineteen such links were neither held nor broken. Their far ends did not see them - standing on a decision, the sign that points at it was not shown - and one written wrongly would have landed unseen, by the check and by the lens alike. It was seen when the program's rule for links and the lens's were put side by side: both read the same edges, and both passed over the same ones.

decision: A table may say how its rows are told in a few words, as it says which field dates them: tells - one of its fields, or several laid out as a line is ({lines} lines). A thing in view says itself by those words; where its table says nothing of it, by the words a list in the program finds.
rejected: More names added to the program's list (the program would go on saying, kind by kind, what each kind can say of itself); the first field of a row that has words in it (a row's first field is often its id, or where it is kept).
why: Things of thirteen kinds said nothing of themselves in a look - files, runs, work done by hand, the links of lenses kept as rows - for the few words of a thing were taken from a list of field names written in the program. Each kind knows which of its fields tells it, as it knows which dates it: read off a lens, some five hundred and seventy things stood with no words beside them.

decision: In the window a thing is stood on by its name, too: said as it was shown or as it is known - the place in full or by its star, its table, its id - one stands on it, as on what a mark marks; an entry named so is said. And the language is read again when an entry has been made in the window: what was just changed in a lens is shown as it now is, in the same look.
rejected: A word of its own before the name - on, at (the name is not the name of anything else: nothing has to say what it is); the language read anew at every look (it is the same until something is entered).
why: One stepped by marks only: a thing known by its name - a part of a lens, a decision of last week - was reached by walking to it from what happened to be shown, or not at all. And the first part of a lens changed from within was shown, right after, as it had been: the language was read once, as the program began.

decision: A thing takes another name in one act, said in the window: standing on it, called and the name. Every link to it goes with it - in its own place, and in every place in view, as each wrote it, by the place's id or its star alone - and a lens kept as rows takes its parts with it. If anything would then point nowhere, nothing is renamed. What the machine keeps of itself, its trail, goes with it too, and is not landed.
rejected: An entry's id given anew (an entry makes or changes a row found by its name: the name itself is what it is found by); a command beside move and take-back only (said from a terminal, where the window is where things are said); the old name kept beside the new one (two names for one thing, with nothing to say which is its own).
why: The first observatory's lens commons-site became site by rewriting its rows and its parts' rows by hand, in a job: a name is what others point at, and changing it alone leaves them pointing nowhere.

decision: A thing that is done is not held back: what holds things back holds only what is not yet done or dropped, whatever halts were drawn to it and whether or not any was said to be over. Saying a halt is over is for a halt lifted while the work it held is still ahead.
rejected: Saying each such halt over by a connection (handwork after every item done - forgotten, as this one was); a part showing the halts drawn to things done (it would show what nobody needs to act on).
why: That a halt is over was asked for in words, where the work already said it: the item was done, its halt stayed, and the sheet counted it among what the author's word would free. What can be read off the work is not asked of a hand.

decision: An entry is offered only a place that keeps its kind. Where the row would be kept is the place given; else, for an entry a place brings, that place; else the place of the thing stood on - if it keeps rows of that kind, or no place does yet. Which places keep a kind is read off what they hold. Where the place one stands in keeps none, the lens says which places do, and nothing is kept until one of them is said.
rejected: Reading a place's mark for the kinds it could keep (no lens reads a mark yet; what a place holds says nearly as much, and is already in view); keeping the row in the nearest place that keeps the kind without saying so (where a row is kept is the driver's to see before it is kept).
why: A connection, entered standing in ocoeco, was offered ocoeco - which keeps none - and the entry refused it only after everything had been given. This is the first lens of the language changed in its place: looked through at once, and landed with no program built.

decision: An entry writes where the row is kept. A lens a place keeps as a file is kept there - what it says of itself, and each of its parts, known by where it stands among them: a row of lenses or of lens_parts given for such a lens is written into its file, in place - what is written around it, and every comment, as it was - and what results must still be a lens, or nothing is written. A part is changed where it stands, or added after the last; a new lens is a new file, where the place keeps its lenses as files and keeps no rows of them. So a lens of the language is changed by the language's own entry - from within the window, landed like any row, and live where the language is read from its place. And what is given in the window keeps its lines: a line that names no field goes on with the field before, on a line of its own.
rejected: The language turned into rows, so that the entries that already write rows would do (a lens file says more than its rows - what is written above each part - and a query kept as one long line is read by no one); a second set of entries for files (what is entered is the same row: where it is kept is the place's affair, not the driver's); the whole file written anew from its rows (every comment would go); a part named by anything but where it stands (a lens file names no part).
why: The language was kept by its place, but changed only by changing its files from a job: said inside, changed from outside. Rows of a lens were already read from its file wherever the language is read; this is the same way, the other way round. A lens file stays what a lens is kept as there - read as it stands, with what each part is for written above it - and is no longer a second thing, edited by hand. And the list of the language's lenses, written once more in a guard, would have stopped the first lens added so: what the language keeps is the list.

decision: In a field that points at things, back names where one stood before - as the word does in the window - beside here and a mark. So in one saying that enters several things, here names what was just made and back what was made before it: a sign, what came of it and the connection between them are said at once, each pointed at and none named from memory. Where here or back names nothing, the lens says so and nothing is kept.
rejected: A table of what this saying made, given by the program, each thing named by its entry (one more thing for the program to give, where the steps already say it: what is made is stood on); a word for each thing made earlier - first, second (counting, where two words already known reach the three things one act mostly has).
why: The first act said at once - a decision and the two connections that lead to it - could point only at what was made last: a third thing had to be typed by its name. What one saying made was the one thing a saying could not point at.

decision: Entering is said by a lens. The lens of entering, built into the language, is looked through from an entry - by its name, or as the thing it is - and says what the entry asks and what it may also carry: which fields point at what, which values they allow, what the computer supplies; where the one looking stands and what was marked in what they were last shown - what here and a mark would name; where the row would be kept; and, given what it asks, the row it would keep - each field and its value, the name it goes by, the place it is kept in - or what is still lacking. The program reads the words given, looks through the lens, and has the entry write what the lens says: what it is to enter something is no longer said in the program. In the window an entry is said by its name or by its mark; with nothing given, the lens is what is shown.
rejected: The program's own saying kept as a second way in (two sayings of one thing drift apart; the lens is built in and always in view); the lens writing the row as well (a lens looks and says, it changes nothing - writing stays with the entry); every line that begins with a word and a colon taken for a field, the lens refusing the ones it does not know (a line of the words that happens to begin so would be taken for a field); the lens kept by one place only (what it is to enter something is the same everywhere: it belongs to the language).
why: The first piece of what the program said from outside, now said from inside: what an entry asks, how the row it makes is named, what here and a mark point at, and where the row is kept were some 170 lines of the program; they are now a lens of the language, read and changed like any other. It was tried first as a place's own lens beside the program's saying - as a language's own compiler is first run beside the one it will replace - and said what the program said, and more, since it reads the declarations themselves: what each field points at, which values it allows, what is supplied. What stays in the program is what touches a surface: reading the words given, and writing the row - which the entry does, guarding and supplying the same wherever a row is made.

decision: Every kind of row a lens file keeps is written into the file by its own entry: the tables a lens defines and their fields, its entries, its links and its ways in - as what it says of itself and its parts already were. A table, a field, an entry and a way in are known by their names; a link, like a part, by where it stands. And what is given in the window may be for more than one entry: after a line that says and, and the name of an entry, what follows is for that one. Each is kept in turn, and one stands on what was made last; all that one saying entered in a place lands as one. Where one of them is not entered, what came before it stays entered, and what was not is said.
rejected: A word for what was just made in the same saying - it (one stands on what was made: here already names it for what follows); all of it taken back where one is not entered (what was entered is sound by itself: it was guarded as it was written); a row of a field or a link named by a name of its own in the file (a lens file is read as it is written: a field by its name, a link by where it stands).
why: A lens file was half written by entries: a part could be changed from the window, the table it reads could not. And each thing entered was a landing of its own - minutes of checks for a few words - so that things belonging to one act, a sign and the connection that leads from it, landed as two.

decision: What repeats joins is one nature with many faces, and it comes to something as one: a sign has come to something when a connection leads from it, or from anything one with it in nature. So two things found to be one are said so by repeats, and the lenses read them as one - nothing of either is taken back.
rejected: Taking the one back and pointing what pointed at it at the other (what was said is consumed by the whole, not erased - and each face says the nature in its own words); a sign said again marked handled by hand (a state written, where it can be read off the act).
why: Merging two things of one nature was to be done by taking one back, once what pointed at it pointed at the other. But the language already says what two things of one nature are - repeats joins them as one nature with many faces - and the lens of signs did not read it: a sign said again stayed showing after the one it repeats had come to something.

decision: What is in view is read in another language where rows are read: each row says, in each field a translation of its own place gives, what the translation says, and everything else as it was written. A lens is rows, so its own words - what it says, a part's heading and line - are translated the same way, by the place that keeps the lens. The language is the reader's: said once in the window (in ru), it stays beside where one stands; or given by the surroundings (OCOECO_IN) where a site is laid out. Entering is done in the words given, beside rows as written.
rejected: A second set of lenses per language (every lens kept twice, drifting); message catalogs for a lens's words beside translations for data (two forms for one nature: a word of a lens is a field of a row); translating where a surface lays a line out (the graph, a thing's few words, a page's title would each need it again); each lens asking for translations in its query (a rule for every lens to remember).
why: The page the language lays out was to be offered in Russian, as the engine's is. The engine translated where it drew a page; in the language there is one place every lens, the graph and every surface read rows from - translated there, everything is, and no lens changes.

decision: The shapes a lens names are made ready each after those it asks of, wherever each stands in the lens; where none asks of another, in the order the lens gives them. So a shape added after the last may be asked of by a part that stands before it. Shapes that ask of each other in a ring are left as the lens gives them, and the engine says what it cannot make.
rejected: A part entered at a place of its own among the parts (a part is known by where it stands: what points at the ones after it would move); the same shape written out in each part that needs it (said twice, and kept twice).
why: A lens grows by entries, and an entry adds a part after the last. A shape had to be named before whatever asks of it, so a lens could not be given a shape that parts already there would ask of - and the first lens grown this way needed one.

decision: That every link within a star leads somewhere is what the lens of signs says must not land: its part of links pointing nowhere stops, and the check of a place carries it with the rest. The program's own telling of links stands in where there is no engine to ask, and tells of the links into the places beside this one when they are named - until the check looks through the lenses with those places beside it too.
rejected: Both kept on where there is an engine (the same link would be said twice, and the two would drift); the program's taken away everywhere (where there is no engine to ask, nothing would tell of links at all).
why: Put side by side, the program's rule and the lens's read the same edges of the same graph, and said the same of a link that leads nowhere: two sayings of one thing, one of them compiled into the program. The lens's is the one that is also shown as a sign.

decision: The check of a place is what its lenses say must not land. A part of a lens may say it stops - stops: what it shows does not hold, and a place that shows any of it does not pass its check. The check looks through every lens over the place, as it already did to see that each comes into focus, and carries each line of a part that stops, deciding nothing itself. The first such part is of the lens of signs: an id two rows go by - kept twice. What the program still holds itself - that the mark parses, that every link leads somewhere, that nothing kept out is kept, that every lens comes into focus - is moved the same way, a rule at a time, each said by a lens beside the program until both say the same.
rejected: The rule written into the program's check (one more thing said from outside, and seen by no lens); a lens of its own for the check (what does not fit is the lens of signs' to say - it already said a link pointing nowhere; the check is that lens, where it stops); every sign stopping a landing (a sign said by someone, or a run that fails, is shown, not a wall); moving the links at the same time (their holding has three sayings - holds, does not, not told - and the program's rule and the lens's are to be seen side by side first).
why: A table is keyed by its id, and nothing held it: sixteen rows once went by three names, and the check said all was well. The rule could have been one more thing the program knows. Said by a lens it is also a sign - shown on the sheet and said aloud while it is true; it is read and changed where the language is kept; and a place can say what must not land of its own. The lens says what does not hold; the check is only where that stops a landing - as the voice is only where urgent is carried.

decision: The check of the language, over every place beside, looks through each lens by the name it is called from there: in full, where several places keep a lens of its name.
rejected: Leaving the check to look by the name a lens is kept under (it would stop every landing of the language for as long as two places keep one name, which is now allowed).
why: Once the first observatory took back the name site, the check of every lens over every place asked for site from a place that keeps neither, and was told several lenses are called so: the trial of a lens of its place had run before the two names met.

decision: With the places beside it named, the check of a place looks through what lenses say must not land over all of them, and carries what is about this place: a link into another of them that leads nowhere is seen only so. And that nothing a place keeps holds what is kept out is said by the lens of what is kept out: its part of what is showing stops. The program's own telling stands in where there is no engine to ask - and where there is, says only what no lens says yet: a link into a star that is not among the places in view. What the check still says itself is reading: that a place has a mark, that its tables are there and are rows - and that each lens comes into focus.
rejected: Every line shown with the places beside it carried (a place would be stopped by its neighbour's sign); a link into a star that is not in view stopping by a lens (from a place alone every link into another star is so: not told is not wrong - the program says it only where the places are beside it); what is kept out left to the program because it guards secrets (the lens already said it, urgently, wherever it showed: the check only carries it).
why: The third and fourth rule moved as the first two did: each time the program's telling and a lens's part read the same rows. A part that stops says the thing each of its lines is about, so that with other places in view the check carries only what is this place's - one place's sign does not stop another.

decision: The language is kept by its place. Where the place that keeps the language - in a folder called language, holding the lens called language - is in view from where one looks, and is not behind the program, its lenses are the language: each as it is kept there, as it is now. A lens changed there is changed - looked through at once, with no program built anew; a lens no longer kept there is gone. The program carries a copy, as it was when it was built, and looks through that everywhere else: where the place is not in view, where the program that place builds is older than this one, and - all of it - where what the place keeps is not sound as a whole. A lens kept there whose text is no lens yet stands as the program carries it.
rejected: The place's copy always winning (a clone left behind would put an older language over a newer program: the program the place builds says which is older, and nothing has to be stated by hand); a version written into each lens (a thing to remember at every change); the language read as it last landed rather than as it is now (what a place keeps is in view as it is now, like its rows and its own lenses - and trying a change before it lands is the point); half of each where what is kept is unsound (a language is one whole).
why: Moving entering inside took four releases of the program, each to change what one lens says: the language was said inside, but could only be changed from outside. The program already treats the words of the language so - it carries them as they were when it was built, and over them the words of the places in view. Read from its place, a lens of the language is changed like any other thing a place keeps, and the program becomes what answers, reads and writes - with a copy of the language for where its place is not. It is the step after the first translator: the language's own saying is no longer inside the thing that runs it.

decision: The language is read as its place keeps it wherever that place is held on the machine one looks from: among the places in view, and else where the machine says it is held (OCOECO_LANGUAGE). So a place's own check, made where it is held, reads the language as it is kept - with what was changed from the window - and not only as the program carries it.
rejected: Each change made from the window released at once (minutes of building for a few words - and the lab would still look through the program it has); a place's check made from the observatory (a place is checked by itself, where it is held); the language's place looked for among the folders around (where it is held is the machine's to say, not to be guessed).
why: A part was taken back where only records pointed at it: from the observatory nothing pointed nowhere, and from the place's own folder two links did - there the language was the one the program carries, older than what had been changed from the window. A place is checked where it is held, so what it was checked with hung on where one stood.

decision: The language being read is a given of every look, as today is ({in}), and the languages there are, are what a lens says (reading): any lens may ask of it, and each surface - a page, the window - says its own offer of them under its own constraints. The program writes no page's words: laying a site out, it hands a page only what a page alone cannot know - where it is written, and the way up to where the site in every language rests - and asks the lens which languages to lay it out in.
rejected: The offer written by the program for the page (one surface served, by words outside the language - landed an hour before, and taken back here); a list of languages the program reads off by itself (a second saying beside the lens's); the language written in named in the program (it is a fact of the whole: a row says it).
why: The author, the same hour: a page is one surface a lens of lenses can project onto; the ecosystem is the main vector. The program had just been made to write a page's offer of languages itself, and to keep its own list of them - the page first, the whole after.

decision: How the latest run of each workflow of a place ended is kept once: as runs, observed of every place by the observatory. The gatherer no longer writes it into each place as ci, the folder it writes is what it gathered that time, and the engine's page reads the runs.
rejected: Declaring ci beside runs (the overlap made official); runs gathered by each place in place of observed (once a day, where the sheet and the voice ask every quarter of an hour).
why: It was kept two ways - ci, gathered by each place's own gatherer once a day, and runs, observed of every place every quarter of an hour: one nature in two tables, of which only runs was declared by a lens and read by the lenses, the sheet and the voice. The engine's page alone read ci.

decision: The one language is seen through a lens of its own (one-language): each form a word names, and how each overlay words it - English one overlay among the others; how much of the language each overlay words; where an overlay words several forms alike, the forms meeting in one word; where an overlay has no word for a form, a gap; and the forms no overlay has a word for at all. It is made of rows that were already there - the words, their wordings in overlays, the overlays - and changes nothing in the program.
rejected: Making English a second table beside the forms first (a move of every word for a frame not yet seen through a lens: the lens first, then what it shows the rows want); one lens per overlay (an overlay is a face of one language, not a language of its own); counting a form unworded only where every overlay lacks it (a gap is of an overlay, and a form no overlay words is its own deeper gap - both are shown).
why: The author, 2026-11-16: there is only one language, and English is an overlay in it; ocoeco, a language intelligent about itself, would show where overlays overlap and where no overlay has a name. The language already kept forms and their wordings - only no lens looked at them as one.

decision: In the window, what a lens places is laid out one step up - its name, what it says of itself, its headings - and one says its name to look through it. But a lens that only places one lens has nothing else to show, and what it places may have no name of its own to be looked through by - a lens seen through the lens behind it: there the window lays out the lines too. And a link pointing nowhere is a line about the row it is written in: it is marked, and one stands on that row to set it right.
rejected: Every placed lens laid out in full (the front would be the whole page at every step up: the window is for moving, and a step shows where one is); a name given to every lens seen through another (the arrangement is the lens that places them - that is its name).
why: What waits on the author - the sheet, seen through the lens behind it - showed in the window as a heading with a count, and no way to the six lines it counted: the first lens made by adding was the one lens the window could not show. Changed in the language's own place, and looked through at once.

decision: What entries add to a lens file is written as the language's files are: each new table, part, link, entry and way in apart from what is before it by an empty line, and what a table says of itself before its fields.
rejected: The file laid out anew after each entry (what is written around a row, comments among it, would be lost); leaving the spacing to whoever opens the file (a file made from the window is read in the window and by hand alike).
why: The first lens of the language made wholly from the window, gathered, came out with no empty line between its tables and a table's words after its fields: it said the same as a lens written by hand, and read closer.

decision: Where an entry is shown, of what was marked in what was last shown only what fits is offered: each thing with the fields of the entry that can point at a thing of its kind - and the thing one stands on says which fields here fits. An entry none of whose fields point at things is offered nothing. And a thing is given one mark, by whichever of its names a line says it.
rejected: All that was marked listed for every entry (most of it fits nothing, and what fits is lost among it); the fitting worked out in the program (it is in the declarations: the lens reads them); a mark for each name of a thing (two marks for one thing say there are two).
why: Shown through the lens, the entry of a source listed twenty-three marked things, none of which it could point at; and a research showed one thing under two marks - by its whole name and by its shorter one. Offering is choosing in place of typing only where what is offered can be chosen. Which fields point at what is declared, so the lens reads it: nothing of it is worked out in the program.

decision: What the gatherer writes of each place is declared by a lens of the language, gathered: its activity day by day and its releases - what a row of each is, how it is told, and when it was. So what is gathered says itself in a look, like anything a place keeps.
rejected: The latest runs declared beside them (they are of one nature with what the observatory observes as runs - a sign of its own); what the gatherer writes left undeclared, as rows the program makes (what a place keeps is said by a lens, whoever writes it).
why: The gatherer writes activity, releases and the latest runs into every place, and no lens declared them: what was gathered said nothing of itself in a look, and nothing said what its rows are.

decision: What the gatherer writes, and where - its two tables, the folder and the branch - is said once, in the program where it writes them; every mark keeps those tables without naming them, a mark that names one elsewhere keeps it where it says, and a place the gatherer does not gather simply has none of them to read. Where only a checkout of a place is in view, its call to the gatherer says it is gathered. The gatherer's workflow no longer takes another folder or branch: no caller gave one, and none would be read.
rejected: A line in each mark saying it is gathered (one fact still said in every place); the lens of what is gathered saying where its tables are kept (the writer says where it writes - a lens saying it too would be a second saying, free to drift); the caller's file read wherever a mark is read (what the gatherer wrote is the act itself: where none was written there is nothing to read).
why: Nineteen marks named the same two tables by the same paths: one fact said nineteen times, so the gatherer writing one table less took nineteen landings. And two places that call the gatherer named nothing of it: what was gathered of them was never read.

decision: A mark may say holds = [places]: the places whose records it keeps in its own tables. When it is gathered, a row whose project names one of them stays theirs; every other row is the place's own, as before.
rejected: Tagging every row with the project of the place it was read from even when the row names another (the face would show every moved record as docs'); keeping any row's own project whatever it names (a place could speak for places that never gave it their records); re-attributing rows in the engine instead of the harvest (one nature - which place a row is of - would be decided in two places).
why: The author decided on 2026-11-17 that linux-phone-oco keeps one database for the whole project (linux-phone-oco/docs, through tad), with a project column: the records of lab-tools, surya-lab, device-template and sxmo-deviceprofiles move there. Each record must still show as of its place on the face, as it did when each kept its own tables. Nothing changes for a mark that does not say holds.

decision: Six meanings, six signs: works, partly, broken or missing, not yet started, not known yet, not applicable. Planned work that has not started is shown calm and grey - never with the red of broken things.
rejected: Reusing the red sign for open backlog items.
why: Red on every planned item painted a project at the idea stage as a failure; like unknown, not yet is not a verdict.

decision: Words are laid out by the browser, never placed inside a drawing: SVG holds shapes only (and fixed-length marks the engine itself makes); every title and label is ordinary text in a cell of its own, shown whole, wrapping inside its cell; a row of cells scrolls sideways rather than squeezing.
rejected: Cutting titles at a fixed length; shrinking the font to fit; adjusting this one path by hand.
why: The path's milestone names were SVG text, which cannot wrap and knows nothing of its neighbours: they ran into each other, and cutting them at a fixed length only hid it until a longer title, a narrower screen or another language.

decision: The page shows how each place's latest runs ended from the runs the observatory observes of every place, no longer from what each place gathered of itself as ci.
why: How the latest runs ended was kept two ways, and is kept once now: as runs, observed every quarter of an hour; ci is no longer gathered.

decision: A site drawn from one family's data alone is that family's face: its name at the top of every page, leading to its own front, and the site's root leading there - read off the data (one grand project in view), with no option to set.
rejected: A flag naming the front (a state to keep true by hand); a copy of the engine's pages in the family's repository (two renderers of one thing).
why: The author asked for linux-phone's own pages, drawn in its own CI from its own data (2026-11-17); the engine already draws the family's views, and only the frame said whose the site was.

decision: Every project tells four things about itself, in its own data: its idea (why it exists, written by the project for anyone, as an ordered piece of writing), its path, its workings (how each step is delivered and proven, by which tools, and why we care), and its work. A lens gathers and shows these and writes none of them. The observatory is one more project that tells the same four.
rejected: How we work as one roof - a separate working set beside the projects (decided earlier the same day); the idea as terse cards written about a project.
why: From the author: how we work must not float beside the projects like a random toolbox - it belongs to each project, tied to its goals; and the idea must tell a commoner what this is, in the project's own voice. Shared tools are projects that others' workings name.

decision: The site is a designed static website from tad data - minimal, elegant, no JavaScript - not a tad text page.
rejected: Rendering tad's own pages for the observatory.
why: It is the observatory's visit card.

decision: Discovery is hexagonal; on GitHub the mark is the oco-project topic plus a kind topic, confirmed by oco.toml.
rejected: Code search for oco.toml (slow, rate-limited) as the primary way.
why: Topics are what GitHub's search indexes best: one query finds every marked repository.

decision: The observatory's engine (mark, discovery, harvest, site) is its own repository, in Rust; tad is to be rewritten in Rust with its formats unchanged.
rejected: Extending the Python tad renderer.
why: Sturdier machinery, compiled checks, one toolchain across the commons' tools.

decision: Essence is its own project - the method - beside ocoeco (the language it is written in) and ocoeco-engine (the eye that draws it). It must describe itself with nothing but itself, and be usable: a short guide with a test for each answer, and a measure of how completely any project tells its essence.
rejected: Essence as only a section of ocoeco's specification and a page of the engine; Essence as an essay with no check.
why: Proposed by the author: it gives why and how about how to do why and how. Weighed against the risk of one more box: the method is knowledge neither the format nor the renderer holds, and it is more general than software.

decision: Everything thought, decided and planned is written into the tad structure - concepts, decisions, backlog, session log, milestones - in the project it belongs to.
rejected: Prose documents alone; plans kept in conversation or memory.
why: Nothing may depend on anyone remembering.

decision: How we work is gathered under one roof, the creation-guidelines organization: the canon, the playbook, lab-agent (renamed lab-agent-oco), land and shot (moved from a personal repository), and the practices (moved from the observatory's own design data). Every practice names the tool or check that carries it; the share of practices so carried is its 'how close are we'. It is shown as a curated lens - think, do, tools - replacing the hard-coded page, and lab-agent-oco guide prints the whole working set. SUPERSEDED the same day by "a project, whole": how a project works belongs to each project, not to a roof beside them.
rejected: Leaving practices in the observatory's design data; a page of principles with no tools behind them; a new organization (the roof already exists).
why: Asked for by the author: a working and usable solution set, part of the grand picture, not a manifest. Two practices were broken on the day they were written, both resting on memory alone.

decision: The face uses Project Fluent message catalogs for its interface; projects keep data translations in a standard translations table (with by: human or machine), falling back to the source language; the site is rendered once per language under /<language>/ with identical paths, the root redirecting old addresses; the switcher is a thin line at the header's end naming each language in itself (English · Русский).
rejected: Plain string tables (wrong plurals); translated columns inside source tables; translating rendered HTML afterwards (fragile, no grammar); flags or bare codes in the switcher; switching by script or by the browser's language (no JavaScript, and a reader's choice should be theirs).
why: Fluent gets each language's grammar right (Russian has three plural forms); separate translation rows keep data made by work untouched; prefixes keep paths identical and old links alive.

decision: Grand views become lenses: repositories of their own that declare a family and its views as data; the observatory discovers and renders them all with one engine, curates some into its navigation and lists the rest as discovered. Our views become curated lenses built like any other; linux-phone-oco/docs keeps producing research data and the Linux Phones lens moves to its own repository in its family's organization.
rejected: Views hard-coded in the engine (a bottleneck and a gatekeeper); our views on a privileged path; a free-form template language for views (the vocabulary grows from real needs instead).
why: An observatory of a commons cannot be the only one allowed to look: views as data make the engine a general renderer, open to anyone's family of projects, with no privileged path.

decision: The observatory is a meta structure, tied to no project; its tabs are itself and the grand projects, each with its own views.
rejected: One flat set of tabs for everything.
why: A devices tab made the whole look device-centred; devices are one part of one grand project.

decision: The ecosystem of gathering, chaining and propagation is called ocoeco (observation commons observatory ecosystem).
rejected: Leaving it unnamed; the dashed form oco-eco.
why: It has become an information ecosystem, and deserves a name.

decision: New projects and organizations of the ecosystem may carry -oco in their names - a telling touch, not a requirement. Nothing existing is renamed: belonging is declared by the mark and shown by the topic.
rejected: -oco added to every existing organization, repository, tool and command.
why: Agreed with the author after weighing it: a name that says where a thing belongs helps a person; but identity by name is the mistake Rhizome names, and renaming has real costs.

decision: ocoeco becomes its own repository and the working system from now on: the principle, the formats (tad is the format it speaks), gatherers, chaining, and the mark, discovery and harvest moved in from the observatory's engine, which keeps the face. tad-engine stays as it is, frozen, its formats unchanged.
rejected: Renaming tad-engine in place (its history and users are a different thing); keeping the machinery inside the observatory's engine.
why: The ecosystem's machinery belongs together and apart from the face; tad's name lives on as the format, keeping every existing file valid.

decision: The working practices are tad data in the observatory, and every agent reads them live through lab-agent guide.
rejected: Practices kept only in one agent's memory or in prose files that drift.
why: An improvement made once reaches every agent; no agent depends on its own memory to work well.

decision: Table columns are ranked best first from the data; unknown is shown as unknown and never counted as failure.
rejected: Hand-ordered columns; one 'how close' percentage that counted unknown as zero.
why: The order corrects itself as support grows; a gap in knowledge is not a verdict.

decision: tad is not a template but a rhizoid module (a rhizcut) supplied in every repository, with standard gatherers (CI jobs and hooks reading real files, tests, releases); tad has its own path, shown among the other projects rather than as a top tab.
rejected: tad as a template or a subtree copy; tad as a top tab.
why: Templates and copied subtrees drift and cannot send fixes back; tad is central but smaller than a grand aim like Linux Phones.

decision: Projects are shown against three horizons - working, perfection, ongoing perfection - on the readiness ladder, with milestones whose criteria are measured data.
rejected: A single progress bar; milestones ticked by hand.
why: Overall progress alone loses the reader; three honest horizons show where a project really stands.

decision: Hand-work is recorded on the way every change already goes: land asks for --hand ACTION or --no-hand, and a failure to record stops the landing.
rejected: A reminder nobody must answer; recording after the fact.
why: A ledger is only worth reading if it is never silently skipped; land is the one path every change takes.

decision: The harvest rebases its data onto whatever landed while it worked, and retries the push up to five times.
rejected: Pushing once and failing; force-pushing (would drop what landed); holding landings while a harvest runs.
why: Since land starts harvests, a change landing during a harvest's three minutes rejected its push (2026-11-11 14:45); the harvest writes only its own data/ files, so a rebase cannot collide with what lands.

decision: The lab machine holds an idle inhibitor while the agent serves jobs; it is updated through its package repository regularly.
rejected: Blocking sleep altogether - its owner may still put it to sleep on purpose.
why: It suspended on idle at 03:09 and the agent stayed stuck after waking until a reboot; and it stayed on lab-agent 0.1.39 for days because its package list was never refreshed.

decision: Everything breathes through ocoeco - its language, gatherers and checks - and the observatory stays a mirror: projects produce their data, the observatory reads it, and no project needs the observatory to work.
rejected: Projects depending on the observatory's site or harvest to function.
why: The author's direction that the whole lives through OCO, weighed against the risk of the mirror becoming a control centre and a single point of failure.

decision: No new Python, even for one-off glue: shell orchestrates, Rust carries the logic (rust-script for single files), repeated work becomes a Rust tool; tad stays as it is until ocoeco replaces it.
rejected: Python for throwaway glue; rewriting tad now.
why: Asked by the author: Python's ecosystem is fragile - versions, imports, strings. Measured on the lab machine: a rust-script one-off compiles once in seconds and then runs at once. The deeper cause of failed runs was text patching, answered by structured tools such as ocoeco note.

decision: land starts the observatory's harvest after merging a marked project; the harvest coalesces bursts - one run in progress, at most one waiting.
rejected: Each project's CI dispatching the harvest (a token with rights on the observatory in every project); harvesting every few minutes on a timer (wasteful when nothing changed).
why: Triggering the harvest and waiting for it was manual work done 19 times.

decision: Mechanical rules are enforced by the tools every change passes through, not kept as practices: land moves tags only onto what merged, checks changed workflows with actionlint and commit titles against the conventional form before pushing.
rejected: More practices; more care.
why: The author asked whether such things should be guarded by a tool rather than a mental note; twice in a day a practice did not hold.

decision: Whatever ships or is called by others is Rust; whatever repeats becomes a Rust tool; one-off glue in a job may stay small.
rejected: Python in shipped or shared code; rewriting every one-off line of glue.
why: Python let bugs reach runtime that a compiled language rules out; the record scripts that repeated became ocoeco note.

decision: tad stays the general substrate - a transparent database of text files in git - and is rewritten in Rust; ocoeco is one specific use built on it, and others (Truelink) will be. The wrap-up pass comes first; then tad in Rust is the focus.
rejected: Moving tad's duties into ocoeco and retiring tad (2026-11-11-wrap-up-then-tad, superseded: it would make a general tool specific); hardening tad's Python.
why: The author: tad is simple and general, and proved that a text/file database in git can be accessible, transparent and intelligible; ocoeco is a narrower use of it, and a coming idea (Truelink: facts, their sources and what is drawn from them, so fact-checking can be automated) needs tad too. Python leaves; tad does not.

decision: First a wrap-up pass settling every in-progress item; then the focus is moving tad's duties into ocoeco (declared table shapes, canonical form, documents rendered from data) and retiring tad's Python; phone work continues where it is not blocked.
rejected: Hardening tad in Python; dropping current work mid-way; switching before the board is honest. Superseded the same day by 2026-11-11-tad-in-rust: tad stays general, in Rust.
why: The author: big ideas wait on a backbone that is not Python, and loose ends make the whole hard to read. Making tad's Python pristine would polish what is being retired.

decision: Everything in progress is parked, each item with its resume point, and lab-agent is redesigned first. Resume order afterwards: 1 the glimpse picker (ocoeco ocoeco-commit), 2 the CI check for glimpses (ocoeco land-needs-a-record), 3 ocoeco release (ocoeco ocoeco-release), 4 argenv for every tool (ocoeco and tad argenv-surface), 5 lab-agent through ocoeco (lab-agent milestone through-ocoeco), 6 ocoeco check over every shared table (ocoeco check-every-shared-table), 7 the modem and telephony checks (surya-lab), 8 the microphone (docs, surya-lab), 9 the remaining parked items in each project.
rejected: Patching lab-agent and carrying on; carrying on and investigating later.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: the 2026-11-11 incident (a stall, then 102 finished jobs replayed, fifty at a time) blocks everything - the lab is how all work is done. Its cause is a foundation laid as a one-off prototype; it needs rethinking against what the world has learned, not patching. No harm was found: four replayed pull requests, all the legitimate tad 0.4.0 pin bump; no direct pushes, tags, releases or phone actions.

decision: The face asks, for each star, why it exists and how far it has come: one part, laid out once for each star - its leading idea, then each milestone that rests on items of work, in the order of its rungs, with how much of what it rests on is done. The lens of purpose is no longer placed first; it follows with every other lens, folded.
rejected: Changing the lens of purpose itself (it is every place's lens, and in a terminal fifteen stars of ten lines each would bury its figures); placing purpose as well as asking (the same said twice on one page); taking the part back and entering another (records of work point at it: it was changed where it stands, saying that it places nothing now).
why: The face says it shows first why each star exists and how far it has come, and placed the lens of purpose for that: fifteen ideas in one list and, far below in another, the milestones of all the stars mixed. What belongs to one star stood in two places. Laid out once for each star, a surface can stand the stars side by side - the page does, as small cards with rings - which is what the engine's front page draws by its own knowledge of stars. Tried on the lab in a working tree that was thrown away, and looked at, before it was entered here.

decision: The harvest observes by holding: each place found is brought to hand, as it is on GitHub now, and read as any place held is read - its tables, those it keeps on another branch, and what the routes read. What this observatory observed then holds what the author's does: a link to a document, a commit, a guard or a file of source points at something here too.
rejected: Leaving the five showing (they say something untrue of the stars: the links hold, this observatory did not look); passing over links to what a route reads wherever what was observed lacks it (a link nobody checks is how one comes to point nowhere).
why: Looked at on its published page on 2026-11-15, once the page was drawn anew: the lens of signs said seven links point nowhere, where the author's observatory, over the same places, says two. Five were links to what a route reads - a document, a file of source - which a harvest that only asks GitHub for each place's tables does not bring. Looked at before changing: this way of observing dates from 2026-11-12, before routes were said; the author's observatory has observed by holding since then, and this workflow was not brought along.

decision: Which pages this observatory publishes in the language is said by a lens of its own, commons-site: the whole, laid out through the face, and a page for each place in view, laid out through what is around it. The harvest lays them out with ocoeco site, beside the engine's views; a star's card on the whole leads to the star's page.
rejected: A page for each sign and each decision, as the author's observatory has (a visitor here meets the stars first; what is around a star leads on to its signs); the whole at index.html (the engine's front page stays the first a visitor meets until the language says a second language); the name site (a lens is named once in the whole: the author's observatory keeps a lens called site, and two lenses of one name stop every look that sees both).
why: The author's observatory has said its pages by a lens since 2026-11-15; this one wrote one page by hand in its workflow, the whole, and its stars' cards led nowhere. A lens of pages is what the language already has for it, and a place says its own.

decision: The lens that says which pages this observatory publishes is called site - the name it was first meant to have - as the author's observatory calls its own: a lens is of its place, and each is site where one stands.
rejected: Keeping commons-site (a name made to step around what no longer stands in the way says so for ever).
why: It was called commons-site only because a lens's name had to be one across every place in view, and the author's observatory keeps a lens called site.

decision: The practices leave the observatory's design data for grenudi/ideal-agent, where they are a table of its tad database; the observatory gathers them from there (the author's observatory and the ecosystem constellation gather grenudi/ideal-agent) and shows them as ideal-agent's rows. design/data/practices.json is removed and its export with it; the links that touched a practice here point to ideal-agent's rows of the same ids (ocoeco #456, ecosystem #160).
rejected: Keeping both copies (two lists drift); keeping the practices here and pointing ideal-agent to them (the one home would not hold what every session reads first).
why: The author, 2026-11-17: one home for general agent know-how, grenudi/ideal-agent (its decision 2026-11-17-one-home-for-agent-know-how). Before removing, both copies were harvested side by side and compared: all 43 practices the same in id, text and reason.

decision: Ingest talks to a small persistent daemon that keeps the analysis warm; reads against the store are a stateless command.
rejected: A fresh process for every call.
why: Loading and resolving a workspace is expensive and worth keeping warm; the daemon is the first instance of the later genome process.

decision: Structure is extracted with rust-analyzer's own semantic layer (ra_ap_hir), pinned, behind a stable SymbolGraph boundary; everything downstream speaks language-agnostic graph types.
rejected: The compiler's internals, MIR or a nightly-only interface; writing a parser or resolver.
why: Real name resolution as a library on stable Rust; the boundary insulates from its 0.0.x instability and is where another language's extractor plugs in.

decision: Graft - a closure turned back into compilable, running code - is in the first milestone.
rejected: Ending the first milestone at ingest, hash, store, sync.
why: If the structure cannot go back into something executable there is no point in it; proving the round trip first tests the representation before anything is built on it.

decision: The graph is the source of truth, without qualification; text is read once on the way in and emitted once on the way out.
rejected: Text as the content with structure as its index.
why: Describing it as 'a store of source text indexed by structure' quietly re-centres files - the old world with a hash bolted on.

decision: H(node) = blake3(postcard(hash form) ++ sorted references); local names replaced by positions; cycles condensed and hashed as one unit.
rejected: Hashing text; adding alpha-equivalence later.
why: Deterministic, structural, fast; alpha-equivalence built in from the start because it changes what the hash is.

decision: The kernel is not in the prototype; its only near-term role is the filesystem view, stages later.
rejected: Starting at the kernel.
why: 'Rust in the kernel' is an argument about timing, not a build target; kernel work is the slowest feedback there is.

decision: Sync is proven between two local stores before any network transport.
rejected: Starting with the network.
why: Deciding what to transfer is the part worth testing; the transport is mechanical after.

decision: Macros are expanded on the way in and not preserved as such.
rejected: Treating macros as something the graph must round-trip.
why: They are a convenience of text-based development; once the structure itself is edited they have no job.

decision: The project is Rhizome - a root system with no root, any point connecting to any point; its foundational engine is Hypha, the single filament; the tools are rz and hy. The substrate is the rhizome, definitions are nodes, a conjured shape is a shoot.
rejected: Alkahest; Aleph (taken); Mycorrhiza (the most exact, the hardest to spell).
why: Biology is load-bearing in the model, so the vocabulary comes from the same well.

decision: No new language: the host language's type system expresses boundaries and transformations.
rejected: A DSL.
why: Inventing a language to avoid using one was Nix's mistake.

decision: One shared store per machine (~/.local/share/hypha/store); a project holds only a hypha.lock - a small pointer file of closure roots.
rejected: A hidden .hypha per project, like .git.
why: A store per project would be isolated and non-deduplicating: the very thing the manifesto opens by attacking.

decision: The compiler is a black-box oracle at the single text boundary - today the only socket it has; Cranelift is the named long-term destination for code generation.
rejected: Treating the round trip through text as the destination.
why: It keeps the first milestone free of compiler engineering while naming where the text boundary finally disappears.

decision: Hypha is to be developed from its own graph, proven by a fixpoint: built from the graph, it ingests and re-emits itself to the identical hash. Files and git demote to a projection.
rejected: Keeping its own source in files for ever.
why: The field's answer to the trust hazard of self-hosting systems, and the hardest stress test for free.

decision: Each node keeps its verbatim source span beside its hash form; graft emits the original bytes, never a reconstruction.
rejected: Regenerating text from stripped structure.
why: Nothing is inferred on the way out; the structural hash is identity, the text a rendering of it.
